name: RunWay token lets anyone burn inflated sell volume from its pair
summary: RunWayERC20 (BYC) adds the full amount of every fee-taking transfer into its USDT pair to lpBurnFrequency, even when the tokens are immediately swapped back out. Its public autoBurnLiquidity() then moves lpBurnFrequency tokens from the pair to 0xdead and calls sync(). In the transaction right after the owner's launch(), the attacker bought 698,539 BYC with flash-loaned USDT, sent them back to the pair and recovered them with a second swap, then called autoBurnLiquidity(). That left the pair's BYC reserve near zero, and one sale drained its 119,950.5 USDT.

name: Moonwell cbETH OEV feed denomination mismatch
summary: Moonwell's ChainlinkOracle treats every configured feed as USD-denominated. MIP-X43 mapped cbETH to a CBETH/ETH wrapper returning the ~1.12 exchange ratio, so cbETH was priced at about $1.12 instead of ~$2,200. Liquidators seized cbETH-backed accounts that had been healthy for negligible repayments, and borrowers drained cbETH against dust collateral.

name: Kinto K token unprotected initializer takeover
summary: The K proxy was deployed with its implementation active but initialize() still callable by anyone. Two seconds later an attacker initialized it, took the admin roles and slipped in a clandestine implementation; months later that retained authority wrote unbacked K balances that were sold into K pools and posted as collateral to borrow USDC.

name: MainchainGatewayV3 cached operator weight left at zero collapses the withdrawal quorum
summary: MainchainGatewayV3 implementation 0xfc274ec92bbb1a1472884558d1b5caac6f8220ee replaced the live read `_getTotalWeight() = IBridgeManager(BRIDGE_MANAGER).getTotalWeight()` with a cached `_totalOperatorWeight` that only `initializeV3()` populates, and `initializeV3` is `reinitializer(3)`. The upgrade that installed it ran `initializeV4(wethUnwrapper)` instead, so OpenZeppelin's `_initialized` jumped from 2 to 4 and `initializeV3` became permanently uncallable while the cache stayed at zero. `minimumVoteWeight()` = `(_num * _getTotalWeight() + _denom - 1) / _denom` therefore returns 0 for every value of the threshold parameters, and `_submitWithdrawal`'s verification loop evaluates `weight >= minimumWeight` after the first iteration with no floor on the quorum, so a single arbitrary signature from a non-operator satisfies it. Any caller could then mint themselves an arbitrary withdrawal receipt with an unused id and drain the gateway.

name: Term Finance tETH price-feed decimals mismatch
summary: Term Finance's TermPriceConsumerV3 scales each feed answer by the feed's own decimals(). During a feed migration Term pointed the tETH primary feed at a new TermTEthPriceFeed whose decimals() is hard-coded to 18 while its answer, tETH.convertToAssets(1e18) times the 8-decimal TermWstEthPriceFeed answer divided by 1e18, has 8 decimals. usdValueOfTokens(tETH, 1e18) fell from $2,147.85 to $0.000000215, putting a healthy tETH-collateralised borrower into shortfall; two public liquidators seized 763.245 tETH in the next two blocks against about 8.5e-8 WETH of repayment.

name: Ploutos Money USDC priced from the BTC/USD feed
summary: Ploutos Money, an Aave V3 fork, had its AaveOracle USDC source repointed by the asset-listing admin to Chainlink's BTC/USD proxy, pricing 1 USDC near BTC. In the next block a searcher flash-borrowed a few USDC, supplied them as collateral and borrowed the WETH reserve; a liquidation bot in the same block seized a USDC borrower's USDT collateral for cents.

name: Neemo StakingManagerL1 unauthenticated weETH sweep 12 seconds after upgrade
summary: The StakingManagerL1 implementation installed on the UUPS proxy 0x54cd2346 in the previous block added three new external selectors, and one of them, 0x03b79c24(address), transfers the proxy's entire weETH balance to a caller-supplied address with no role or owner check. The previous implementation did not expose that selector, so the upgrade itself introduced an unauthenticated sweep of the staking manager's whole weETH reserve; a searcher called it 12 seconds later from transaction index 0 of the next block and sold the proceeds into the weETH/WETH Uniswap V3 pool.

name: USPD StabilizerNFT unprotected initializer on a freshly deployed proxy
summary: The StabilizerNFT ERC-1967 proxy was deployed without its initializer being run, leaving the audited implementation’s unprotected initialize() callable by anyone. Twelve seconds after deployment an attacker called it, took the admin and upgrader roles, briefly swapped in an implementation of their own and swapped back so the proxy looked untouched. Seventy-nine days later they used the upgrader role to install purpose-built implementations that minted unbacked USPD and drained stETH from position escrows plus USDC from the USPD/USDC pool.

name: Pundi AI uninitialized swap proxy takeover
summary: Pundi AI deployed its FXSwap ERC1967 proxy with empty init data, leaving initialize(address,address) open. In the next block the attacker initialized it, took ownership and upgraded it to a pass-through backdoor; months later it used the proxy's minter role to mint one million unbacked PUNDIAI and sold them.

name: Radiant Capital rUSDCn index-rounding drain
summary: Radiant (an Aave v2 fork) listed a native USDC market 15 seconds before the exploit. As its only supplier, the attacker inflated the empty reserve's liquidity index with repeated flash loans whose premiums accrued to its tiny supply, then used rounding in rUSDCn burns to withdraw more than it held while borrowing WETH.

name: VOW temporary usdRate exposure
summary: A scheduled rate-setting transaction changed the effective VOW-to-vUSD conversion from [5,1] to [1,100]. Twenty-four seconds later, the attacker flash-borrowed VOW, sent it through the permissionless VSCTokenManager receive path, minted 148.66 million vUSD, and traded it against VOW liquidity pools.

name: Onyx Protocol empty-market rounding
summary: The oPEPE market, listed as collateral with no supply, could be redeemed down to two wei of shares while donated PEPE raised the exchange rate. The attacker borrowed the other markets against the inflated collateral, then redeemUnderlying's truncating division burned one wei to recover the donation, leaving the debt unbacked; a copycat repeated it.

name: Rho Markets native-ETH feed overwritten by rWBTC listing
summary: PriceOracleV2 keys each Chainlink feed by the configured underlying of an rToken. Rho listed rWBTC without setting its RTokenConfig, so its underlying remained the zero address used by the native-ETH market. The admin's subsequent rWBTC feed transaction therefore replaced the ETH/USD feed with WBTC/USD and made 1 ETH read as $63,653.144. Seven borrow transactions then used ETH collateral at that price to remove wstETH from the rwstETH market.

name: PLN permissionless liqBurnAt pair-reserve destruction
summary: PLNTOKEN._transfer contains an unauthenticated branch that destroys the Uniswap V2 pair's own token reserve: when the sender or the recipient is fee-exempt and the recipient is 0xdead, it calls liqBurnAt(), which _basicTransfer's balanceOf(uniswapV2Pair) - minimumTokens from the pair to the dead address and then calls IUniswapV2Pair.sync(). Nothing restricts who may reach that branch, and transferFrom needs no allowance for amount 0 because it settles the allowance with SafeMath.sub(allowance, 0). The attacker therefore bought PLN, called transferFrom(0x3f5a63b89773986fd436a65884fcd321de77b832, 0xdead, 0) to burn 497,295,516.022683914 of the pair's 497,295,616.022683914 PLN and resync the reserves, and sold its position back into the emptied pool. The invariant broken is that an ERC-20 transfer may only move the caller's own approved balance; here a zero-value call moves and burns a third party's liquidity. No parameter repairs it: minimumTokens only sets the burn floor, and the branch stays reachable by any caller at every value.

name: EFVault v4 upgrade storage-layout collision
summary: The EFVault v4.0 implementation put a new assetDecimal variable on the storage slot v3.0 used for maxDeposit without re-initialising it, so assetsPerShare() scaled by the old 5M USDC cap and inflated each share about five million-fold. A small depositor redeemed tiny share amounts twice and withdrew the strategies' funds as USDC.

name: Compound Proposal 62 COMP distribution bug
summary: Proposal 62's Comptroller set the COMP index of markets without rewards to compInitialIndex but re-based a zero user index only when the market index was strictly greater. Borrowers in those markets kept index 0, so any interaction credited their whole normalised borrow as COMP, which claimComp paid out of the Comptroller.

name: Zoth ZeUSD router opened unslippaged USDC deposits
summary: Fifty-one minutes before the exploit, a ZeUSD_Router upgrade removed whitelistedOnly from mintWithStable. The router mints ZeUSD equal to the deposited USDC amount, while WMSubVault swaps that USDC into wM on Uniswap V3 with amountOutMinimum 0, and on redemption swaps wM back with the same zero bound. With a flash loan, the attacker bought the wM/USDC 0.01% pool's wM, added its own liquidity at an extreme price, and deposited 330,979 USDC for 7,669 wM, receiving 327,619 ZeUSD. It then burned that ZeUSD after resetting the pool, so the vault sold 330,979 of its pre-existing wM to repay the attacker in USDC.

name: DeezNutz404
summary: DN404Reflect._transfer() snapshots sender and recipient reflection balances and writes both back without rejecting from == to, so on a self-transfer the recipient credit overwrites the sender debit and the balance grows. The attacker self-transferred repeatedly and sold the unbacked tokens into the WETH pair; copycats repeated it for months.

name: Legendary MoneyMon zero-signer claim bypass
summary: LegendaryMoneyMonNft.verify compares raw ecrecover output with admin without rejecting the zero address. After the owner sets admin to zero, an invalid 65-byte signature recovers zero and authorizes cliamRewred to transfer an arbitrary ERC20 balance to the caller.

name: DDCoin Marketplace sellItem pays the seller twice
summary: Marketplace.sellItem pays the seller and also approves it for the same USDT amount, so a seller can pull each payout twice. An owner setInviteRadio call that put an address into the invite ratio gave inviters unbounded sell credit; the attacker listed through helpers it invited, sold DD into the queued buy orders and pulled every payout again.

name: ResupplyFi zero exchange-rate solvency bypass
summary: ResupplyPair inverted the collateral oracle price with integer division and accepted a zero result. The attacker inflated the nearly empty CurveLend vault's share price by donation so the exchange rate rounded to zero, then borrowed 10 million reUSD against one wei of collateral and swapped it out of the reUSD/scrvUSD Curve pool.

name: Thoreum V4 self-transfer balance doubling
summary: The V4 implementation's transfer accounting credited the recipient without debiting the sender when both are the same address, so any account could call transfer(self, balanceOf(self)) and have its recorded THOREUM balance grow by the post-fee transfer amount. The campaign repeatedly doubled small acquired balances and sold the unsupported tokens into the THOREUM/WBNB BiSwap pair. The defect is permissionless executable logic in the implementation the project itself authored, deployed and installed; the privileged upgrade is the code-change event, not the cause.

name: DDC handleDeductFee missing access control
summary: DDC (a BananaSwap token) exposed handleDeductFee without access control; it debits _balances[from] for any address. The attacker called it with the DDC/USDT pair as from, moving the pair's DDC to the fee handlers, synced the pair and swapped a little DDC for nearly all of its USDT.

name: LI.FI GasZipFacet unvalidated swap call
summary: GasZipFacet.depositToGasZipERC20 passed caller-controlled swap data to LibSwap without the call-target allowlist other facets use, so the LI.FI diamond could be made to call ERC-20 transferFrom against wallets holding unlimited approvals to it.

name: ShiMamaProtocol executePairBurn without access control
summary: ShiMamaProtocol.executePairBurn(referenceIn,minPull,deadline) is callable by anyone and sizes the pull from the caller-supplied referenceIn; it makes ShiMamaToken.forcePullFromPair move that many ShiMama out of the ShiMama/FlapTaxToken PancakeSwap pair, syncs and burns them. The attacker pulled 1,311,349,143.96 ShiMama (all but 21.54) from the pair and sold 30.78 pre-acquired ShiMama into the collapsed reserve for 14.88M of the pair's quote token, which it sold for 52.98 WBNB.

name: Pond0x PNDX public directTransfer
summary: The Pond0x (PNDX) token kept solady's mock helpers directTransfer(from, to, amount) and directSpendAllowance as public functions without access control, so anyone could move anyone's PNDX. Hours after launch, takers moved PNDX out of holders and pools with directTransfer and sold it into the Uniswap PNDX/WETH pools.

name: Aave V3 wstETH CAPO snapshot ratio/timestamp misalignment
summary: WstETHPriceCapAdapter caps the wstETH ratio at snapshotRatio grown since snapshotTimestamp. An automated update wrote a rate-limited snapshotRatio 1.1919 with a 7-day-old snapshotTimestamp meant for 1.2282, capping the ratio near 1.194 vs a live 1.229. Underpriced ~2.85%, wstETH collateral made healthy Core and Prime E-Mode positions liquidatable.

name: MetaSea atomic open/redeem distributor depletion
summary: Round implementation 0x13dde273 added openV6/redeemPosition with no elapsed-time gate: a 3,000 USDT position opened and redeemed in one transaction returns 2,000 USDT plus SEA quoted at the full deposit, paid from the SEA distributor. Attackers looped open/redeem under flash loans and sold the SEA into the SEA/USDT pair.

name: WDGG burnFrom without authorization burns the PancakeSwap pair reserve
summary: The WDGG implementation's burnFrom(from,value) debits any holder's balance with no allowance or caller check (and setWdgAddress lets anyone mark themselves fee-exempt). The attacker exempted its contract, bought 45.62 WDGG, burned 399,902.21 WDGG straight out of the WDGG/USDT pair, called sync() and sold the 45.62 WDGG for 40,008.28 USDT. Two later actors repeated the pair burn against newly added liquidity.

name: AkuAuction refund-counter mismatch permanently locks project funds
summary: claimProjectFunds() required refundProgress to reach totalBids, but processRefunds() advanced refundProgress once per bidder entry while totalBids counted auction units. Once the refund sweep processed every bidder entry, refundProgress stopped at bidIndex below totalBids, so the withdrawal condition can never hold and the auction proceeds stay locked.

name: Unknown leverage helper unauthenticated onMorphoFlashLoan callback
summary: An unverified leverage helper that EOA 0x85b5bef6 deployed and granted Aave v3 credit delegation exposes onMorphoFlashLoan(uint256,bytes) without checking that the caller is Morpho Blue or that a flash loan is in progress. Any caller can make it repay and re-borrow USDC, borrow USDe on behalf of the delegator and forward caller-supplied calldata to the Pendle router, so attackers had 1.51m USDe borrowed against the delegator's position and added as Pendle PT-pUSDe liquidity with the LP tokens minted to themselves.

name: Unizen Trade Aggregator arbitrary call in swap
summary: The implementation installed on the Unizen Trade Aggregator proxy four hours and fifty-two minutes before the exploit added a swap entrypoint, selector 0x1ef29a02, that executes a caller-supplied array of (targetExchange, calldata) calls without checking targetExchange against any exchange whitelist. Callers passed an ERC-20 address as targetExchange and transferFrom(victim, aggregator, amount) as the calldata, so the aggregator spent the allowances users had granted it, and the entrypoint then forwarded the pulled balance to the caller-supplied receiver.

name: Polter Finance BOO price adapter pool-balance ratio
summary: The deployed contract that computes the BOO price is the SpookySwap pool adapter at 0x875d564a6a86f6154592b88f7a107a517f00cc17 (and its byte-identical twin 0x2ceca12a53e428d37a62448fc818bf2e15b7e462), which Polter's price feed 0x80663edff11e99e8e0b34cb9c3e1ff32e82a80fe aggregates and the Aave-fork oracle 0x6808b5ce79d44e89883c5393b487c4296abb69fe serves to lending pool 0x867faa51b3a437b4e2e699945590ef4f2be2a6d5 through getAssetPrice(address). Its latestRoundData() answer is exactly IERC20(WFTM).balanceOf(pool) * chainlinkFtmUsd / IERC20(BOO).balanceOf(pool), reproduced to the wei in the anchor trace: 1,828,570.941372594816969307 WFTM times 0.75128777 divided by 0.000000000001 BOO equals the reported 137,378,298,483,061,759,618,513,154. It reads the pool's raw ERC-20 balances at call time rather than a time-weighted or cumulative observation, and validates nothing: no TWAP window, no minimum-liquidity floor, no deviation cap against the previous answer, no staleness or sanity bound on the ratio. A SpookySwap flash loan that removes every BOO from pool 0xec7178f4c41f346b2721907f5cf7628e388a7a58 except 1,000,000 wei, leaving its WFTM balance untouched, therefore lifts the adapter's answer from about 1.19 USD to 1.37e19 USD per BOO inside one transaction. The attacker deposited 1.000000000000000000 BOO as collateral at that price and drew every other Polter market to zero. No parameter value makes this code correct: the pool, token and Chainlink feed addresses are configuration, but a raw balance ratio is manipulable under every configuration of them.

name: TSURUWrapper unauthorized ERC1155 callback mint
summary: onERC1155Received returns early for the immutable trusted NFT contract but mints for every other caller. Three transfers of an unrelated ERC1155 first minted 1.2 million unbacked TSURU; a later caller minted another 167.2 million directly. Both actors sold the counterfeit tokens into the same WETH pool.

name: SafeMoon public burn() after upgrade
summary: Upgrades hours before the incident made burn(address,uint256) callable by anyone, moving any holder's SFM to the bridge burn address. The attacker burned nearly all SFM held by the SFM/WBNB PancakeSwap pair, sync()'d it to an inflated SFM price and sold its own SFM into the WBNB reserve; copycats repeated this on smaller SFM pairs.

name: MuBank bonds MU and MUG at the live pair quote
summary: MuBank.mu_bond and mu_gold_bond pay out the bank's MU and MUG at quotes computed from live reserves of the Trader Joe USDC.e/MU and MU/MUG pairs. Inside a flash swap of MU from the MU/MUG pair, the attacker dumped MU into USDC.e/MU to skew the quote, bonded 10,290 USDC.e for excess MU and MUG, and sold them back.

name: Themis Balancer LP oracle spot-balance manipulation
summary: Themis priced its B-wstETH-WETH-Stable vault collateral with an oracle that valued the BPT from the Balancer pool's live token balances over total supply. The attacker flash-borrowed WETH, deposited the vault token as collateral, skewed the pool with a large swap to inflate the oracle price, and borrowed far more WETH than the collateral was worth.

name: bZx BZxOracle sUSD Kyber spot-rate collateral valuation
summary: BZxOracle valued collateral at Kyber's marginal getExpectedRate quote, with no averaging or deviation bound. The attacker flash-borrowed WETH from iETH, bought sUSD from the Synthetix depot and pushed the Uniswap V1 sUSD rate Kyber quoted, then deposited the sUSD via iETH borrowTokenFromDeposit and borrowed ETH far above its value.

name: Tender.fi GMXPriceOracle tGMX price 1e20 decimal inflation
summary: Tender.fi activated a new GMXPriceOracle whose tGMX branch multiplied a price already scaled by 1e20 by another 1e10, returning the GMX price with 38 instead of 18 decimals. While it was live, healthy GMX borrowers became liquidatable for wei-sized repayments, and one GMX of collateral let an attacker borrow about $1.59m of every other market's assets.

name: BUBU2 accumulated burn rounds drain the BUBU2/WBNB pair after the owner cut the trigger interval to 120 seconds
summary: BUBU2's transfer hook burned 0.5% of the pair's BUBU2 per elapsed TRIGGER_INTERVAL, uncapped, then synced the pair. After the owner cut the interval to 120 s, 6.7 hours without a trigger accrued 199 rounds; the attacker flash-borrowed WBNB, bought BUBU2, fired the burn with a self-transfer that removed 99.5% of the pair's BUBU2, and sold back.

name: GradientMakerPool heterogeneous-unit LP share accounting
summary: GradientMarketMakerPool minted LP shares on the raw sum of GRAY token units and wei of ETH and redeemed them pro rata against the pool's separate ETH and GRAY totals. A deposit at the pair's ratio, mostly GRAY by unit count, received shares worth far more ETH than it brought, and an immediate withdrawal took other providers' ETH.

name: BoostHook leveraged longs financed at a manipulable spot price
summary: BoostHook's openLong lends ETH from the hook's own Uniswap v4 liquidity bands and spends collateral plus loan on BOOST at the pool's instantaneous price, with caller-set slippage. The attacker bought BOOST, opened 5x longs that pumped the price with band ETH, then sold its BOOST into the pumped pool, leaving the longs insolvent.

name: Unverified BSC executor unrestricted printMoney
summary: The executor contract exposes printMoney(), selector 0x94655f2b, with no caller check. It forwards caller-supplied token, amount and recipient words to the paired holder contract 0xb5cb0555a1d28c9dfdbc14017dae131d5c1cc19c, which trusts the executor as its only authorised caller, so anyone could transfer the holder’s balances anywhere. The attacker called it seven times in one transaction and swept the holder’s WBNB, ETH, USDT, TUSD, BTCB, USDC and FDUSD.

name: XPlayer NodeDistributePlus permissionless DynamicBurnPool drains the XPL/USDT pair
summary: XPL.DynamicBurnPool moves XPL from the XPL/USDT PancakeSwap pair to DEAD and calls sync(), and is restricted to owner, staking, marketing and nodeShareAddress. nodeShareAddress is the NodeDistributePlus proxy, whose DynamicBurnPool(date, amount) forwards any caller's request within the day's burn cap with no caller check. The attacker bought almost all pair XPL with flash-loaned USDT, burned the day's remaining 3,078 XPL cap from the pair through NodeDistributePlus, and sold 57 XPL back against a near-zero XPL reserve for all pair USDT.

name: DIP double router transfer
summary: DIP._transfer executes the base transfer twice when either endpoint is the router. Skimming excess DIP to the router debited the pair twice; sync committed the reduced reserve, allowing the attacker to exchange remaining DIP for almost all AIC.

name: Melo unrestricted mint sold into USDT liquidity
summary: MEL exposed mint(address,uint256,string) without authorization or supply limits. Callers minted arbitrary balances and sold them into the MEL/USDT pair, depleting its USDT. The initial transaction and later repetitions exercise the same immutable token defect.

name: DPCLock claimToken pays DPC at manipulable spot quotes
summary: DPCLock.claimToken sets its unlock multiple from the FSP balance of the FSP/DPC pair plus Staking's total stake, and converts each locker's USDT entitlement to DPC with PancakeRouter getAmountsOut spot quotes. With flash-loaned USDT attackers skewed the pairs, locked FSP via swapDPC, claimed inflated DPC and sold it back.

name: XBITVault fail-open transfer authorization while unbound
summary: XBITVault keeps the XBIT balance ledger and its transfer(from,to,amount) only enforces msg.sender == xbitContract when xbitContract is non-zero. bindXBIT was never called, so anyone could move any holder's XBIT. The attacker moved 1,526,216,569.965537999999999998 XBIT out of the XBIT/USDT PancakeSwap pair, synced its XBIT reserve to 2 wei and sold XBIT back 20 times for the pair's USDT.

name: CitadelRedeem fixed-rate live-route quotation
summary: CitadelRedeem.redeem converted a fixed-rate stake's USD entitlement into WETH with Camelot's live getAmountsOut on the USDC.e/WETH pair. The attacker staked CIT, flash-borrowed 4,500 WETH, dumped it into the pair so each USDC quoted far more WETH, redeemed for treasury WETH and swapped back, three times.

name: XBridge permissionless listToken then withdrawTokens
summary: XBridge.listToken() has no caller restriction, so anyone could register a listing for a token the bridge already custodies and pair it with a corresponding token and chain of their own choosing. The attacker listed the bridge’s own STC, SRLTY and Mazi holdings against listings they controlled and then called withdrawTokens() to move the real deposits out.

name: ARA swap arbitrary approved-source authorization failure
summary: The ARA swap helper let any caller name the source account whose allowance it spent with transferFrom. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker forced an approving EOA to sell ARA, pumped ARA on Pancake V3, forced the same EOA to buy ARA back at the inflated price, and dumped its ARA for USDT.

name: AutoShark SharkMinter mints on donated balances (May 2021)
summary: SharkMinter.mintFor, a PancakeBunny-style minter, zaps its whole LP, SHARK and WBNB balance (balanceOf(this)) into SHARK-BNB liquidity and mints SHARK in proportion to that value, so donated tokens inflate the reward. The attacker sent flash-borrowed WBNB and SHARK to the minter, claimed a tiny vault reward that minted a huge SHARK amount, and sold it.

name: Juice JuiceStaking unbounded stake multiplier
summary: JuiceStaking.stake() accepted any stakeWeek, and harvest() paid a bonus of pending × (stakeWeek − 1) × 9% with no cap. The attacker staked a little JUICE with stakeWeek 3,000,000,000, then called harvest() to pay out the contract's reward pool and stakers' JUICE as bonus, and sold it for ETH.

name: Eminence EMN claim/award bypasses bonding-curve reserve accounting
summary: EminenceCurrency prices buy() and sell() on a Bancor curve over totalSupply and reserveBalance, but its gamemaster functions claim() and award() burn and mint EMN without touching the reserve. eAAVE, a gamemaster, calls them. Under a flash loan the attacker bought EMN, burned half into eAAVE to lift EMN's price, sold, minted it back and sold again.

name: SHIDO permissionless V1-to-V2 migration arbitrage
summary: ShidoLock let anyone deposit a current V1 balance after the global unlock time and redeem the same token count of V2, without a holder snapshot, cutoff, cap, or value check. The attacker flash-bought cheap V1, immediately migrated it 1:1 into the more valuable V2 inventory, and sold the V2 into its WBNB pool.

name: MineSTM live-reserve LP redemption
summary: MineSTM.sell converted the STM a caller sent into a share of its own STM/USDT LP using the pair's live STM reserve, then removed that LP to the caller. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought STM to shrink the reserve, and sold STM back through MineSTM repeatedly, burning nearly all its LP for the pair's USDT.

name: Wault Finance WUSDMaster unbounded spot WEX swap and pro-rata redeem
summary: WUSDMaster.stake() swapped a share of each USDT deposit into WEX at the pair's spot price with zero minimum output and minted WUSD 1:1, while redeem() paid a pro-rata slice of the contract's WEX. The attacker redeemed flash-borrowed WUSD for WEX, pumped the pair, staked 68 times so the contract bought WEX at inflated prices, then sold the WEX back.

name: BRA pair self-transfer tax inflation
summary: BRA's _transfer applied both the buy and the sell tax branch when the BRA/USDT pair sent BRA to itself, deducting one tax but crediting two. With both tax destinations set to the pair, every skim(pair) grew the pair's BRA balance by 3%. Attackers looped skims, skimmed the unreserved BRA out and swapped it for the pair's USDT.

name: Yiedl vault forwards caller-supplied 1inch calldata
summary: The Yiedl vault's redeem path forwarded caller-supplied router calldata without validating the swap recipient, allowing one constructor transaction to deplete the vault's USDC, BTCB, and ETH inventory.

name: Blueberry PriceOracleProxy unscaled price adapter
summary: The money market's PriceOracleProxy returned the CoreOracle's 18-decimal USD price from getUnderlyingPrice() without normalising for the underlying's decimals, so OHM, USDC and WBTC borrows were valued 1e9–1e12 too low. With 1 ETH of bWETH collateral the exploiter borrowed those markets' entire cash.

name: AzukiDAO BEAN repeated airdrop claims
summary: Bean.claim sets signatureClaimed and tokenClaimed but never checks them before paying. NFT holders replay valid signed claims and repeatedly transfer BEAN from the preminted airdrop reserve to themselves, then sell it for ETH.

name: TrustPad LaunchpadLockableStaking reward accounting
summary: receiveUpPool accepts arbitrary callers and trusts their reported lock history. It computes reward debt before increasing the stake, so an attacker supplies an old lock date, repeatedly deposits and withdraws, then compounds unearned historical rewards with stakePendingRewards.

name: Inuko bond prices LP from the pair's raw USDT balance
summary: The Inuko bond contract valued LP as 2 x USDT.balanceOf(pair) x lpAmount / totalSupply and quoted that in INUKO via getAmountsIn. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, sent it to the INUKO/USDT pair, bought bonds with LP while the balance was inflated, skimmed the USDT back, and claimed the oversized INUKO payouts after the lock expired.

name: LotteryTicketSwap50 live-reserve redemption misprices LP
summary: LotteryTicketSwap50 sized each ticket redemption's LP burn from the NATA/USDC pair's live reserves. A flash-financed reserve skew let one helper mint 2,600 tickets and redeem them in 130 calls while destroying too much protocol-owned LP, depleting the protocol entity's native Base USDC.

name: CashCowCoin trading proxy sell() burns CCC from the pair and syncs
summary: CashCowCoin's trading proxy sell() swapped the caller's CCC into the CCC/WBNB pair, then had the token burn that CCC from the pair (proxy-only 0xb20a0b6f) and sync, so each sell took WBNB while the CCC reserve stayed flat. With a flash-loaned buy the attacker ran 80 sells and drained the pair's WBNB.

name: NewFreeDAO reward contract repeatable claim
summary: The NFD reward contract pays its bonus, selector 0x6811e3b9, to any caller in proportion to that caller’s NFD balance and records the claim only against the caller’s own address. The attacker looped: deploy a fresh claimer contract, move the same NFD into it, claim again. The payout multiplied without limit, and the accumulated NFD was sold into the NFD/WBNB pair for its WBNB.

name: D3x.ai exchange spot-price manipulation
summary: The D3x exchange priced USDT/D3XAT conversions with D3XAT.price(), which returned the PancakeSwap spot quote from Router.getAmountsOut with no time-weighting or bound. In one transaction the attacker bought D3XAT from the exchange through fresh helper accounts, pumped the pool's spot price, and redeemed D3XAT against the exchange's USDT at the manipulated quote.

name: GROKD deposit contract unauthenticated updatePool
summary: The GROKD LP-staking contract's implementation exposed updatePool without a caller check, letting anyone overwrite a pool's reward schedule. After staking 1 LP, the attacker raised pool 0's rewardPerBlock to an enormous value and called reward() in the same transaction, collecting almost the contract's whole GROKD reward balance, then sold it.

name: BTC20 presale dynamic-price manipulation
summary: PresaleV4.buyWithEthDynamic priced BTC20 from the spot reserves of the BTC20/WETH Uniswap V2 pair. The attacker flash-borrowed BTC20 from V3 pools, dumped it into the V2 pair to crash the quote, bought the presale's remaining allocation for 12.19 ETH, and sold it back through the pools.

name: YuliAI sell inventory live V3 quotation
summary: YuliAI's sellToken valued incoming YULIAI with a QuoterV2 quote against the live YULIAI/USDT Pancake V3 pool and paid that quote from its USDT inventory. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker pushed the pool price up, sold YULIAI to the contract in many calls at the inflated quote, then sold back into the pool.

name: BYToken permissionless auto-burn of the pair reserve
summary: BYToken's public triggerAutoBurn() burned 1% of total supply per elapsed interval from the BY/WBNB pair, regardless of the pair's own reserve, then synced it. With flash-borrowed WBNB the attacker opened trading, bought the pair's BY down to just above the burn amount, triggered the burn so 1 wei of BY remained, and sold dust BY for all the pair's WBNB.

name: AIDC pair-side accumulated burn
summary: AIDCToken adds 30% of every sell to accumulatedBurnAmount and, on the next ordinary transfer, burns that amount from the AIDC/WBNB pair and syncs it. The attacker bought AIDC through the whitelisted router, sold repeatedly via fresh helpers to pile up the pending burn, triggered burns that drained the pair's AIDC and sold into it for WBNB.

name: BCE deferred burn against the PancakeSwap pair
summary: BCE accrued a scheduledDestruction amount on sells and settled it during a later ordinary transfer by burning that amount out of the PancakeSwap pair's own balance and calling sync(), collapsing the BCE reserve so the attacker's remaining BCE could be sold into the distorted pair for its USDT side.

name: LeetSwap V2 pair public fee-transfer drain
summary: LeetSwapV2Pair declared its fee-transfer helper _transferFeesSupportingTaxTokens(token, amount) public, so anyone could move any amount of a pair's reserve token into its fees contract. After sync() the reserve collapsed and a tiny swap drained the other side; the moved tokens stay locked in the fees contract, outside the fee index.

name: SVT pool marginal-price quote without an invariant
summary: The SVT pool 0x2120f8f305347b6aa5e5dbb347230a8234eb3379 quotes both sides of the market at its instantaneous spot ratio and applies no constant-product or any other invariant to the trade being executed. buy(uint256) (selector 0xd96a094a) takes a 1.5 percent USDT fee and pays out (amount - fee) * 1e18 / price SVT, and sell(uint256) (selector 0xe4849b32) pays out amount * price / 1e18 USDT less a 10 percent fee, where in both cases price = USDT.balanceOf(pool) * 1e18 / SVT.balanceOf(pool) read from the live balances before the transfer. Because the quote ignores the trade's own effect on those balances, a buy moves the ratio without charging for the move, and the SVT just bought redeems immediately at the new, higher ratio. I reproduced all four legs of the anchor transaction to the wei with that formula. The invariant broken is that an automated market maker must price a trade against the reserve curve it will end on, not against the marginal price it starts from. No parameter repairs it: for any fee below 100 percent an attacker sizes the buy so that the ratio distortion exceeds the fees, and as the USDT input approaches the pool's USDT balance the payout approaches the pool's whole SVT inventory.

name: Zeed Finance YEED reflection skim drain
summary: The YEED token distributes a reflection fee to every holder on each transfer, including the PancakeSwap pairs it trades in, without those pairs resyncing. The attacker cycled skim() between the three YEED pairs so each cycle credited the pairs more YEED than their recorded reserves, then swapped the accumulated YEED out for the pools’ USDT.

name: Bazaar Balancer-fork exitPool without sender validation
summary: The Bazaar vault, a Balancer fork, passed exitPool's caller-chosen sender to the LBP without checking that the caller was that sender or its approved relayer, and the LBP only required sender to be its owner. The attacker exited the only registered LBP naming its owner as sender and itself as recipient, taking the pool's WETH and rYOLO.

name: Trusted-forwarder open relay approval drain
summary: Forwarder 0x26bbc304 appended any caller-claimed sender to caller-supplied calldata and called the target without checking a signature or the caller. Executor 0xa152 trusted it as its ERC-2771 forwarder, so anyone could act as any user who had approved the executor's AllowanceTarget and have that user's tokens pulled and swapped to themselves.

name: ATM BlindBox predictable expired-blockhash settlement
summary: BlindBox bets resolve on blockhash(betBlock+2), but anyone may settle any bet at any time, and after that hash expires _trySettle uses keccak256(prevrandao, betId, timestamp), known to the settler. The attacker stalled auto-settlement with 1-ATM filler bets and settled expired losing bets only in blocks where the fallback made them win 1.95x from DEAD.

name: Will trading zero-margin order forced into public expired settlement
summary: The WILL short-trading contract's placeSellOrder accepts margin 0, giving closeTime = block.timestamp, and sells contract-held (staked) WILL for USDT. Anyone can then call updateExpiredOrders, which books 1.8x the shorted USDT for buy-back, and settleExpiredPositions, which spends that contract USDT on WILL at the live pool price with a caller-chosen minTokensToReceive. The attacker opened an instantly expired order, pumped WILL, and made the contract buy back at the inflated price before dumping.

name: Unknown BSC swap-bot contract lets anyone swap approved wallets without slippage limits
summary: Unverified contract 0x16d7c6f4, used by an operator's EOAs to trade for managed wallets, let any caller name a wallet in f8c03cc4: it pulled that wallet's approved tokens, sold them on PancakeSwap V3 with no minimum output and bought the same amount back for the caller. After moving the pools, the attacker ran it for 152 approved wallets.

name: CS Token stale sellAmount pair burn
summary: CS stores the current sell size in a global sellAmount variable, then lets a later qualifying transfer consume that stale value to burn 80% of it directly from the CS/USDT pair before calling pair.sync(). The attacker repeatedly paired a sale with a self-transfer to contract the CS reserve and drain USDT.

name: MetaWin staking USD reward settled at FCN/USDT pair balance spot price
summary: The staking contract 0x431abb27dab05f4e7cdeaa18390fe39364197500 accrues each staker a reward denominated in USD and settles it in FCN at a price it derives, inside the paying transaction, from two raw balanceOf reads on the PancakeSwap V2 FCN/BSC-USD pair 0xacb496dd4a8b6b9d1b99d422b8700f6ef932bc10. In the anchor transaction the claim entry point, selector 0xd9574d4c, reads the caller's stored 10e18 USD entitlement from slot 0x9c6375cda627d083cbb712ee89f8748935cee8e2ed0be5ca571a2fdf7ae3eba3, reads BSC-USD.balanceOf(pair) = 0.02 and FCN.balanceOf(pair) = 0.501971077397338362, and pays out 10 / (0.02 / 0.501971077397338362) = 250.985538698669186971 FCN. Those pair balances are what the caller had just set: the same transaction is a PancakeSwap flash swap that removed 512963.341056079475662703 BSC-USD from that exact pair before calling the claim. The invariant violated is that a fixed USD liability may not be settled at an instantaneous, caller-controllable AMM quote; there is no TWAP, no minimum-reserve or deviation guard, no getReserves-versus-balance check and no re-entrancy or flash-loan protection on the read. No parameter value repairs it: the reward rate, the priced pair and the fee split are configuration, and at any non-zero entitlement a claimer who can move the pair's balances within the transaction converts that entitlement into an arbitrary quantity of FCN.

name: OPC trading helper burns sold tokens out of its pair
summary: Every OPC trade goes through the unverified helper 0xa642e668. On a sell (db3f7000 with flag 1), it swaps 95% of the tokens into the OPC/USDT pair, burns 90% of the sold amount from the pair with burnFrom, and calls sync(), so the pair's OPC reserve barely grows while USDT flows out. Its e3bb6e96 liquidity removal also pays the caller the helper's entire OPC balance. The attacker flash-borrowed 10M USDT and bought OPC with the helper as recipient, then swept it out with e3bb6e96. It made 100 helper sells, each burning OPC from the pair, and dumped the rest, taking 112,750 USDT.

name: Brahma TOPG zapper unvalidated call
summary: The Brahma TOPG Zapper's zapIn called a caller-supplied swapTarget with caller-supplied calldata. The attacker passed its own contract as the input token and USDC.transferFrom calldata, moving USDC from three accounts that had approved the Zapper to itself.

name: ZORA community claim allocation to the stateless 0x Settler
summary: ZoraTokenCommunityClaim pays each account's allocation to any _claimTo chosen by that account. Its allocation setter wrote a 5,500,777.45 ZORA allocation for 0x's BaseSettler, a stateless router whose execute runs arbitrary actions for any caller. Once claims opened, an attacker's constructor had the Settler call claim(attacker) and received the whole allocation.

name: NXUSD Cauldron LP-price accounting
summary: The Cauldron accepted a live reserve-derived LP valuation when checking solvency, allowing one borrower to withdraw 998,000 NXUSD against insufficient JLP collateral.

name: Bedrock uniBTC vault native mint without price conversion
summary: The uniBTC Vault's payable mint() minted one uniBTC per whole native coin, a rate only sound on BTC-gas chains. The upgrade that activated this code replaced the balance-based cap check with a supply-feeder total that returned 0 for NATIVE_BTC, so native mints passed on ETH chains. Attackers minted uniBTC 1:1 for ETH or BNB and sold it into uniBTC pools.

name: BitCrown distributor missing caller authorization
summary: The stateless distributor let any caller choose a token, recipients and amounts for transfers from its own balance. The attacker removed its entire 100,000 BTCn inventory and sold it for USDT.

name: Malda Migrator accepted an attacker-supplied Comptroller
summary: Malda's Migrator took the Mendi comptroller from caller calldata and trusted whatever positions its markets reported. The attacker passed a fake comptroller reporting fake positions, so the Migrator minted unbacked mTokens, made the eight Malda markets lend underlying via borrowMigration, and repaid the fake markets, which pulled the tokens.

name: Dexible v2 selfSwap arbitrary router call
summary: Dexible v2's selfSwap() executed each route's caller-supplied router address and calldata from the Dexible proxy without checking the router against an allowlist. The attacker routed through token contracts with transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount), draining wallets that had approved Dexible, on Ethereum and on the Arbitrum deployment.

name: DCF Token sell-side burnPair reserve destruction
summary: DCF's sell path burned (amount - 5% fee) / deadCfg tokens from the PancakeSwap pair's own balance and called sync() before crediting the seller. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker bought almost all DCF out of the pair to a buy-restriction-whitelisted address, then sold DCF sized to burn the pair's remainder to dust and swapped it for the pair's USDT.

name: Alpha Homora v2 HomoraBank zero debt-share borrow
summary: HomoraBank v2's permissionless resolveReserve raised a bank's totalDebt without minting debt shares, and borrow() converted amounts to shares with truncating division, recording zero debt for borrows below totalDebt/totalShare. After shrinking the sUSD bank to one share, the attacker borrowed sUSD for free repeatedly via its own spell, used it as Iron Bank collateral and drained other markets.

name: DEI lending sAMM spot-oracle liquidation drain
summary: The DEI lender valued Solidex sAMM-USDC/DEI collateral with an oracle reading the pair's spot balances. Inside a flash swap that pulled DEI out of that pair, the attacker liquidated the now-undercollateralized borrowers, burned their DEI debt, took their LP collateral and redeemed it for USDC and DEI.

name: Stars Arena share-buy reentrancy
summary: The share-buy entry point (selector 0xe9ccf3a3) sent AVAX back to the caller before finalising share accounting, letting the attacker re-enter the weight-setting function (selector 0x5632b2e4) mid-call so that a single share could then be sold via sellShares() for ~266,000 AVAX.

name: Warp Finance LP collateral priced from spot reserves
summary: UniswapLPOracleFactory.getUnderlyingPrice valued a Uniswap V2 LP token as (twapPrice0 * reserve0 + twapPrice1 * reserve1) * 10**decimals / totalSupply, taking the reserves from the pair's instantaneous state through UniswapV2Library.getReserves while taking only the unit prices from a TWAP. Flash-loaned swaps that skewed the DAI/WETH pair raised that sum without changing totalSupply, so WarpControl.getBorrowLimit valued the attacker's LP collateral at 135.470392 USDC per token against a true 58.815427 and authorised 3.86 million DAI and 3.92 million USDC of borrowing. The reserve term is unbounded and none of the contract's parameters bounds or averages it, so no parameter value makes the function correct.

name: GDCToken sell burn exceeds forwarded amount, with reentrant tax-free exit
summary: GDCToken's sell hook forwards 30% of a taxed sell to the pair but burns the full sold amount from the pair's reserve and syncs, and a mid-sell referral BNB callback lets transfers into the pair skip the tax. Constructor-deposit helpers bought GDC; a sell then collapsed the GDC reserve while a pre-bought bag was dumped tax-free at the inflated price.

name: SELLC StakingRewards permissionless token listing and spot-priced sell
summary: StakingRewards.addLiquidity has no access control and sets listToken[_token]=true for any caller-supplied token. sell(token, token1, amount) then pays any token1 the contract holds, priced from the caller-controlled token/token1 pair. The attacker listed its own token, created a custom pair against SellQILP (the SELLC/QIQI LP that StakingRewards held) and sold worthless tokens for the contract's LP. It burned the LP and dumped the SELLC for WBNB. Copycats repeated the drain within hours.

name: FPC sell hook drains the pair reserve and syncs
summary: On every sell FPC's _update calls burnLpToken, which moves 65% of the sold amount out of the PancakeSwap pair and calls sync() before the swap settles, collapsing the pair's FPC reserve. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought most of the pair's FPC, then sold FPC so the router priced it against a near-zero reserve.

name: Sonne Finance soVELO empty-market donation
summary: Sonne's timelock queued the listing of an empty soVELO market with a 35% collateral factor, executable by anyone after the delay. The attacker executed it, minted 2 wei of soVELO and donated VELO to inflate the Compound-v2 exchange rate, borrowed other markets' assets against that collateral, and recovered the donation via redeemUnderlying rounding.

name: P719 internal AMM mints its swap output and burns its swap input
summary: P719 is its own market maker: sending BNB to the token buys, and transferring the token to the token sells. Both legs quote a constant-product price from the token's own two balances, tokenOut = balanceOf(token) * bnbIn / (address(token).balance + bnbIn) and bnbOut = address(token).balance * tokenIn / (balanceOf(token) + tokenIn), but neither leg settles against the reserve it just priced. The buy leg mints 1.55x the quoted output instead of debiting balanceOf(token), paying the quote to the buyer, 10 percent and 5 percent of it to two fee sinks and retaining 40 percent, so the token reserve rises when it should fall. The sell leg takes 95 percent of the incoming tokens as the swap input and then burns exactly that amount, forwarding the remaining 5 percent to the fee sinks, so the token reserve does not rise while the BNB reserve is paid out. The product of the two reserves is therefore not preserved by a swap: over the exploit transaction it collapsed from 4.3015e43 to 1.3229e42, 3.1 percent of its starting value, and 3,440 BNB of buys were redeemed for 3,987.799074208829188341 BNB of sells.

name: DPC stake changes duplicate accrued reward quota
summary: DPC's stakeLp and claimStakeLp add getClaimQuota() to oldClaimQuota although getClaimQuota() already includes oldClaimQuota, so each stake change doubles the accrued airdrop credit. The attacker bought airdrop allotments, staked LP, looped claimStakeLp to inflate the credit, and drained DPC through claimDpcAirdrop.

name: NGFS public proxy initialization
summary: NGFSToken left its single-use proxy initializer public, letting the attacker appoint its own contract as both privileged proxy and library, credit itself an unbacked NGFS balance, and sell it against the NGFS/USDT pool.

name: Pike Finance uninitialized upgrade implementation
summary: The implementation Pike installed on 2024-04-28 to fix an earlier incident left initialize() reachable on the proxy, so the first caller could set every privileged role. The attacker called initialize() to make itself owner and upgrader, then called upgradeToAndCall() through the same implementation to install its own logic and sweep the proxy’s 479.39 ETH in the same transaction.

name: CrowdRingCircle pair-reserve burn
summary: CRC's sell hook burned the sold amount from the receiving DEX pair's own balance and called sync() before crediting the seller. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker bought almost all CRC out of the pair (routed to the restriction-exempt owner), then sold CRC equal to the pair's remainder, burning its reserve to dust, and swapped it for the pair's USDT.

name: RANT pair-reserve burn and sync
summary: A transfer of RANT to the token contract invoked _sellBurnLiquidityPairTokens(amount), which removed an attacker-sized amount of RANT directly from the RANT/WBNB pair and called sync() without removing WBNB. The resulting reserve collapse let rant_center sell the attacker's remaining RANT into the manipulated pair and extract its WBNB reserve.

name: Scroll Network token unchecked router transfer underflow
summary: SCROLL's transfer(address,uint256) blocks ordinary holder-to-holder transfers with a bare "Err" revert but exempts the Uniswap UniversalRouter, and on that exempt path it debits the sender without any balance-sufficiency check. Because UniversalRouter.execute is permissionless and its TRANSFER command (0x05) moves the router's own token balance, the attacker made the zero-balance router send 1 wei of SCROLL, underflowing the router's SCROLL balance to 2^256-1, then routed 136,275,915 SCROLL from that fabricated balance into the SCROLL/WETH Uniswap V2 pair and swapped it out for the pair's entire WETH reserve.

name: wBARL pod flash-loan bond reentrancy
summary: The wBARL WeightedIndex pod's flash() sent out the pod's entire BARL reserve and only checked its balance after the callback, so the attacker called bond() inside the callback: the bonded BARL repaid the loan and also minted pod shares. Repeating this and debonding the free shares drained the pod's BARL, which was sold for DAI and WETH.

name: JimboController permissionless shift/reset rebalancing
summary: JimboController.shift() and reset() were public and redeployed the protocol-owned ETH liquidity of the JIMBO/ETH Trader Joe LB pair around the current active bin, with no price bound. With flash-loaned WETH the attacker moved the active bin, called shift()/reset() so the ETH was placed at the manipulated price, and bought it out with JIMBO.

name: GymSinglePool depositFromOtherContract missing access control
summary: GymSinglePool.depositFromOtherContract had no caller check and its _autoDeposit credits a staking deposit for any _from address without pulling tokens. From a series of throwaway contracts the attacker booked fake GYMNET deposits, claimed rewards on them and withdrew the fabricated principal out of the pool's real GYMNET, then sold it for BNB.

name: Unibot router unvalidated external call
summary: The direct Unibot router's externally callable function 0xb2bd16ab accepted an unvalidated external target and calldata without binding the token owner to the caller or an authorized Unibot operator. It therefore made attacker-selected transferFrom calls as the approved router, allowing the original exploiter to pull tokens from wallets that had approved it.

name: MBU deposit() price-scale mint inflation
summary: The MobiusDAO deposit proxy's deposit(token, amount) values the deposit as amount x oracle token price without dividing out the 18-decimal price scale, then mints value x 1e18 / MBU price, so it mints 1e18 times the correct MBU. A 0.001 WBNB deposit (0.657 USD at the oracle's 656.92 USD/BNB) minted 9731099570720980.659843835099042677 MBU instead of 0.00973 MBU; selling 28,500,000 of them into the MBU/USDT PancakeSwap pair drained 2,157,126 USDT. Copycats repeated the same 0.001 WBNB deposit ten more times.

name: Value DeFi vSafe StrategyAlpacaWBNB in-flight ibBNB valuation
summary: StrategyAlpacaWBNB values its ibBNB at Alpaca's spot totalToken()/totalSupply(), and vSafe WBNB mints shares against that value. Inside Alpaca Vault.work() the loan leaves before the debt is booked, so the attacker's farming token re-entered vSafe depositFor() from approve() at a depressed share price and redeemed at the true price later, nine times.

name: Rugged Art RuggedMarket targetedPurchase arbitrary router call
summary: RuggedMarket.targetedPurchase ran caller-supplied Universal Router commands before settling. From the router's ETH callback the attacker staked flash-loaned RUGGED, the purchase then paid those tokens out as NFTs while the stake stayed credited, and a following unstake withdrew the market's RUGGED again.

name: dForce LPCurveGaugeAggregatorModel read-only reentrancy
summary: LPCurveBaseAggregatorModel._getPrice(), the code behind dForce's wstETHCRV-gauge vault aggregator, prices the collateral as priceOracle.getUnderlyingPrice(pool.coins(0)) * pool.get_virtual_price(). get_virtual_price() is an unguarded external view on the Curve ETH/wstETH pool 0x6eb2dc694eb516b16dc9fbc678c60052bbdd7d80 and returns D * PRECISION / token_supply, so while remove_liquidity() is paying out native ETH through raw_call the LP supply has already been reduced but the balances have not fully settled and the ratio is wrong. The aggregator performs the read with no reentrancy probe, so re-entering from the pool's ETH refund let the attacker have dForce value the vwstETHCRV-gauge collateral at a distorted price, seize a 1,019.577317265394873995 gauge-token position and mint 1,219,437.439363481229905117 USX of unbacked debt in the same transaction.

name: GiddyVaultV3 compound signature covers only the swap payload hash
summary: GiddyVaultV3.compound() authenticates the caller with an EIP-712 signature whose digest binds only keccak256 of each SwapInfo.data field, leaving the accompanying fromToken, toToken, amount and aggregator addresses outside the signed scope. The attacker replayed a signature the operator had already produced, substituted its own token and aggregator parameters, and had the vault route the strategies’ balances out through an aggregator it controlled.

name: MonoX Monoswap self-swap price inflation
summary: Monoswap never rejected tokenIn == tokenOut and wrote the tokenIn price before the tokenOut price, so repeated MONO-for-MONO swaps ratcheted MONO's internal price; removeLiquidity also let anyone pull other LPs' liquidity. The attacker emptied the MONO pool, pumped MONO and sold it for the other pools' assets on Polygon, then Ethereum.

name: Cream Finance (AMP reentrancy)
summary: crAMP's borrow transferred hook-enabled AMP before recording the borrower's new debt, so the attacker's ERC-1820 tokensReceived hook re-entered crETH.borrow while the comptroller still saw the crAMP debt as unrecorded, borrowing ETH against collateral the outer borrow had already consumed.

name: MINER ERC-X self-transfer balance duplication
summary: The MINER ERC-X token's _transfer rejects only the zero address for sender and receiver, and the _update it calls caches uint256 fromBalance = _balances[from] and uint256 toBalance = _balances[to] before writing _balances[from] = fromBalance - value and _balances[to] = toBalance + value. When from == to the second write restores the pre-transfer balance and adds value on top, so a transfer to one's own address is a pure credit of value out of nothing while _totalSupply is unchanged. The attacker's contract looped this self-transfer 2000 times inside a Uniswap V3 swap callback, minting the MINER it owed the pool and paying for 999.999999999999998 MINER of output it never held. No parameter value repairs this: the write order is wrong for every amount.

name: UvToken Eco Staking pool caller-supplied pledge contract
summary: The UvTokenWallet Eco Staking pool 0x5ecfda78754ec616ed03241b4ae64a54d6705a1a pays withdrawals from a caller-supplied pledge contract address. Its withdraw function (selector 0xc81daf6e, arguments user and pledge) asks that address for the user's amount through selector 0x95b81c68 and has UVT vault 0x36f277165c8b1b80cc3418719badb1864e2687bc transfer that amount, without checking the address against the pool's registered pledges. The attacker passed its own contract, which reported 100,449,018.65 UVT, received that from the vault and sold it for 5,011.175 WBNB.

name: Four.meme launchpad liquidity migration into pre-initialized pools
summary: The launchpad's addLiquidity() migration accepted an existing PancakeSwap V3 pool without checking its initialized price, so attackers pre-created pools at manipulated sqrtPriceX96 values and swapped out the WBNB deposited during migration.

name: MO Loan borrow burns pair reserves and prices collateral from the manipulated spot
summary: Loan.borrow priced MO collateral at the MO/USDT pair's spot reserves and then burned 90% of the borrowed amount from the pair's own reserves, while duration-0 orders could be redeemed at once for the full collateral. The attacker looped borrow/redeem to ratchet the MO price, then borrowed USDT and sold MO into the depleted pair.

name: GlueX callback drains CoW fee buffers
summary: The GlueX swap helper authenticates uniswapV3SwapCallback against a pool address supplied in the callback data itself. A caller supplies its own address as the pool, the CoW settlement as payer and an approved token, causing transferFrom to pay the caller without an active swap.

name: STO pending sell burn removes the previous sale from the STO/WBNB pair, with trading opened by permissionless initializeLiquidity
summary: While burnEnabled is set, every non-whitelisted sale to the STO/WBNB pair adds its after-tax amount to pendingBurnFromSell, and the next non-pair transfer moves that amount from the pair to DEAD and calls sync(), so a seller can sell and then delete the sold tokens from the reserve. Buying was still disabled, but initializeLiquidity is permissionless and enables buying and selling once the pair holds 2,000 WBNB. The attacker donated flash-loaned WBNB to the pair, called initializeLiquidity with 1 wei of BNB, bought 7.85M STO, and alternated sells with transfers that burned each prior sale from the pair until it held no WBNB.

name: Neko Network MainPool borrow on behalf of any account
summary: Neko's Aave-style MainPool borrow(asset, amount, onBehalfOf) minted the variable debt to onBehalfOf but paid the underlying to msg.sender, with no borrow-allowance or credit-delegation check. Anyone could borrow against another depositor's collateral and keep the funds; the attacker and copycats borrowed USDT, BUSD, USDC and BTCB against 16 depositors.

name: LEDS chained unguarded deflationary burns collapse the pair reserve
summary: The LEDS implementation had several unguarded burns of LEDS from its WBNB pair followed by sync (triggerDailyBurnAndMint, a deferred sell-burn and a public flush). Inside flash loans the attacker made LP deposits, chained the burns to cut the pair's LEDS reserve to dust while its WBNB stayed, then swapped tiny LEDS back for the WBNB.

name: Cover Protocol Blacksmith stale-cache infinite mint
summary: Blacksmith.deposit cached the pool struct in memory before updatePool and set the miner's rewardWriteoff from the stale accRewardsPerToken. Exploiters left a pool with ~1 LP so the next update jumped the index, deposited a large amount in that update and withdrew, minting COVER for rewards accrued before their deposit.

name: SpiralHookV2 spot-price borrow with tx.origin same-block guard
summary: SpiralHookV2.borrow values SPIRAL collateral at the live slot0 price of its own Uniswap V4 pool, and its only same-block defence keys lastSwapBlockOf on tx.origin. The attacker pumped the pool from one EOA, then borrowed hook-owned ETH against the bought SPIRAL at the inflated spot from six other EOAs through one contract in the same block.

name: ATK live-pair reward pricing
summary: The ATK reward contract sized claimToken1 from the configured pair's live ATK and USDT balances, so a claim inside a pair callback released reward inventory at a transient reserve ratio and the resulting ATK removed USDT from the pair.

name: Pesto self-balance-triggered swapback sandwich
summary: PESTO's transfer hook sells the token contract's own balance on Uniswap V2 with no slippage bound whenever a sell arrives and that balance exceeds a threshold. Inside a Uniswap V3 flash loan the attacker sold PESTO, topped up the contract's balance by direct transfer, triggered the swapback with a small sell and bought back cheaper.

name: SocketGateway wrapped-token swap route arbitrary call
summary: Socket route 406 (WrappedTokenSwapperImpl 0xcc5fda5e3ca925bd0bb428c8b2669496ee43067e) is delegatecalled by SocketGateway and, in performAction, forwards fully caller-controlled calldata to a caller-controlled address with `fromToken.call(swapExtraData)`. With amount = 0 the surrounding balance-delta and safeTransferFrom checks are satisfied trivially, so the attacker made the gateway execute `USDC.transferFrom(victim, attacker, allowance)` and equivalent calls on WETH, USDT, WBTC, DAI and MATIC, draining every unlimited approval users held on SocketGateway. The route had been registered three days earlier through NewRouteAdded(uint32,address); the gateway itself was never upgraded.

name: DEI lender Solidex LP oracle balance-based collateral valuation
summary: The Solidex DEI/USDC LP oracle used by DeiLenderSolidex priced LP collateral from the Solidly pair's live token balances and getAmountOut quote, and checked the Muon-signed price only against that same on-chain value. With flash-borrowed USDC the attacker pushed the pair, inflating its LP collateral's value, borrowed 17.2M unbacked DEI and sold it.
unverified: 0x8129026c585bcfa530445a6267f9389057761a00: slot write attributed to block 36852574, not traced to 0x24d5e3339aef3cff6e7567671109d257c2fb1dfb1a0291f74b3cba301f58e41e

name: USDTStakingContract28 public tokenAllowAll()
summary: tokenAllowAll(token, spender) was public with no owner check, so the attacker had the staking contract approve them for unlimited USDT and then transferred out the whole deposit balance.

name: Origin Dollar Vault mintMultiple reentrancy
summary: VaultCore.mintMultiple() skipped the supported-asset check that mint() performed, so the attacker passed a self-controlled fake stablecoin whose transferFrom re-entered the vault and triggered a rebase between the first mint's asset transfer and its OUSD supply increase, minting more OUSD than the vault held in assets.

name: DeltaPrime claimReward unvalidated LFJ pair
summary: DeltaPrime's TraderJoeV2 facet claimReward(pair, ids) accepted any LFJ pair and paid the Prime Account's balance increase of the pair hook's reward token to the owner with no solvency check. The attacker's fake pair re-entered wrapNativeToken to wrap borrowed native AVAX or ETH mid-claim, so pool loans were paid out as rewards.

name: SushiSwap RouteProcessor2 unvalidated route pool
summary: RouteProcessor2.processRoute() never checked that the pool address encoded in the caller-supplied `route` was a genuine UniswapV3 pool. The router called swap() on that address and then trusted whoever called back into uniswapV3SwapCallback(), whose implementation transfers `tokenIn` from the address recorded in the router's transient `lastCalledPool`/msg.sender state instead of from the caller. An attacker-controlled contract posing as a pool could therefore make the router execute transferFrom against any wallet that had granted RouteProcessor2 an ERC20 allowance.

name: NOVO transferFrom without allowance check drains the NOVO/WBNB pair
summary: NOVO's transferFrom moves tokens from any sender without spending an allowance (the _approve deduction is commented out). The attacker bought NOVO with flash-swapped WBNB, called transferFrom to move most of the NOVO/WBNB pair's NOVO to the token contract, synced the pair, and sold NOVO into the collapsed reserve for the pair's WBNB, then repeated five blocks later.

name: RWT privileged sell reserve burn
summary: The role-authorized RWT sell contract exposed sell() without caller authorization and each call burned tokens from the AMM pair before sync, letting anyone repeatedly inflate the pool price and drain USDT.

name: Midas Capital fsAMM-HAY-BUSD cToken rounding loss
summary: Midas CToken.redeemFresh converts a requested underlying amount into cTokens to burn with truncating division. The attacker cut the empty fsAMM-HAY-BUSD market to 1,001 wei of supply, donated LP to inflate the exchange rate, borrowed three markets' cash against it, then redeemed ~2 wei of underlying per 1 wei burned to withdraw it, leaving bad debt.

name: ChaingeFinance MinterProxyV2 arbitrary-call allowance drain
summary: MinterProxyV2.swap() called a caller-chosen target with caller-chosen calldata, only checking that the proxy's balance of a caller-chosen receive token rose. Attackers pointed it at token contracts with transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount), draining the tokens Chainge's wallet had approved to the proxy.

name: AROS claim flow zeroed its own AMM pair reserve
summary: AROS's signed claims pay out of its own AROS/USDT pair and then sync it, with no floor on the remaining reserve. The attacker bought the pair down to its claimable amount, routing the AROS to the whitelisted feeRecipient to pass the buy block, claimed that amount so sync set the AROS reserve to zero, and bought all the pair's USDT for a little AROS.

name: edel-xStock mutable ERC-4626 share-rate oracle
summary: The wGOOGLx price source multiplied an independent stock price by wGOOGLx's same-transaction convertToAssets rate, so an underlying donation could atomically inflate collateral value and support reserve borrowing.

name: Lodestar GLPOracle donatable plvGLP exchange rate
summary: Lodestar's GLPOracle priced plvGLP collateral from plvGLP's spot totalAssets/totalSupply. The attacker built a looped lplvGLP position, donated GLP to the Plutus vault to inflate the exchange rate, borrowed every market's liquidity against the inflated collateral, and redeemed the borrowed plvGLP at the inflated rate.

name: OneRing OShare vault share price from spot strategy valuation
summary: The OShare vault implementation prices its shares from IStrategyManager.investedBalanceInUSD(), an aggregate mark that each MasterChef strategy derives from the live token balances of the stable pools it farms via getUSDBalanceFromUnderlyingBalance(). depositSafe() reads that mark before pulling the deposit, routes the deposit into the same pools through assetToUnderlying(), and mints shares from the USD figure the strategies report after the pools have moved; withdraw() reads the same mark again and then settles by removing the caller's pro-rata share of the strategies' LP positions. Both legs of a deposit-then-withdraw round trip therefore read a quantity the deposit itself controls inside one transaction. With an 80,000,000 USDC Solidly flash loan the attacker deposited 79,999,997 USDC into a vault whose pre-deposit mark was 4,448,686.168049134972760253 USD on 4,185,979.962653993796224466 shares, was credited an under-reported 44,599,205.960575506514590319 USD and minted 41,965,509.691846094312718922 shares, and then burned them for 47,696,475.292371545217068603 marked USD which settled as 81,534,750.101089 USDC out of the still-imbalanced pools. Boundary test: the mark is read unconditionally in the executed deposit and withdraw paths with no time average, invariant-based valuation or deviation bound, and the only caller-facing guard is the depositor's own _minAmount argument, so no configured value makes the deployed code correct.

name: Astrid unvalidated restaked-token withdrawal
summary: AstridProtocol.withdraw accepted any contract as the restaked token. Withdrawal processing trusted the fake token's stakedTokenAddress() and scaledBalanceToBalance(), so attacker-deployed tokens booked the protocol's real stETH, rETH and cbETH as claimable and claim() paid them out.

name: Value DeFi MultiStables vault share value from manipulable Curve 3pool quote
summary: MultiStablesVault prices a share against IMultiVaultController.balanceOf(3CRV, _sell), which converts every non-3CRV strategy holding through ShareConverter.convert_shares_rate. That function quotes the holding as StableSwap3Pool.calc_token_amount([0, usdc, 0], true), a spot, fee-free, single-transaction-manipulable pool quantity. Because mint uses balance() before the transfer and redemption uses balance_to_sell() computed at the same instant, an attacker who deposits, imbalances the Curve 3pool and redeems inside one transaction is paid at an inflated share price. In the anchor the identical BUSD-pool holding of 1,988,683.965709684903991584 BCrv quoted 2,100,754.566072978362359769 3CRV before the imbalance and 11,140,592.572211842856711915 3CRV after it, so 24,923,202.990614843737795018 shares redeemed for 33,089,069.045892566308558644 3CRV. withdrawFor carries no contract-depositor guard at all, and the deposit-side checkContract guard was satisfied because the whitelisted ValueVaultBank 0x8764f2c305b79680cfcc3398a96aedea9260f7ff forwards any caller's deposit.

name: BTC24H Lock claim() without beneficiary check
summary: The BTC24H Lock held the owner's 110,000 BTC24H until a release date, but claim() checked only the date and a claimed flag and paid the whole amount to msg.sender. After the release date, before the owner claimed, the attacker called claim() and sold the tokens through Uniswap V3 pools in the same transaction.

name: Umbrella StakingRewards unchecked withdrawal accounting
summary: StakingRewards.withdraw() subtracted the caller-supplied amount from total supply and the caller's balance without checked arithmetic (Solidity 0.7), so an unstaked caller could withdraw LP it never staked. Front-running bots, the named attacker and copycats drained the UMB LP pools on BSC and Ethereum.

name: DKP exchange live-pair valuation
summary: The DKP exchange contract (unverified) sizes DKP payouts from the DKP/USDT pair's live token balances. The attacker flash-swapped nearly all USDT out of the pair, called exchange at the depressed DKP price for a large DKP payout, repaid the flash swap and sold the DKP into the pair.

name: MIC public swapManual()
summary: MIC's unrestricted swapManual() paid LP fees according only to msg.sender's current LP-token balance and reduced a global fee pool without recording which LP position had already claimed. Transferring the same LP position between addresses therefore allowed repeated claims against the remaining accrued fees.

name: Harvest Finance Vault share price from manipulable Curve y-pool mark
summary: Harvest's fUSDC and fUSDT vaults priced shares with the strategy's investedUnderlyingBalance, which valued its yCRV through Curve Y pool's spot calc_withdraw_one_coin. With flash loans the attacker skewed the Y pool, deposited at the depressed share price, unwound the swap and withdrew at the restored price, staying inside the 3% arb check, in 30 rounds.

name: Zoomer buyback spot-price accounting
summary: The buyback contract valued incoming ZOOMER at the current pool spot price, allowing one transaction to exchange attacker-supplied tokens for most of the contract's ETH inventory.

name: FoxLpBondsPool pre-swap spot pricing over-mints FOX
summary: stake() prices the entire USDT bond from the FOX/USDT pair before swapping half of that same deposit through the shallow pair. It then mints FOX-denominated bond and referral inventory from the stale pre-swap quote. One financed call minted endogenous FOX and sold it back into the pair, depleting its liquid USDT reserve.

name: ULME arbitrary approved-user spending
summary: buyMiner(user, usdt) was public and passed its caller-supplied user directly to USDT.transferFrom without requiring user == msg.sender or another authorization. The attacker invoked it for 100 holders who had approved ULME, forcing their USDT through the ULME/USDT pair while sandwiching those trades.

name: EvoDeFi MasterChef updatePower raises power without settling rewardDebt
summary: MasterChef.updatePower(pid) is public and recomputes the caller's power from its stake and current NFT bonus without paying pending rewards or resetting rewardDebt, so the next claim pays the added power times the pool's entire accumulated reward per power. Attackers staked, raised their NFT bonus, called updatePower and claimed.

name: GROK token triggerable zero-slippage swapback
summary: GROK's _transfer sells the token contract's own accumulated GROK on Uniswap V2 with zero minimum output whenever a transfer to the pair finds that balance above a fixed threshold. The attacker topped the balance up by direct transfer, sandwiched the triggered sale inside flash loans, bought back cheaply and arbitraged the GROK against the V3 pool.

name: BH farm redeems LP from the pair's spot token balances
summary: The unverified BH farm held the protocol's BUSDT/BH LP and let anyone redeem it by burning BH, sizing the LP removed from the pair's live BUSDT and BH balances. The attacker flash-borrowed BUSDT, pushed it through the pair to cut its BH balance and raise its BUSDT balance, then redeemed ten times, each pulling about half the remaining LP.

name: MoonHacker vault unauthenticated Aave flash-loan callback
summary: MoonHacker.executeOperation, the Aave V3 flash-loan callback of each MoonHacker leverage vault, is declared external with no check that msg.sender is the Aave pool and no check that initiator is the vault, and it takes the money-market address out of the caller-supplied params blob. Any address can therefore call it directly: with SmartOperation.REDEEM and mToken set to the real Moonwell mUSDC market the vault repays its own borrow with USDC the caller pushed in and redeems its entire collateral, and with SmartOperation.SUPPLY and mToken set to an attacker contract whose mint() and borrow() return 0 the vault executes IERC20(token).approve(mToken, amountBorrowed + amountToSupplyOrReedem), handing the caller an allowance over the redeemed balance, which the caller then pulls with transferFrom.

name: Carson custom pair sell-side reserve burn
summary: The closed-source Carson/USDT pair, after each swap's k check, moved a factory-configured share of the input token out of its own reserve (30% to 0xdead, 30% to a fee wallet for Carson sells) and synced. The attacker bought Carson with flash-loaned USDT and sold it back in 51 chunks, each shrinking the Carson reserve, draining the pair's USDT.

name: bZx iToken self-transfer duplication
summary: LoanTokenLogic's _internalTransferFrom cached sender and receiver balances before writing them and never rejected _from == _to, so a self-transfer credited the receiver without debiting the sender. Attackers doubled their iUSDT, iUSDC, iDAI, iLINK and iETH balances with repeated self-transfers and burned them for the pools' underlying.

name: ParaSwap Augustus V6 uniswapV3SwapCallback approval drain
summary: AugustusV6.uniswapV3SwapCallback() skipped its pool-caller check when the callback data carried a multi-hop path and took the payer from that data. Anyone could call it directly, make the router swap through a genuine Uniswap V3 pool and pay the pool by transferFrom from any wallet that had approved the router, on every chain running V6.

name: dTRINITY dLEND empty cbBTC reserve liquidity-index inflation
summary: dLEND, an Aave v3 fork, listed cbBTC as flash-loanable collateral (LTV 73%) with no supply. The attacker left one scaled share in the empty reserve, donated cbBTC to the aToken and ran 150 flash loans whose premiums, spread over that single share, raised the cbBTC liquidity index from 1e27 to 6.2e33. At that index deposit/withdraw rounding let it keep aToken collateral while withdrawing its cbBTC, and two blocks later it borrowed the entire dUSD reserve against the phantom collateral.

name: Unnamed Base Compound fork slot0 spot price feeds and open whitelist
summary: The fork priced cSUI (and cMIGGLES) through adapters that read a thin Uniswap-V3-style pool's instantaneous slot0 with no TWAP or bounds, and its comptroller's __setWhitelist__ had no access control. The attacker whitelisted its contracts, pushed the uSUI pool price to the clamp with one swap, posted 50 uSUI as collateral and borrowed every market.

name: bZx Fulcrum margin trade skipped health check
summary: bZx's takeOrderFromiToken required (loanDataBytes empty && withdrawal == loan) || !shouldLiquidate(), so Kyber-routed margin loans never ran the health check. The attacker pumped WBTC on Uniswap V1 with WBTC borrowed from Compound, opened a 5x sETHwBTC short whose iETH-funded swap bought WBTC at the inflated price, and left the underwater loan.

name: BXH TokenStakingPoolDelegate pays USDT bonus at the live BXH/USDT spot quote
summary: BXH's TokenStakingPoolDelegate paid pending BXH rewards in USDT, converted at the BXH/USDT pair's live reserves and paid from its own USDT balance. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought BXH to inflate its USDT price, then harvested the small pending reward of an earlier vUSDT stake as about 40k USDT, draining the bonus balance.

name: APC TransSwap swaps inventory at the live APC/USDT spot quote
summary: The TransSwap proxy priced APC against MUSD from the APC/USDT PancakeSwap pair's live reserves and paid from its own inventory. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker pumped APC, swapped APC for MUSD at the inflated quote, dumped APC, swapped the MUSD back for more APC at the depressed quote and sold it.

name: KyberSwap Elastic tick-crossing double-liquidity
summary: In Elastic pool swaps, a crafted amount made the price land exactly on a tick boundary through rounding so the pool moved the price past the tick without crossing it, leaving base liquidity counted twice. After concentrating liquidity at that tick, the attacker swapped back against the doubled liquidity and drained pool reserves.

name: FH sell path burns the sold amount from the FH/USDT pair before the sale
summary: On a sale to the FH/USDT pair, FHToken._transfer burns 80% of the after-fee amount from the pair, moves 20% to the treasury and syncs before the sold tokens arrive. Buys need a whitelisted recipient, but a whitelisted PancakeSwap router's public sweepToken releases held tokens. An attacker looped flash-loaned buys to that router, sweeps and sells.

name: unverified_0x452E25 unauthenticated uniswapV3SwapCallback
