summary: The contract's uniswapV3SwapCallback() paid out the requested amount to msg.sender without verifying that the caller was a genuine Uniswap V3 pool, so a direct call with a fabricated delta and token address transferred 27.3 WETH out.

name: ShadowFi SDF unauthenticated burn(address,uint256)
summary: ShadowFi's SDF token declares burn(address account, uint256 _amount) public with no owner check, no allowance check and no msg.sender == account check; it simply calls _transferFrom(account, DEAD, _amount). The attacker deployed a one-shot contract that bought 0.010354936721195452 SDF from the PancakeSwap SDF/WBNB pair 0xf9e3151e813cd6729d52d9a0c3ee69f22cce650a with 0.001 WBNB, called SDF.burn(pair, 10354936721195451) to destroy the pair's entire SDF reserve except one wei, called pair.sync() so the reserves became 1 wei SDF against 1,078.615699417903036883 WBNB, and then swapped 8.461538283 SDF for 1,078.616699290110670619 WBNB before selfdestructing.

name: EST delayed sell-burn drained by skim loop
summary: ESTToken books every taxed transfer into the pair as a pending sell burn; the next non-pair transfer burns that amount, capped at 10% of the pair's EST, from the pair and syncs, even if the tokens were skimmed back out. The attacker looped transfer-to-pair and skim about 150 times, shrinking the pair's EST to dust, and sold EST for its WBNB.

name: LeverageUsingSiloFlashloanWithGeneralSwap unvalidated swap target
summary: openLeveragePosition() on the unreleased leverage helper accepted a caller-supplied flashloan target and swap calldata without constraining them to the selected Silo market, so a fake flash lender's onFlashLoan callback made the helper call the real WETH Silo's borrow() on behalf of a third party that had granted it debt-receive approval.

name: Vee Finance leveraged-trade swap without a valid price bound
summary: When a Vee lending market opens a leveraged position it hands control to the trading proxy 0xd1f855cef146d36cc5851e2139c54524420797f2, which resolves its execution venue with PangolinFactory.getPair(collateral, target) and then swaps the borrowed principal through PangolinRouter.swapExactTokensForTokens. The deployed code applies no liquidity floor to the pair it receives, no comparison against an independent price, and the amountOutMin it supplies is computed wrongly (Halborn attributes the miscalculation to dropped token decimals). In the anchor transaction it swaps 1.551393710318664115 WETH.e into a WETH.e/QI pair that the attacker had created 21 minutes earlier and seeded with 0.000003118379317223 WETH.e and 0.059871635214100967 QI, with amountOutMin set to 10649908 wei of QI, and accepts 0.059871514507227568 QI as the whole position. The attacker immediately bought the WETH.e back out of their own pair for the same dust, leaving Vee's market holding worthless collateral against the borrow. Repeating this 1,232 times emptied Vee's WETH.e and WBTC.e markets.

name: Makina DUSD manipulable Curve accounting instruction
summary: Makina approved a permissionless accounting instruction that valued the Caliber's Curve MIM/3CRV position with the pool's manipulable calc_withdraw_one_coin quote. A searcher flash-manipulated that pool, ran the instruction to inflate Caliber and Machine AUM, and the inflated DUSD rate let two cycles drain the DUSD/USDC Curve pool's USDC.

name: ChainSwap bridge receive() accepts self-signed signatories via auto quota
summary: ChainSwap's receive() only checked that each signature recovered to the signatory it named, then charged that signatory's quota. authQuotaOf() accrues quota from lasttimeUpdateQuotaOf, zero for a never-seen address, so any fresh key held a full auto quota. The attacker self-signed receives, releasing locked tokens on Ethereum and minting mapped tokens on BSC.

name: IPC sells burn the pair's balance
summary: The IPC token burns a pending destroyNum of IPC straight out of its PancakeSwap pair and calls sync() on every sell, and each sell adds half its size to destroyNum. Inside flash loans the attacker repeatedly flash-swapped IPC out of the pair and sold it back, so each round burned pair-held IPC and lifted the price, then sold into the inflated USDT reserve.

name: Rodeo Finance OracleTWAP samples an AMM spot price on a predictable schedule
summary: OracleTWAP priced unshETH as the plain mean of four spot samples of a thin Camelot pair, one taken per keeper update every 30 minutes. The attacker sandwiched three updates to inflate the samples, then opened leveraged unshETH positions whose oracle-based slippage and health checks let borrowed USDC buy the attacker's unshETH at the inflated price.

name: Punk Protocol pool re-initialization
summary: The three Punk CompoundModel pools exposed initialize() without access control or a one-time initialization guard. The extraction contract reinitialized each pool with itself as forge_, invested the pool's stablecoins into Compound, and called withdrawToForge() to redeem and sweep the funds.

name: RWC deferred sell burn removes pair RWC and syncs on demand
summary: RWC._transfer queues part of every sell as pendingPoolBurn, and the permissionless executePendingPoolBurn() later debits it from the PancakeSwap pair's own RWC balance and calls sync(), so the pool pays the burn. A flash-loan attacker looped buy, sell and burn to shrink the RWC reserve, ratchet the price and sell back for the pair's USDT.

name: Prisma MigrateTroveZap flash-loan callback injection
summary: MigrateTroveZap.onFlashLoan only checked that the debt token called it, not who initiated the flash loan or with what data. The attacker flash-borrowed mkUSD with the zap as receiver and data naming a victim trove whose owner had delegated to the zap, closing the trove and reopening it with less collateral, leaving the surplus in the zap to be taken.

name: BSC swap router unauthenticated uniswapV3SwapCallback pays any approver
summary: The router's uniswapV3SwapCallback (0xfa461e33) accepted calls from any msg.sender and ran transferFrom(payer, msg.sender, amount) with the payer taken from callback data, never checking for a factory pool or binding the payer to the swap initiator. A fake pool reached through the public swap entry 0x33411b5e pulled approvers' tokens.

name: Super Sushi Samurai stale-balance self-transfer inflation
summary: The token's custom _update() read the recipient balance before reducing the sender balance. When sender and recipient were equal, its final recipient write overwrote the reduction with the stale balance plus the transfer amount, so every self-transfer minted the transferred amount out of nothing. The first exercise, on 2024-03-17, was a self-transfer of an entire 272,222,222,222.22195 SSS balance whose minted duplicate was sold into the SSS/WETH pair two minutes later; from 2024-03-21 game players, a whitehat that emptied the pair, and two later actors who self-transferred the pair's own balance through skim() repeated it.

name: Seneca Chamber arbitrary-call approval drain
summary: Chamber's public performOperations exposed an OPERATION_CALL action with attacker-controlled target and calldata. Because users had standing token allowances to their Chamber, an attacker could make the Chamber call token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance) and drain approved wallet assets.

name: LW buyback trigger counted from a spot-balance price
summary: LW increments thanPrice for every sell worth over 2,500 USDT at a spot balance price, and its public receive() then spends 3,000 USDT of the market wallet on an LW buyback per unit. The attacker made repeated large sells with flash-loaned funds, sent 1 wei BNB to fire the buybacks into the pair, and sold LW into the USDT they added.

name: OSN LP dividend weights not reduced on LP transfer
summary: OSN's _transfer set LP-dividend weight only on router adds and on removals, where it took the recipient's full pair-token balance, while plain LP transfers never cut the sender's weight. LP passed through addresses that each made a dust add and remove was counted many times, and the attacker collected the tax-funded USDT dividends.

name: ATM transfer-triggered fee auto-swap manipulation
summary: ATM sold its own token inventory into the ATM/WBNB pair before each non-whitelisted transfer to the pair, sized by that transfer, with no threshold and zero minimum output. A flash-funded attacker repeatedly transferred ATM to the pair and skimmed it back, triggering dozens of protocol dumps, then unwound against the depleted pool.

name: EGD Finance claimAllReward prices rewards from live pair balances
summary: EGD_Finance.claimAllReward converts each stake's USDT reward quota into EGD at getEGDPrice(), the EGD/USDT pair's live USDT balance divided by its EGD balance. Inside a flash swap that emptied the pair's USDT, the attacker claimed the reward of an 18-block-old 100 USDT stake, received 99% of the contract's EGD and sold it.

name: NGP transfer hook drains the pair reserve and syncs
summary: On every sell the NGP token’s _update hook moves treasury and reward fees out of the PancakeSwap pair itself, with super._update(mainPair, treasuryAddress, ...) and super._update(mainPair, rewardPoolAddress, ...), and then calls IUniswapV2Pair(mainPair).sync(). Each sell therefore permanently shrinks the pair’s NGP reserve and raises the NGP price. The attacker repeated small sells behind a flash loan until the price was inflated, then sold a large NGP position and took almost the whole USDT reserve.

name: PearlDriver NLAMM unchecked buy() cost overflow
summary: NLAMM.buy(token,index,amount) computes the USDT cost amount * currentPrice inside an unchecked block and then mints amount * 1e18 craft tokens. Choosing amount so the product wraps bought up to 1e63 tokens of five resources for fractions of a cent, sold into their PearlDEX USDT pairs; two copycats repeated it before the fix.

name: LAXO_Token
summary: LAXO's sell hook burned the sold amount from its USDT pair and synced before the sale, and buys sent to the fee-excluded PancakeSwap router skipped the buyer quota. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker bought LAXO to the router, swept it out via a dust-pair removeLiquidity, then sold to burn the pair's LAXO and swapped out its USDT.

name: Unknown batch executor unauthenticated execute(actions)
summary: EOA 0x98289e90 deployed an unverified batch executor and gave it an unlimited yvWETH allowance. Its execute((address,uint256,bytes)[]) runs arbitrary calls for any caller. An attacker's constructor had it transferFrom the owner's entire 384.667 yvWETH balance to itself, withdraw the underlying from the Yearn vault, and send the 429.21 WETH to the attacker.

name: CoW Protocol solver SwapGuard unprotected call
summary: A solver's SwapGuard helper, to which GPv2Settlement had granted unlimited token allowances during settlements, exposed a permissionless envelope() that executes arbitrary caller-supplied calls; attackers called it to transferFrom the settlement contract's fee buffer to themselves.

name: VerusBridge duplicate-proof-root parser divergence
summary: NotarizationSerializer used the last Verus proof-root entry when duplicate system IDs were present, while Verus consensus kept the first. Two signed notarizations therefore installed and confirmed an attacker-chosen root that authorized a later unbacked import.

name: NblNftStake withdrawNft reentrancy
summary: NblNftStake.withdrawNft() returned the staked ERC-721 with safeTransferFrom before paying NBL and clearing the slot, despite inheriting a reentrancy guard that the function did not use. The receiver callback re-entered the same slot, so two nested withdrawals each paid its unchanged NBL amount and emptied the staking contract.

name: MetaPoint user contract unrestricted approve
summary: Each MetaPoint per-user contract exposes a public approve() that grants the caller an unlimited POT allowance, so an attacker can authorize itself and transferFrom the contract's entire POT balance.

name: BT.Finance Curve aave-pool strategies unbounded slippage
summary: BT.Finance's USDC and USDT Curve strategies entered and left the Curve aave pool with no slippage bound, and anyone could trigger vault deposit and earn. With flash-loaned funds the attacker unbalanced the pool, deposited so vault funds entered at the distorted rate, restored the pool and redeemed its shares, leaving the slippage on depositors.

name: CloberDEX Rebalancer burn reentrancy
summary: Rebalancer._burn computed a burner's share and called the pool strategy's burnHook before writing down the pool's reserves. The attacker opened a pool with its own token and itself as strategy, minted with flash-loaned WETH, and re-entered burn from the hook so the stale reserves paid out twice, taking WETH held for other pools.

name: Platypus MasterPlatypusV4 emergencyWithdraw solvency check
summary: MasterPlatypusV4.emergencyWithdraw() asked PlatypusTreasure for solvency before removing the staked LP collateral, so the check passed while the collateral was still counted. The attacker staked flash-loaned LP-USDC, borrowed the maximum USP against it, emergency-withdrew the collateral and swapped the unbacked USP for the pool's stablecoins.

name: Maestro Router 2 unvalidated external call
summary: Maestro Router 2 implementation 0x8eae9827 exposed function 0x9239127f, which made the router call a caller-chosen target with caller-chosen calldata and no authorization. The attacker had the router call transferFrom on tokens users had approved to it, moved their balances to its helper and sold them for ETH.

name: MOKE spot-price settlement and LP-dividend sybil claims
summary: MokeRelease.settle() let any EOA set settledMokePrice from AMM spot reserves; after dumping WBNB into WBNB/USDT the attacker settled a crashed price and claimed 43.86M MOKE on its quotas. Released MOKE could only go to handlers, so it was fed to MokeLPDividend and claimed back through 65 addresses whose LP records syncUserLP had duplicated.

name: FlooringPeriphery extMulticall arbitrary call
summary: Multicall.extMulticall() in the FlooringPeriphery implementation executed caller-supplied (target, callData) pairs from the periphery proxy with no access control. Users had approved the proxy for their NFTs and WETH, so the attacker made it call safeTransferFrom and transferFrom on approval holders and took their BAYC, Pudgy Penguins and WETH.

name: BetterBank FavorRouterWrapper unvalidated-pair ESTEEM bonus minting
summary: FavorRouterWrapper.swapExactTokensForFavorAndTrackBonus only checks that the path ends in a registered FAVOR token, so any token and pair qualifies, and FAVOR.logBuy credits an ESTEEM bonus on the amount bought. The attacker wash-traded FAVOR against a worthless token to farm ESTEEM, redeemed it for minted FAVOR and sold that into the official pairs.

name: Uranium Finance v2 pair k-check miscalculation
summary: The v2 UraniumPair.swap() scaled its balance adjustment by 10000 for the new fee but kept Uniswap's 1000**2 factor on the reserve side of the constant-product require, making the post-swap invariant check 100x too weak and letting the attacker take ~99% of each pair's reserves for a token dust input.

name: ARK public liquidity-pair burn and reserve collapse
summary: ARK exposed an unrestricted function that burned tokens held by its ARK/WBNB pair and synchronized the reduced reserve. The attacker repeated it 6,794 times, then swapped against the collapsed ARK reserve and withdrew the pair's WBNB.

name: LocalTrader price-manager missing access control
summary: The LocalTrader price-manager proxy left storeConstructor unprotected, so anyone could overwrite its feed, admin, owner and LCT price. The attacker took ownership, set the price to 1 wei, bought the exchange's whole LCT inventory for a negligible BNB payment and dumped it into the LCT/WBNB pool.

name: Palmswap PLP AUM ignores collateral bought as USDP
summary: Palmswap's PlpManager prices the PLP liquidity token off PlpManager.getAum(), which credits the whole of Vault.poolAmount() to PLP holders and deducts only permanentPoolAmount, aumDeduction and open-trader profit. It never deducts the vault's own Vault.usdpAmount() liability, so BUSDT deposited through Vault.buyUSDP by an account that is not the PlpManager raises the PLP redemption rate even though the depositor keeps a fully redeemable USDP claim on the same pool. With inManagerMode false, buyUSDP and sellUSDP were callable by anyone. The attacker flash-loaned 3,000,000 BUSDT, minted 996,324.456826157454206069 PLP at an AUM of 1,060,591.303897471446528544 USDP against a supply of 1,060,117.814431969258921599 PLP, then sent 2,000,000 BUSDT straight to the vault and called buyUSDP for itself, lifting AUM to 4,050,654.353532854041808248 USDP against 2,056,442.271258126713127668 PLP, and redeemed its PLP at the inflated 1.9697 rate before selling the USDP it had just bought back for BUSDT.

name: HB reward claim refills PROOF by pulling HB from the HB/USDT pair
summary: A PROOF reward claim makes HERMES.swapBack top PROOF up with up to 200,000 HB taken straight from the HB/USDT pair, then sync it. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought the pair down to 200,000 HB, claimed a reward so the refill took the rest, and sold dust HB into the near-empty reserve for the pair's USDT.

name: Zunami zETH and UZD permissionless rebase price latch on spot-valued rewards
summary: Zunami's elastic vaults (zETH, UZD) let anyone call cacheAssetPrice, which latches the pool's lpPrice whenever it rises; strategy holdings count donatable reward tokens at spot DEX prices. The attacker donated CRV (zETH) and SDT (UZD) to strategies, pumped their spot prices, cached the inflated price, and sold rebased tokens into Curve pools.

name: Nimbus fixed-APY staking rewards priced from spot swap feed
summary: Nimbus StakingRewardFixedAPY and LockStakingRewardFixedAPY convert NIMB-denominated accrued rewards into GNIMB with PriceFeeds.queryRate. On 2022-12-01 the owner rewired PriceFeeds' NIMB and GNIMB feeds from owner-set static NimbusPriceFeed contracts to PriceFeedSwap contracts that return the live NimbusRouter getAmountsOut spot quote. The attacker staked through three helper contracts, and 8.6 days later flash-borrowed about 75,477 BNB, bought NIMB in the NBU_WBNB/NIMB pair to raise the NIMB/GNIMB rate about 42,000-fold, and claimed rewards that emptied all three staking contracts.

name: APIG token business-logic flaw
summary: APIG's transfer accounting credits a self-transfer without preserving the sender debit. The attack helper doubled its APIG balance with 28 self-transfers, then spent the inflated balance into two PancakeSwap pairs and removed their USDT and BETH reserves.

name: ApeStaking NFT ownership accounting
summary: ApeStaking's deposit path could attribute an already-staked NFT position and caller-supplied stake amounts to a temporary NFT holder without receiving corresponding ApeCoin, allowing repeated withdrawApeCoin calls to drain APE and support cross-market borrowing.

name: Hyperdrive Router unrestricted CALL action abuses user operator approvals
summary: RouterUpgradeable's CALL action (kind 15) lets any caller make the Router call any AddressRegistry-listed contract with arbitrary calldata. Users approve the Router as market operator and token spender, so callers had it withdraw other users' collateral, borrow against their positions and transferFrom their approved balances.

name: Level Finance LevelReferralControllerV2 claimMultiple duplicate-epoch claimed overwrite
summary: LevelReferralControllerV2.claimMultiple() accepts duplicate epochs and sets claimed = reward instead of adding to it, so repeating an epoch alternates claimed between c and full-c and re-pays the reward every two iterations. The attacker earned referral points with self-referred swaps, claimed once, then repeated one epoch thousands of times per call.

name: DODO DVM re-callable init()
summary: DVM.init() had no initializer guard or access control. Inside a flashLoan callback an attacker called it again to repoint _BASE_TOKEN_ and _QUOTE_TOKEN_ at worthless tokens it controlled, so the repayment check measured the fake balances and passed while the real reserves left. A front-running bot, the attacker and copycats drained 13 DVM clones.

name: BNB48 private-tx MEV bot pancakeCall access control
summary: The bot's pancakeCall callback trusted any caller as a swap pair. The attacker's fake pair invoked it once per token, and the bot transferred its six-token inventory to the caller.

name: Inverse Finance YVCrv3CryptoFeed spot-balance LP valuation
summary: YVCrv3CryptoFeed priced Anchor's yvCurve-3Crypto collateral from tricrypto2's live token balances times Chainlink prices over LP supply. With flash-loaned WBTC the attacker minted the collateral, then swapped heavily through tricrypto2 to inflate the balance-sum price about 2.9x and borrowed DOLA against it, leaving the collateral behind.

name: xToken xSNXa and xBNTa unvalidated mint pricing
summary: xSNX.mint priced new xSNXa from the caller's own Kyber swap (TradeAccounting took weiPerOneSnx as ETH paid over SNX received), so a flash-loan-skewed SNX market let 0.125 ETH mint 1.28B xSNXa. xBNT.mint passed a caller-supplied Bancor path and credited its output as BNT, so paths ending in a junk token minted xBNTa. Both were sold into pools.

name: Paribus pETH redeem reentrancy
summary: PEther.redeemFresh sent ether to the redeemer before reducing its pETH balance and totalSupply, so the receive hook re-entered the comptroller and borrowed from other markets against pETH collateral that was being withdrawn. The attacker supplied ETH and USDT, borrowed, then redeemed and borrowed USDT and WBTC inside the callback.

name: Conic ETH omnipool Curve reentrancy guard skipped for WETH-listed pools
summary: CurveHandlerV3.reentrancyCheck only probed pools the registry cache lists with the 0xEeee ETH coin, but the Curve v2 rETH and cbETH pools list WETH while paying out native ETH. The attacker re-entered the ConicEthPool from a remove_liquidity ETH callback and ran handleDepeggedCurvePool and withdraw against mid-update Curve balances, draining depositors.

name: SOF sell hook burns the sold amount from the SOF/USDT pair before the sale
summary: SOF._update handles a sale to the SOF/USDT pair by moving 90% of the sold amount from the pair's own balance to DEAD and calling sync() before the seller's tokens arrive. Buys revert unless the recipient is fee-excluded, so the attacker bought 991,223 SOF with flash-loaned USDT for a fee-excluded mining contract, leaving 787.9 SOF in the pair, then sold 875.45 SOF: the hook burned the remaining 787.9 SOF from the pair, and the sale received all of the pair's USDT.

name: Paribus Camelot PNFT instantaneous-position oracle
summary: Paribus's Algebra V1 position oracle valued a Camelot liquidity NFT from the pool's instantaneous globalState price. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, pushed the thin PBX/USDT pool, minted a position, deposited it into the newly listed PNFT market, borrowed ETH, ARB, WBTC and USDT against the inflated valuation and unwound the swap.

name: Conic crvUSD omnipool mints and redeems against manipulable Curve LP marks
summary: ConicPoolV2 minted and redeemed shares at Curve LP marks computed from the pools' instantaneous balances, guarded only by a loose 2% imbalance bound, and traded its own Curve positions with no minimum out. The attacker skewed the crvUSD/USDC and crvUSD/USDT pools, had the omnipool deposit, swapped back and withdrew, four times per transaction.

name: PancakeBunny BUNNY minter spot LP valuation
summary: PriceCalculatorBSC.valueOfAsset() priced WBNB-paired Cake-LP from the pair's spot WBNB balance, and BunnyMinterV2.mintForV2() minted BUNNY in proportion to that value with no cap. Flash-loaned WBNB pumped into the BUNNY-WBNB pair made a tiny VaultFlipToFlip getReward() mint 8M BUNNY, which the attacker sold into both BUNNY/WBNB pairs.

name: TMM deferred sell burn drains the TMM/USDT pair
summary: While freeTrade is off, TMM accumulates waitBurnTokenAmount from buys and, on the next sell into the pair, transfers that amount from the TMM/USDT pair to 0xdead and calls sync(). The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought TMM to grow the pending burn beyond the pair's balance, triggered two pair burns that left a reserve of 1 TMM-wei, and sold a small amount of TMM for almost all of the pair's USDT.

name: thirdweb legacy Bridge approval misuse
summary: The legacy thirdweb Bridge implementation executed a caller-chosen forward call from the bridge's own context after 'collecting' a caller-chosen token. With a codeless fake token the collection was a no-op and the forward call was USDC.transferFrom(victim, attacker), spending wallets' standing approvals to the bridge.

name: SafeDollar reward pool deflationary-token accounting
summary: SdoRewardPool credited the nominal PLX deposit and returned that nominal amount even though PLX burned 0.15% on transfer. Repeated deposit/withdraw cycles depleted the pool's actual PLX balance to two wei; updatePool() divided newly accrued SDO by that balance, inflating accSdoPerShare and allowing a pre-positioned stake to mint unbacked SDO.

name: Yearn v1 yDAI loose Curve slippage configuration
summary: Yearn's controller selected StrategyDAI3pool for the v1 DAI vault while the strategy's slippage allowance was 1% and the vault's earn() function was permissionless. In each exploit round the attacker imbalanced Curve 3pool, deposited DAI into yDAI, called earn() so the strategy added that DAI near the configured minimum, restored the pool, and withdrew. Eleven transactions repeated the loss-making round trip before Yearn disabled further investment.

name: Gym Network LiquidityMigrationV2 migrate() flaw
summary: LiquidityMigrationV2.migrate removes the caller's GYM v1 LP and re-adds the received v1 token quantity as GYMNET from the migrator's own reserve, with zero slippage bounds and no value check. The attacker flash-loaned WBNB, skewed the v1 pool, minted and migrated LP so the migrator spent its GYMNET into new LP for the attacker, then removed it and sold.

name: Beanstalk GovernanceFacet emergencyCommit on unsnapshotted voting power
summary: GovernanceFacet.vote and emergencyCommit read voting power (Roots) at call time with no snapshot or holding period, so Silo deposits made in the same transaction count. The attacker flash-borrowed liquidity, deposited it, voted its own BIP to the two-thirds supermajority and emergency-committed it; the BIP's init delegatecall moved the Silo's assets out.

name: Bamboo AI spoofable sale activation and pair-burn drain
summary: BambooAI._transfer set sale = block.number on any addressDev-to-pair transfer, and transferFrom(addressDev, pair, 0) needed no allowance, so anyone could switch on updatePool. That moved 1% of every non-pair transfer amount out of the pair's BAMBOO balance and synced, so loops of self-transfers shrank the BAMBOO reserve and let attackers sell into it for the pair's WBNB.

name: XSURGE SurgeBNB sell() reentrancy
summary: SurgeToken.sell() sent BNB to the seller before updating the token supply and reserve, so the attacker's receive() hook re-entered purchase()/sell() repeatedly and drained the contract's BNB backing at a stale price.

name: CvxRewardDistributor claimMultipleStaking
summary: CvxRewardDistributor.claimMultipleStaking accepted caller-supplied staking contracts without checking them, minted CVG for whatever claimable amount they returned and paid out other reward tokens. The attacker passed its own contract, minted 58.7M CVG and dumped it into the CVG/WETH and CVG/crvFRAX Curve pools; a copycat later used the same call to take the distributor's reward tokens.

name: Shezmu permissionless collateral mint
summary: Shezmu's 18-decimal pseudo-WBTC collateral token exposed mint(address,uint256) without caller authorization. Attackers minted arbitrary collateral, deposited it into the ShezUSD and ShezETH vaults, borrowed unbacked ShezUSD/ShezETH and sold them into the Curve and Balancer pools.

name: vETH virtual-liquidity factory unbacked mint
summary: The vETH virtual-liquidity factory 0x62f250cf7021e1cf76c765dec8ec623fe173a1b5 exposed a permissionless addVirtualLiquidity(address,address,uint256,uint256) (selector 0x6c0472da) that called VirtualToken.takeLoan to mint up to the 300 ether per-block limit of unbacked vETH straight into a caller-named Uniswap V2 vETH/token pair, pulled only the matching amount of the counter token at the pair's live spot ratio, burned the resulting LP to address(0), and never called repayLoan. Because vETH is redeemable one-for-one for ETH through the whitelisted router, the caller could first push the pair's spot ratio with a flash loan so that 300 vETH required almost no counter token, then sell the counter token back and withdraw more ETH from VirtualToken than had been deposited. No parameter value fixes this: the loan is never repaid at any limit, so the deployed factory code mints an unbacked redeemable claim on every call.

name: Akropolis Delphi SavingsModule fake-token reentrancy
summary: SavingsModule.deposit accepted any token address and credited pool tokens from the protocol's balance change around the token's transferFrom, with no reentrancy guard. The attacker named its own contract as the token and re-entered deposit with real DAI from its transferFrom, so the DAI was counted twice; it redeemed the doubled pool tokens for DAI.

name: Cheese Bank LP oracle priced from spot pair reserves
summary: CheesePriceOracle valued the CHEESE/WETH Uniswap V2 LP token from the pair's spot WETH balance, without the TWAP its other assets used, and refresh() was permissionless. The attacker swapped flash-loaned ETH into the pair, refreshed the inflated LP price, and borrowed the USDC, USDT and DAI markets' cash against LP collateral.

name: FILX LinearVesting unguarded init
summary: The FILX LinearVesting implementation's init(token, periods, interval) has no initializer guard and sets owner to the caller, so it can be re-run after deployment. The attacker re-initialised the vesting proxy to become owner and used withdraw() to take all of its FILX, which it sold for USDT.

name: Predy Finance PredyPool lock settlement credits a supply() as repayment of take()
summary: PredyPool settles a trade lock by comparing raw ERC20 balances. TradeLogic.callTradeAfterCallback() runs GlobalDataLibrary.initializeLock(), which snapshots the pool's quote and base token balances, then hands control to the caller's predyTradeAfterCallback, then runs finalizeLock(), whose settle() computes paid = balanceOf(this) - snapshot. PredyPool.take() is guarded only by onlyByLocker and sends any amount to any address without recording a debt, and PredyPool.supply() is reachable from inside that callback because trade() carries no reentrancy guard. The attacker registered its own pair through the permissionless registerPair(), acquired the lock with a zero-size trade(), and inside the callback called take() for the pool's entire WETH and USDC balances and then supply() to put the same tokens back. settle() saw both balances restored and reported paid = 0, so the lock finalised and the empty vault passed PositionCalculator.checkSafe(), while supply() had minted the attacker supply tokens for the whole pool. Two withdraw() calls after the lock closed burned those supply tokens and removed everything. The violated invariant is that a locker's take() must be repaid with assets that create no offsetting claim; a balance delta cannot distinguish repayment from a new deposit that mints its own LP position.

name: LpdFi sizes an interest-bearing principal from the LPD spot pair price
summary: LpdFi.buy(uAmount) books an order's USD value from Lpd.price(), the LPD/USDC Pancake pair's spot reserve ratio, and pays 0.5% of it per day in USDC by removing protocol-owned LP. The attacker flash-pumped LPD, bought an order valued at a hugely inflated USD amount just before the daily rollover, dumped, and claimed a day's interest one block later.

name: DEI token burnFrom reversed allowance lookup
summary: DEI's burnFrom() read the caller's allowance to the account but wrote the decremented value as the account's allowance to the caller. After approving a holder, calling burnFrom(holder, 0) gave the caller an unlimited allowance over that holder's DEI; the attacker drained DEI pools, synced them and sold the DEI back for their stablecoins.

name: XCarnival XNFT withdrawn-collateral order reuse
summary: XNFT.withdrawNFT() returned a pledged NFT without closing or invalidating the pledge order, so getOrderDetail kept reporting the collateral and P2Controller.borrowAllowed kept approving borrows against it. The attacker pledged one BAYC, withdrew it, re-pledged it into a new order, and repeated the cycle to open 83 simultaneously borrowable orders backed by the same token.

name: Galaxy Fox claim contract unprotected setMerkleRoot
summary: The unverified GFOX claim contract's setMerkleRoot had no caller check. The attacker set a root equal to its own leaf, claimed nearly the whole GFOX balance with an empty proof and sold it into the GFOX/WETH Uniswap V2 pair; two other actors repeated the same calls on the remainder within two hours.

name: LavaLending UniV3Wrapper one-sided unclaimed-fee inflation
summary: LiquidityProviderBase._limitFees() caps a Uniswap V3 position's pending fees only when BOTH token fee amounts exceed their max-APR budget (`if (totalFees0 > max0 && totalFees1 > max1)`), so fees accrued in a single token are returned uncapped. UniV3Wrapper.getAssetsBasedOnPrice() adds those uncapped fees to the oracle-priced fair reserves, and Lava's WrapperOracle divides that sum by totalSupply to price the USDC/USDC.e wrapper LP token. The attacker minted a dust LP position, drove one-directional swaps through the 0x8e295789 USDC/USDC.e pool to accrue ~100k of token0-only fees against a 0.000999-share supply, and borrowed the Lava market out against the inflated collateral. The Chainlink-derived sqrtPriceX96 in WrapperOracle defends only the getAmountsForLiquidity() leg; the unclaimed-fee addend bypasses it entirely.

name: MEV bot 0x05f0 unprotected swap entry point
summary: The MEV bot contract exposed selector 0xf6ebebbb, an internal swap-execution entry point, with no caller check and no output validation. A flash-loan-funded attacker called it directly with pool and amount parameters of their own choosing and moved the contract’s whole USDC, USDT, WETH and WBTC balance out through the pools it was told to trade against.

name: LML pair-funded staking rewards claimed against a pumped pair
summary: LML.swapBack() refills the reward contract with LML taken out of the LML/USDT pair (then sync()), and staking sizes LML rewards at a stored price that ignores the live pair. The attacker pumped the pair by buying LML to 0xdead, claimed rewards for 11 pre-staked accounts until swapBack emptied the pair's LML, and sold LML back for the USDT.

name: Hinkal legacy-note nullifier double-spend
summary: Hinkal's legacy-note spend circuit, live through the verifier adapter registered in June 2026, did not bind a note's nullifier uniquely to its commitment. Changing private inputs while keeping the proved relation yields fresh nullifiers for the same note, so one shielded deposit can be spent repeatedly; the attacker double-spent small deposits and then a 25,000 USDC note.

name: WGPT sell hook burns treasury LP before crediting the deposit
summary: AiWGPTToken.transferFrom executes its treasury-funded LP removal and exact-output WGPT purchase before crediting the caller’s deposit to the pair. The hook updates pool reserves, then credits an unconsumed deposit that the caller can reclaim with skim. Repeated calls consume treasury LP and raise the WGPT price, allowing the caller to sell the retained tokens for USDT.

name: Siren MinterAmm withdrawCapital ERC1155 callback reentrancy
summary: MinterAmm.withdrawCapital burned LP and snapshotted the AMM's collateral, then sent the redeemer's ERC1155 option tokens before paying collateral and had no reentrancy guard. The attacker re-entered withdrawCapital from onERC1155Received, so nested withdrawals were priced against a stale collateral balance, draining six Siren Polygon AMMs.

name: Spectra Router arbitrary call
summary: The Router's KYBER_SWAP command forwarded caller-supplied calldata to a caller-chosen target with the Router as msg.sender and no check on target or selector. The attacker pointed it at tokens with transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance), pulling balances users had approved to the Router.

name: Layer3 USD live spot collateral valuation
summary: Loan.supply valued deposited collateral with PancakeSwap Router getAmountsOut, a live spot quote, and minted LUSD from it. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, pumped BTCB in the BTCB/USDT pair, supplied a little BTCB for inflated LUSD, and redeemed that LUSD for USDT at LUSDPool.withdraw.

name: PolyDEX PLX Locker (vMToken) claimUnlocked ERC777 reentrancy
summary: vMToken.claimUnlocked (the fPLX token locker) transfers the claimable PLX before increasing _released. PLX is an ERC777-style token that calls the recipient's tokensReceived hook, so an attacker contract re-entered unlockAll()/claimUnlocked 40 times per transaction and was paid the same vested amount repeatedly. Eleven transactions with growing lock sizes drained 59.6M net PLX from the locker, which the attacker sold for USDC and WETH.

name: TGBS public _burnBlock()
summary: A public state-changing token function allowed an arbitrary caller to reduce the TGBS balance held by its PancakeSwap pair, breaking the pair's reserve accounting and depleting its WBNB reserve.

name: DEPUSDT/LEVUSDC approveToken missing access control
summary: DEPUSDT and LEVUSDC inherit CurveSwap.approveToken, a public function that approves any token held by the contract to any spender. The attacker had each proxy approve its USDT or USDC to the attack contract and pulled the balances with transferFrom.

name: MetaDragon token-id transfer unrestricted minting
summary: P404Token treated any transfer value below 30,001 as an ERC-721 token ID. When the recipient was the token contract itself, _update skipped ERC-20 balance accounting, called the linked collection's burn without checking that the caller owned the NFT, and minted 9,800 MetaDragon tokens to msg.sender. The attacker repeated this over existing token IDs and sold the unbacked mint into the MetaDragon/WBNB pair in 12 transactions.

name: DFX Finance Curve flash() reentrancy
summary: DFX v2 Curve pools left flash() without the nonReentrant guard their other entry points had and checked repayment by balance, so the attacker re-entered deposit() from the flash callback, had the borrowed tokens count as both repayment and a new LP deposit, then withdrew the LP.

name: HYPR L1StandardBridge reinitialization
summary: HYPR's L1StandardBridge implementation wraps initialize() in a clearLegacySlot modifier that zeroes storage slot 0, which also holds Initializable's version, so reinitializer(2) passes on every call. The attacker reinitialized the bridge with its own contract as messenger and, as that messenger, finalized a withdrawal of the bridge's escrowed HYPR.

name: Dough ConnectorDeleverageParaswap unvalidated swap calls
summary: Dough's ConnectorDeleverageParaswap let anyone start its Aave flash-loan deleverage and executed caller-supplied swapData as arbitrary calls from the connector, which every Dough DSA trusts in executeAction. Attackers repaid a DSA's debt with the flash loan, then had the connector withdraw the DSA's Aave collateral and send it to them.

name: Exactly Protocol DebtManager unvalidated-market impersonation
summary: DebtManager accepted a caller-supplied market in its permit and leverage path without checking that the Auditor listed it. A malicious market bypassed the permit, set DebtManager's effective sender to a victim, then reentered crossDeleverage with a real market to withdraw the victim's position through an attacker-controlled swap pool.

name: SQUID migration self-sale uses manipulable minimum output
summary: SquidTokenSwap.sellSwappedTokens is public and derives its minimum output from the same PancakeSwap reserves its trade consumes. An attacker repeatedly trades around the SQUID v1-to-v2 conversion and these treasury-funded sales, controlling both legs of the spot quote and extracting WBNB. The nominal 5% slippage check has no independent price reference.

name: Reaper Farm ReaperVaultV2 redeem without owner authorisation
summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) and withdraw never checked that the caller was the owner or held its share allowance, so anyone could burn any depositor's vault shares and receive the underlying. Several parties, then the main attacker's contract, redeemed other holders' shares across Reaper's rfETH, rfUSDC, rfWFTM, rfBTC, rfDAI and rfUSDT vaults.

name: Rabby Wallet SwapRouter arbitrary-call allowance drain
summary: Rabby's swap router accepted caller-selected external-call targets and calldata, so the attacker made it call approved token contracts with transferFrom payloads and drain users' balances.

name: MEV bot 0xa47b unguarded callback
summary: The MEV bot's Balancer receiveFlashLoan callback did not check that the bot had started the loan and executed the swap route encoded in userData. The attacker flash-loaned 1 wei to the bot with a route that sent the bot's WETH through its own swap module into a Uniswap V3 swap paying the attacker, then through a fake pair.

name: GDS LP-mining reward paid on current LP balance
summary: GDS paid LP-mining rewards for every epoch since an account's lastEpoch in proportion to its LP balance at claim time. The attacker registered dozens of helper contracts holding dust LP, waited for the epoch to roll over, then passed flash-funded LP through each helper so every one claimed the full backlog, and sold the GDS into the pair.

name: Value DeFi vStake ProfitSharingRewardPool initializer never sets its initialized flag
summary: ProfitSharingRewardPool.initialize() is guarded by notInitialized but never sets initialized, so anyone could re-initialize the vStake proxy and become operator. The attacker did so with a dummy stake token, pulled the staked vBSWAP/BUSD LP via governanceRecoverUnsupported, re-initialized with the real LP and pulled the WBNB and BUSD rewards.

name: Pickle Finance ControllerV4 fake-jar swap
summary: ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar validated only approvedJarConverters for the call targets and never checked that _fromJar/_toJar were Pickle jars, so an attacker-deployed fake jar turned the controller into an arbitrary-call proxy that withdrew the real DAI strategy's cDAI.

name: Balancer V1 deflationary-token (STA/STONK) pool drain
summary: BPool credited swaps with the requested amountIn rather than the amount received and let anyone gulp() a token's recorded balance down to its real one. Repeated flash-loaned swaps of the 1%-burn token STA plus gulp drove the pool's STA balance to dust, so 1 wei of STA bought each of the pool's other tokens; the same was then done to a STONK pool.

name: Venus zkSync uncapped wUSDM ERC-4626 oracle
summary: Venus priced wUSDM with an ERC4626Oracle that read convertToAssets without bounding donation-driven appreciation. The attacker borrowed wUSDM against flash-loaned WETH, redeemed and donated the USDM to the wUSDM vault to raise its rate, then liquidated its own wUSDM debt from a second account, seizing the WETH collateral at the inflated valuation.

name: OCA SwapHelper sellOCA recycles the sold OCA out of the OCA/USDC pair
summary: The OCA SwapHelper's public sellOCA(amount) sells the caller's OCA into the OCA/USDC PancakeSwap pair with the USDC paid to the caller, then calls OCA.recycle to pull the same OCA amount back out of the pair and sync(), so every sale removes the pair's OCA without USDC coming back in. The attacker obtained OCA untaxed by flash-swapping it directly from the pair, which OCA's liquidity-removal heuristic exempts from its 100% buy tax, then repeated buy/sellOCA cycles to shrink the OCA reserve and sold its remaining OCA for the pair's USDC.

name: Goledo PPI collateral priced from Swappi spot reserves
summary: Goledo, an Aave V2 fork, accepted PPI as 65%-LTV collateral priced by a feed that multiplies Pyth CFX/USD by the live WCFX/PPI reserve ratio of a Swappi pair. The attacker flash-swapped WCFX, bought PPI to inflate that price, deposited the PPI and borrowed every other market's liquidity, then swapped the loot back to CFX.

name: Belt Finance beltBUSD Ellipsis LP mispricing
summary: StrategyEllipsisImpl.eps3ToWant() valued the strategy's 3EPS stake as its share of the raw sum of BUSD, USDC and USDT balances in the Ellipsis pool, a spot quantity any swap moves. beltBUSD minted and redeemed shares against that value, so cycling deposit, Ellipsis exchange and withdraw in one transaction drained BUSD from the Venus strategy.

name: Hundred Finance Gnosis ERC-677 transfer-hook reentrancy
summary: Hundred's Compound-fork CToken.borrow sends the underlying before recording the debt. On Gnosis the bridged USDC and WBTC are ERC677 tokens that call the recipient's onTokenTransfer, so the attacker re-entered from the hUSDC and hWBTC transfers and borrowed further markets while the comptroller still saw no debt, then left the collateral behind.

name: DAO Maker vesting unprotected init()
summary: The vesting implementations behind DAO Maker's EIP-1167 vesting clones let anyone call init() again, which made the caller the clone's owner. The attacker re-initialized six clones and used the owner-only emergencyExit() to sweep their vested sale tokens.

name: RADT DAO wrapper unauthenticated withdraw
summary: The RADT-DAO token (TWN) calls wrapper withdraw(from,to,amount) on every transfer, and the token's fallback lets the wrapper move any holder's balance. The wrapper, a proxy to implementation 0x9122191d7b2ccf11a2600de4eafd6b8cd3d03a62, never checks that withdraw's caller is the token. With cc (slot 0x1a) false, a direct call with to = the RADT/USDT pair and a pair USDT balance above reserve runs the pair-payout branch, which transfers RADT out of the pair to the named LP holder and fee recipients. The attacker stripped the pair's RADT, called sync() and sold RADT into the remaining USDT.

name: Opyn ETH put double exercise
summary: oToken.exercise(uint256,address[]) loops over the caller-supplied vault array and calls _exercise() once per vault, and _exercise() settles the ETH underlying leg with require(msg.value == amtUnderlyingToPay) against the same unchanged msg.value on every iteration while crediting vault.underlying to each vault. One ETH payment therefore exercised the put against several vaults, paying out each vault's USDC collateral, and removeUnderlying() then returned the single ETH payment from the attacker's own vault.

name: PerpPair liquidity-matrix rounding and unsafe cast
summary: PerpPair's LONG trade path updates the liquidity matrix with divCeil while other paths floor, so repeated trades drift it; getLpLiquidityBalance then casts a slightly negative int256 to uint256 unchecked, wrapping to a huge LP balance. With flash-loaned USDC the attacker added one-sided liquidity, traded, and realised the inflated PnL from the Vault.

name: LULA reward recycle confiscates and re-syncs the LULA/USDT pair reserve
summary: LULA.recycle() lets the rental contract move up to a third of the LULA/USDT pair's LULA to itself and sync() the pair, and the rental's claimTeamReward() calls it on every payout. The attacker bought the pair's LULA float into a fee-exempt address with flash-loaned USDT, ran 41 claims that took the pair's remaining LULA, and sold it back for the USDT.

name: CrossCurve ReceiverAxelar spoofed expressExecute
summary: ReceiverAxelar inherited Axelar's expressExecute, which runs _execute without gateway validation, and its peer check trusted the caller-supplied sourceChain and sourceAddress. With the Receiver threshold for the Berachain route lowered to one, a forged receiveData payload executed directly and made PortalV2 unlock its tokens to the caller.

name: Olympus BondFixedExpiryTeller unvalidated bond redemption
summary: BondFixedExpiryTeller.redeem() trusted the caller-supplied bond token's underlying and expiry values without verifying that the token was created by the teller. The attacker supplied a forged bond token, burned its arbitrary balance, and made the teller transfer its real OHM reserves.

name: 0VIX VGHSTOracle donatable vault share price
summary: VGHSTOracle priced vGHST as the GHST feed times vGHST's convertVGHST rate, the vault's GHST over its supply, which a bare GHST transfer raises; 0VIX listed ovGHST as borrowable with it. The attacker borrowed vGHST and other assets against flash-loaned stablecoins, donated GHST to inflate its vGHST debt, and liquidated itself to seize the collateral.

name: MARA sale proxy mints referral rewards into the LP pair
summary: The MARA sale proxy's payable buy entry point (selector 0x5fc985ea) mints MARA referral rewards to caller-supplied referrer addresses. The attacker bought with flash-loaned BNB naming the MARA/WBNB PancakeSwap pair as both referrers, so unsynced MARA landed in the pair, then swapped that surplus for the pair's WBNB.

name: KiloEx MinimalForwarder unguarded execute
summary: KiloEx's price feed accepted price updates relayed by its trusted forwarder, whose execute() relayed any request signed by its own sender, so anyone could set oracle prices. The attacker opened a position, pushed crafted prices through the forwarder and closed against the vault on BSC, opBNB, Base and Taiko, and pulled the BSC forwarder's own USDT.

name: Popsicle Finance Sorbetto reward-accounting exploit
summary: SorbettoFragola vaults transferred LP shares without settling or moving the per-account fee accounting, so a recipient was credited with fees accrued before it held the shares. With flash-loaned deposits the attacker passed the same shares through helper contracts, each collecting the full historical fees, then withdrew, across eight vaults.

name: Quixotic ExchangeV4 missing buyer authorization
summary: ExchangeV4.fillSellOrder validates only the seller signature, then pulls ERC-20 payment from the caller-supplied buyer without buyer authorization. The attacker signed sales of a fake ERC-1155 token and named allowance-holding wallets as buyers, draining OP and WETH.

name: Market.xyz transient Curve LP collateral price
summary: The miMATIC market accepted a Curve/Beefy LP collateral value read while the Curve pool was inside remove_liquidity, allowing loans against a transiently inflated virtual price.

name: SIR vault uniswapV3SwapCallback caller check on stale transient storage
summary: The SIR vault authorised uniswapV3SwapCallback by checking msg.sender against an address held in transient storage, and mint later reused that slot for the minted amount. The attacker minted an amount equal to a vanity CREATE2 address via its own pool, then called the callback from that address to transfer out the vault's USDC, WBTC and WETH.

name: SpankChain LedgerChannel reentrancy
summary: LCOpenTimeout refunded the channel's ETH deposit and then called the channel's token, which the opener chooses, before deleting the channel. The attacker opened a channel with its own contract as token, whose transfer re-entered LCOpenTimeout to refund the same deposit repeatedly.

name: RareStakingV1 universal Merkle-root update
summary: RareStakingV1.updateMerkleRoot() attempted to restrict callers with require(msg.sender != owner() || msg.sender != 0xc2F394a45e994bc81EfF678bDE9172e10f7c8ddc). Because the owner and fixed address were distinct, at least one inequality was true for every possible caller, making Merkle-root replacement permissionless. The attacker deployed a helper, set the root to keccak256(abi.encodePacked(helper, the staking proxy's full RARE balance)), and called claim() with that amount and an empty proof in the same transaction, draining the proxy.

name: WiseLending empty-market donation/rounding inflation (second incident)
summary: The attacker reduced the PLP-stETH-Dec2025 lending market to a tiny share base, donated pool tokens, and repeatedly exercised asymmetric deposit/withdraw rounding to inflate the collateral value of a second position, which then borrowed assets from five other WiseLending markets.

name: RWAVault ERC-4626 withdraw override without allowance spend
summary: RWAVault.withdraw(uint256,address,address) overrides OpenZeppelin's ERC4626.withdraw and bypasses ERC4626._withdraw, which is the only place the base implementation performs 'if (caller != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares)'. The override reads _depositInfos[owner], computes the share and principal reductions, and then calls _burn(owner, shares) and SafeERC20.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets) with no check that msg.sender is the owner or holds an ERC-20 allowance from the owner. Any external caller can therefore name an arbitrary owner and an arbitrary receiver and take that depositor's position out of the vault. The invariant broken is that an ERC-4626 vault may only move a share owner's assets on the owner's own authority or against an allowance the owner granted. No parameter restores the check: the allowance spend is absent from the compiled code, and the phase and withdrawalStartTime gates that the override does enforce were satisfied by the vault's normal Matured state. RWAVault.redeem has the same omission.

name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain
summary: Aperture's closed-source router executed a caller-supplied call target and calldata from its swap path without validation, so anyone could make it call ERC-20 transferFrom() or the Uniswap V3 position manager against the token and position approvals users had granted it, moving those assets to themselves.

name: Nomad Bridge Replica zero-root message acceptance
summary: The June 2022 Replica upgrade made unproven messages map to the zero root, which initialisation had marked confirmed, so process() accepted any message without a proof. The first exploiter withdrew from the BridgeRouter with an unproven message; hundreds of copycats then replayed the same transaction with their own recipients across the Replicas.

name: LBP addLp hashrate credit from flash-inflated pair reserves
summary: LBP credited add-liquidity hashrate from live pair reserves within the same transaction and allowed the pair itself as recipient. The attacker flash-inflated the LBP/USDT pair's USDT reserve and added liquidity so the pair got a huge credit; the auto-harvest minted unbacked LBP into the pair, which the attacker swapped out for its USDT.

name: Sperax USDs non-rebasing migration reinterprets credits as tokens
summary: The USDs implementation keeps two balance representations: rebasing accounts store scaled credits in _creditBalances and divide by rebasingCreditsPerToken, while non-rebasing (contract) accounts are flagged by nonRebasingCreditsPerToken[account] = 1 and have _creditBalances read back as plain token units. The lazy migration that _isNonRebasingAccount() runs the first time a transfer touches an unclassified contract account sets that flag without rescaling the account's stored credit balance, so a balance accumulated while the address was still an EOA is reinterpreted at a factor of rebasingCreditsPerToken/1e18. The attacker sent 11 USDs to a counterfactual Gnosis Safe address, deployed the Safe, and let the first transferFrom() out of it trigger the migration: with rebasingCreditsPerToken = 890714019687982181365620786, the Safe's 11 USDs became 9,797,854,205.567804 USDs of spendable balance, which was then sold into Arbitrum liquidity.

name: CUT valuePreservationByRemoveLP pays compensation at the live PancakeSwap spot price
summary: On LP removal CUT credits the remover extra CUT so the position keeps the USDT value recorded when it was added; its deal-type logic contract computes both values from the USDT/CUT pair's spot reserves. The attacker pumped CUT, added liquidity, dumped CUT, then removed the liquidity for a large CUT credit and sold it for the pair's USDT.

name: Morpho Blue PAXG/USDC oracle decimal misconfiguration
summary: The PAXG/USDC market selected a MorphoChainlinkOracleV2 deployed with both token-decimal constructor arguments set to 8, although PAXG has 18 decimals and USDC has 6. Its scale factor was therefore 1e12 too large. The attacker supplied 0.132577813003136114 PAXG as vastly overvalued collateral and borrowed 230,002.486670 USDC without repayment.

name: StoneVault instant withdrawal pays uncapped strategy proceeds
summary: StoneVault.instantWithdraw paid the withdrawer whatever StrategyController.forceWithdraw returned, not the burned shares' value, and the Balancer/Aura rETH strategy exited more WETH than asked. The attacker flash-borrowed 8,600 ETH, deposited, called the permissionless rollToNextRound to push it into the strategies, and instant-withdrew more than it put in.

name: Qubit Finance (QBridge)
summary: Ethereum QBridgeHandler accepted the zero address as an ERC-20 resource: its low-level transferFrom call returned success without moving tokens, yet the bridge emitted a Deposit event. Relayers then minted unbacked qXETH on BSC, which the attacker used to borrow the lending markets' assets.

name: ZZF burnToHolder pays BNB at a live spot quote
summary: ZZF.burnToHolder prices the ZongZi a user burns with uniswapRouter.getAmountsOut against WBNB and has the ZongZi token pay that many BNB from its reward pool into ZZF, from which receiveRewards pays the burner. After flash-loan buys pumped the WBNB/ZongZi pair, the attacker burned ZongZi at the inflated spot quote and withdrew nearly all of the pool's BNB in two transactions.

name: BunniHubLogic withdrawal rounding reserve depletion
summary: BunniHubLogic.withdraw() rounded the pool's idle-balance update in the withdrawer's favour. Dozens of tiny withdrawals burned negligible shares but shrank the pool's accounted active balance, so swaps priced against the distorted balances and later withdrawals took far more reserves than the burned shares were worth.

name: NeverFall sell() redeems protocol liquidity pro rata to the pair's spot NF balance
summary: NeverFall.sell(amount) removes amount * pairTotalSupply / balanceOf(pair) of the protocol-owned USDT/NF liquidity and pays the seller a share of the USDT. After flash-loaned USDT bought most of the NF out of the pair, the pair's NF balance was tiny, so selling NF removed almost all protocol liquidity and paid the attacker far more USDT than the NF was worth.

name: Unknown Arbitrum LP manager public withdraw swaps user positions with no minimum output
summary: Two byte-identical, unverified Uniswap V3 WETH/USDC position managers, 0x09c12514 and 0x3b329559, expose withdraw(address user, uint128 liquidity) (0x08fab167) to any caller. It removes and collects the user's position, sells all WETH for USDC via SwapRouter exactInputSingle with amountOutMinimum 0 and no price limit, and sends the USDC to the user. The attacker flash-borrowed 20,000 WETH from Aave and sold 7,825 WETH into the 0.05% pool. It then called withdraw for all 11 open positions in both managers, so the positions' WETH was sold at the depressed price. Finally it swapped back and kept 71.54 WETH.

name: TheDAO splitDAO recursive-call drain
summary: TheDAO.splitDAO(uint256,address) moved the caller's proportional ether to the child DAO with createTokenProxy.value(fundsToBeMoved) and then called withdrawRewardFor(msg.sender) before zeroing balances[msg.sender], totalSupply and paidOut[msg.sender]. withdrawRewardFor forwards nearly all remaining gas through ManagedAccount.payOut(address,uint256), which performs a value-bearing call to the token holder, so the attacker's fallback re-entered splitDAO while its own DAO-token balance was still intact and fundsToBeMoved was recomputed from the same unburned balance on every recursion. The violated invariant is that a split must pay out a token holder's share at most once per token lot; the deployed code performed the external interaction before the state update that enforces it.

name: Numa donation-manipulable vault price used as lending oracle
summary: NumaVault prices NUMA from its raw rETH balanceOf divided by circulating supply, and NumaPriceOracleNew feeds that spot price to the Numa lending comptroller for both collateral and debt. Within one flash-loaned transaction the attacker built a looped NUMA short against rETH collateral, sold the borrowed NUMA into the vault, donated 150 rETH to the vault to lift the oracle NUMA debt price from 116.94e12 to 161.23e12 wei, then liquidated its own position 26 times to recover its collateral and borrowed rETH against its remaining cNUMA, draining the vault.

name: Furucombo Proxy delegatecall context hijack
summary: Furucombo's Proxy delegatecalled any address its registry marked valid, and the registry also listed Aave V2's LendingPool proxy as a flash-loan caller. The attacker delegatecalled that proxy's initialize() in Furucombo's context, writing its own implementation into Furucombo's EIP-1967 slot, then used it to pull tokens users had approved to Furucombo.

name: EGA pond _openAPond unbounded buyback percentage
summary: The EGA deposit pond's payable _openAPond(uint256,uint256) swaps percent/100 of its BNB into EGA with amountOutMin 1 and never caps the caller's percent. After a flash-loan buy of EGA, the attacker called it with 1 wei and a percent of 100 times the pond's balance, so the pond spent all its BNB at the inflated price; the attacker then sold back.

name: OLPC pair-side burn multiplier collapses the OLPC/LABUBU reserve
summary: OLPCToken._update() sends every pair-to-user transfer down a branch that burns value * decimalsValue from the pair and then delivers value = 0 to the recipient. decimalsValue is an unbounded owner parameter that was raised from 1 to 7326680472586200649 on 2026-05-05, so any unprivileged caller could make the pair destroy 7.3e18 times the moved amount of its own OLPC. The attacker sent dust to the OLPC/LABUBU PancakePair and called skim() twenty times, collapsing the pair's OLPC balance from 51928294.25 to about 0.375, then pre-funded the pair with 8.1 OLPC and ran a Pancake supporting-fee swap with amountIn = 0, which prices that 8.1 OLPC against the collapsed reserve and released 688380.90 LABUBU.

name: Orion ExchangeWithOrionPool depositAsset reentrancy
summary: Exchange.depositAsset() carries no reentrancy guard and credits the caller with the exchange's own token balance delta, while swapThroughOrionPool() settles a caller-supplied token path by crediting the balance delta of the path's output token. The attacker put a fake ERC-20 in the middle of the path whose transfer hook re-entered depositAsset() with flash-loaned USDT, so the same 2.84M USDT was credited twice and withdrawn once.

name: Team Finance arbitrary-pair migration drain
summary: LockToken.migrate() authorized the caller using one lock ID but accepted a separate caller-supplied Uniswap V2 pair and liquidity amount. The attacker used locks for a worthless self-made token to migrate other users' locked LP balances into attacker-controlled Uniswap V3 positions.

name: BNO pool stale NFT reward accounting
summary: The BNO staking pool's emergencyWithdraw returned the stake and zeroed reward debt but left the user's NFT reward addition and the pool totals intact. The attacker looped stakeNft, pledge, emergencyWithdraw and unstakeNft with flash-swapped BNO, collecting unbacked rewards each round until the pool was empty, then sold the BNO.

name: Sovryn loan-closing cross-contract reentrancy into iToken mint
summary: Sovryn's LoanClosingsWith protocol module reduced the lender pool's principalTotal in _settleInterest before pulling the repayment (an rUSDT ERC777 transferFrom that calls the payer's tokensToSend hook) or refunding native RBTC to the borrower. From those callbacks the attacker minted iUSDT or iRBTC while the pool's totalAssetSupply omitted the repaid principal, i.e. at a depressed tokenPrice, then burned the iTokens at the corrected price once the close finished. Repeated with flash-swapped collateral, this drained the iUSDT and iRBTC lending pools.

name: FFIST predictable airdrop balance overwrite
summary: FFIST._airdrop sets the balance of addresses derived from lastAirdropAddress, block number, sender, recipient and amount to one raw unit, overwriting whatever they held. A zero-value transfer to a crafted recipient made the derived address the USDT pair; after sync, a tiny FFIST sale drained the pair's USDT.

name: Elephant Money Reserve TRUNK mint/redeem spot-price valuation
summary: The Elephant Money Reserve priced TRUNK mint and redeem from live PancakeSwap ELEPHANT/WBNB and WBNB/BUSD reserves in the same transaction. With flash-loaned BNB and BUSD the attacker pumped ELEPHANT, minted TRUNK, dumped ELEPHANT, then redeemed the TRUNK so the Reserve paid out a multiple of the ELEPHANT pool from its treasury.

name: TLN Protocol spot-reserve reward and collateral manipulation
summary: TLNProtocolStaking priced staked VOW/vUSD LP from live reserves of that pool and the thin VOW/USDT pair, and TlnSwap.lock sized VOW collateral from the same live reserves. A flash-loaned VOW buy let the attacker stake a little LP for millions of TLN, lock it for vUSD against negligible VOW, and sell the vUSD through VOW for USDT.

name: UwU Lend sUSDe price provider spot-median manipulation
summary: sUSDePriceProviderBUniCatch.getPrice() takes the median of eleven USDe price observations, but five of them are instantaneous Curve spot quotes read through get_p(0) on five hard-coded pools (FRAX, USDC, DAI, crvUSD, GHO), alongside five price_oracle(0) EMAs and one Uniswap V3 TWAP. Because a single transaction can move all five get_p inputs at once, the sorted median is pushed to whichever end of the honest cluster the attacker chooses; the code applies no deviation, staleness or spot-versus-EMA sanity check before scaling the median by sUSDeScalingFactor and returning it as the sUSDe price. All five pool addresses are compile-time constants, so no parameter value makes the deployed logic sound. Flash-loaned swaps across those pools drove UwU's reported sUSDe price from 1.03040982 to 0.98821237 and then to 1.03183659 inside the anchor transaction while the five EMA inputs stayed byte-identical, and the attacker converted that mispricing into deposits, borrows and self-liquidations that emptied every UwU reserve.

name: Aurellion diamond uninitialized initialize takeover
summary: The owner's diamondCut registered the SafeOwnable facet's initialize(address) selector without invoking any initializer, leaving the OpenZeppelin guard slot at zero on a diamond whose ownership had never written it. The attacker called initialize() to seize ownership, cut in a malicious facet exposing pullERC20, and swept outstanding user USDC approvals via transferFrom.

name: BonqDAO TellorPriceFeed accepts the latest Tellor report unvalidated
summary: BonqDAO's TellorPriceFeed.price() returned Tellor's latest wALBT report via getCurrentValue(), with no dispute delay, staleness or deviation check, although anyone staking 10 TRB can report. The attacker reported a huge wALBT price and minted 100M BEUR against 0.1 wALBT, then reported a near-zero price and liquidated 33 other wALBT troves.

name: Rikkei Finance SimplePriceOracle setOracleData access control
summary: SimplePriceOracle 0xd55f01b4b51b7f48912cd8ca3cdd8070a1a9dba5, the price oracle of the Rikkei Finance Cointroller, declares `function setOracleData(address rToken, oracleChainlink _oracle) external { oracleData[rToken] = _oracle; }` with no owner, admin, or any other caller restriction, so any address can repoint any market's feed. getUnderlyingPrice then reads decimals() and latestRoundData() straight from whatever contract that mapping holds. The attacker deposited 0.0001 BNB into rBNB, called setOracleData(rBNB, ownContract) to make the rBNB feed return 4.16881147930e32 with 18 decimals instead of the Chainlink BNB/USD 416.24753868 with 8 decimals, and borrowed the entire cash of the rUSDC, rBTC, rDAI, rUSDT and rBUSD markets against the resulting 2.918e28 account liquidity, then restored the original feed. A second transaction in the same block repeated the pattern in the opposite direction, repointing the rBNB feed at a second attacker contract so that BNB was priced low enough to borrow the whole rBNB market against a dust rBUSD deposit.

name: iVest donation-on-burn double debit
summary: Transfers to the zero address trigger the token's _MakeDonation path, which debits the sender's balance a second time; repeatedly sending iVest to the PancakeSwap pair and calling skim/sync shrank the pair's token reserve and let the attacker swap the reserve out for WBNB.

name: DLMC live-reserve sell pricing
summary: DLMCToken priced buys and sells from its live USDT reserve, so linked buys could transiently raise the price used by a subsequent sell and remove more USDT than the buys supplied.

name: Raft InterestRatePositionManager collateral-index inflation with round-up share mint
summary: InterestRatePositionManager.liquidate() closes the liquidated position and then calls _updateDebtAndCollateralIndex, which resets the raft collateral token index to collateralToken.balanceOf(address(this)) divided by the remaining share supply. The attacker donated 6,001.45 flash-loaned cbETH to the manager and liquidated the only other cbETH position, leaving 89 shares backing 6,003.44 cbETH, so the stored index became 6.745e19 wei of cbETH per share. ERC20Indexable.mint then mints amount.divUp(storedIndex) shares, so each subsequent 1-wei managePosition collateral deposit rounded up to a full share worth 67.45 cbETH. Repeating the 1-wei deposit inside the same transaction inflated the attacker position's collateral claim far past the manager's real cbETH holdings and let it borrow 6,705,028.47 R against it.

name: Eleven Finance NeverSellVault share-burn omission
summary: ElevenNeverSellVault.emergencyBurn() paid out the caller's underlying LP for their share balance without burning the shares. The attacker deposited flash-loan-funded LP, recovered it with emergencyBurn(), then redeemed the same shares again with withdrawAll(), taking an equal amount from other depositors; copycats repeated this on sibling vaults.

name: ChainSwap TokenMapped public sendFrom
summary: ChainSwap's TokenMapped bridge exposed sendFrom(from,toChainId,to,volume) publicly with no check that the caller was from or approved by it, so anyone could move tokens users had approved to the bridge into a cross-chain send to themselves; the attacker did so on ten token bridges and claimed the sends with receive.

name: ORBCore refund-before-sell reentrancy with pair-reserve burnLP
summary: ORBToken forwards BNB it receives to ORBCore.addPoolAndSell, whose sell branch refunds the BNB to the caller before selling, and _sellToken pays the caller before calling ORBToken.burnLP, which burns up to 20% of the pair's ORB and syncs; none of this is reentrancy-guarded and Core's own swaps are tax-free. With flash-loaned and Venus-borrowed WBNB the attacker first bought almost all ORB out of the ORB/WBNB pair, then re-entered at the refunds so that 58 nested sells ran their burnLP calls against the emptied reserve on the way out, grinding its ORB side to dust, and a final sell drained the pair's WBNB.

name: Impermax V3 permissionless reinvest collateral-value destruction
summary: TokenizedUniswapV3Position.reinvest is permissionless and mints collected fees back as liquidity at the pool's unchecked spot price, while Impermax values positions at an oracle price. The attacker wash-traded fees into its own position, borrowed against them, skewed the pool, reinvested to destroy the value and wrote the debt down via restructureBadDebt.

name: AFX liquidity intermediary sweeps its swap helper's whole AFX balance and matches it from a funding wallet
summary: Function 0xb1a87f2c of intermediary 0x560d3973 swapped the caller's USDT to AFX into helper 0x671ce4, then took the helper's entire AFX balance instead of the swap output, refunded it to the caller and matched it with AFX and AHT pulled from funding wallet 0x146933f2 into the AFX/AHT pair. Donating AFX to the helper around a pool manipulation drained the wallet.

name: Cream Finance yUSD price-per-share collateral inflation
summary: Cream's PriceOracleProxy priced Yearn-vault collateral as underlying price times the vault's live pricePerShare, with no bound or time average. The attacker built a huge crYUSD position, then transferred yCRV straight into the yUSD vault, doubling pricePerShare and the oracle's crYUSD price, and borrowed every market against the phantom collateral.

name: TMX Tribe Router-minted USDG inflates TLP AUM
summary: TMX, a GMX-v1 fork on Arbitrum, made its public Router a manager of the Vault, so any user could mint USDG through Router.swap([token, USDG]). GlpManager prices TLP as pool AUM divided by TLP supply and does not subtract USDG minted outside GlpManager, so each such mint raised the TLP redemption price while the minted USDG stayed redeemable 1:1. The attacker looped mintAndStakeGlp, a Router USDG mint, unstakeAndRedeemGlp at the inflated price and sellUSDG, draining the Vault's USDT0, WBTC, WETH, wSOL and USDC.

name: Unverified USDC/WETH liquidity pool credits nested reentrant liquidity additions against one payment
summary: Unverified pool 0x39ed372f8e9f316029994ca7f73b6683829c6b08 records liquidity and tick reserves in function 0xbe16634e before settlement, then calls back msg.sender without a reentrancy guard and checks payment per call. The attacker re-entered the add path 20 levels deep from the callback, paid once in the deepest frame to satisfy every nested balance check, and then removed the inflated liquidity, taking the pool's entire 7,167.42 USDC and 2.05 WETH.

name: Gamma Strategies Clearing single-sided ratio-check bypass
summary: Gamma's Clearing deposit gate skips its ratio check whenever a vault's holdings are single-sided, and the vaults' per-vault TWAP threshold of 200 let spot drift far from TWAP. With flash loans the attacker pushed each pool out of the vault's range, deposited at any ratio for shares priced at the manipulated spot, restored the price and redeemed.

name: SwapNet Router arbitrary call
summary: The closed-source SwapNet Router's swap entrypoint (selector 0x87395540) performed a low-level call to a caller-supplied target with caller-supplied calldata and no target validation, so passing a token address made the router itself execute transferFrom() against users' standing infinite approvals.

name: WiseLending empty-pool share inflation through a direct WBTC donation
summary: MainHelper._cleanUp, run through the syncPool modifier on every WiseLending entry point, compares IERC20.balanceOf(address(this)) against totalPool plus totalBareToken and credits any surplus to both totalPool and pseudoTotalPool without minting shares, so an unsolicited token transfer is booked as pool income for existing shareholders. MainHelper.calculateLendingShares additionally returns the raw amount when totalDepositShares is at most 1, so the first deposit into an empty pool mints one share per wei. Two one-wei WBTC depositExactAmount calls left the WBTC pool with two shares and a pseudoTotalPool of two, a direct transfer of 49.99999998 WBTC then made _cleanUp value each of those shares at about 25 WBTC, and the inflated collateral let borrowExactAmount take every other asset the protocol held before the flash loan was repaid out of a geometric sequence of WBTC withdrawals.

name: landNFT permissionless whitelisted minter
summary: The NFT owner whitelisted a helper whose public batch mint forwards arbitrary recipients and quantities without caller authorization. An unrelated caller minted 876 NFTs in five transactions and redeemed 143 for 28,600 XQJ.

name: HopeLend empty-market liquidity index inflation
summary: HopeLend, an Aave V3 fork, listed WBTC as collateral with an empty hEthWBTC market. The exploiter deposited a little WBTC, pumped the liquidity index with repeated flash loans whose premium accrues to the few suppliers, borrowed every other reserve against the inflated balance, and withdrew its WBTC through rayDiv rounding that burns fewer shares than owed.

name: RICE BentoBox-fork vault unauthenticated setMasterContractApproval
summary: The unverified BentoBoxV1-fork vault 0xcfe0de4a's setMasterContractApproval(user, masterContract, approved, v, r, s) performs no authorization: it ignores v, r, s and msg.sender, requires only masterContract != 0, and writes masterContractApproved[masterContract][user]. The attacker contract called registerProtocol() to become its own master contract, approved itself for depositor 0x49876a20 with a zero signature, and withdrew that depositor's entire 22,189,176.5 RICE vault balance through the allowed(from) check.

name: Kame Aggregator AggregationRouter arbitrary executor call
summary: AggregationRouter.swap forwarded caller-chosen calldata to a caller-chosen executor without validation. Attackers set the executor to an ERC-20 and the calldata to transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount), so the router spent the approvals users had given it; the attacker, copycats and white hats drained approvers of both Kame routers.
unverified: no RPC serves eip155:1329 history; facts carried from the v2 record
no RPC for eip155:1329; set RPC_URL_FOR_CHAIN_1329

name: bEarn BUSD/ibBUSD withdrawal-unit mismatch
summary: The BUSD Alpaca strategy's withdraw(address,uint256) passed a BUSD-denominated request to FairLaunch as an ibBUSD amount. Because each ibBUSD was worth more than one BUSD, repeated deposit/emergencyWithdraw cycles withdrew excess BUSD and compounded the attacker's credit.

name: Zentra aToken burn clamp lets repayWithATokens clear debt without burning
summary: Zentra, an Aave V3 fork on Citrea, upgraded its aTokens to an implementation whose _burnScaled caps the scaled burn at the holder's scaled balance with no bound on the difference. Pool.repayWithATokens burns the caller's aTokens and marks the debt repaid, so a caller holding no aTokens repays in full while burning nothing. With 200,000 flash-borrowed USDC.e as collateral, the attacker borrowed 140,000 ctUSD, cleared the debt with repayWithATokens and withdrew the collateral. It repeated this for 30 USDC.e.

name: RES token fee settlement against manipulable pair state
summary: BEP20TokenA (RES) settles its transfer fees against AMM state the caller controls in the same transaction. _distB() pays the fee out of the contract's ALL treasury in an amount computed by _atoB()/_tokenACalcTokenB() from live getReserves() of the RES/USDT and USDT/ALL PancakeSwap pairs, and _isBuySwap()/_isSellSwap() arm that path from the pair's raw balanceOf rather than from any manipulation-resistant price, so donating USDT into the RES/USDT pair turns a negligible buy fee into an arbitrarily large ALL payout. The external thisAToB() has no caller restriction and sells the contract's accumulated RES balance into the same pair, then calls _burn(_swapV2Pair, burnNumber) for the full pre-swap amount before sync(); because that sell is itself fee-charged, the burn destroys more RES than the pair received, so the pair pays out USDT for tokens it does not keep.

name: NORMIE premarket-flag balance inflation and forced swapback
