summary: NORMIE's _transfer contains two cooperating defects. _get_premarket_user sets premarket_user[recipient] for any address that receives exactly balanceOf(teamWalletAddress) in a single transfer, so the flag is self-assignable; and for a flagged recipient buying from a market pair, _transfer executes _balances[address(this)] += amount, crediting the token contract the full purchase amount without debiting any account and without changing _totalSupply, so the sum of balances exceeds supply. The same function then sells the contract's balance through swapAndLiquify whenever it exceeds a threshold randomised from block.timestamp and block.difficulty, with no slippage bound and no per-block cap. The attacker flagged their helper by flash-swapping exactly the team wallet's 5,000,000-token balance out of the SushiSwap pair, then shuttled 2,266,628.300256719 NORMIE between the helper and the pair with skim, minting that amount into the contract each round and forcing 51 unbounded swapbacks that dumped 237,150,000 NORMIE into the pair, collapsing the price so the tokens flash-borrowed and sold at the pre-attack price could be repurchased for a fraction of the proceeds. No parameter choice makes this correct: the credit is unbacked at every threshold, and the threshold only sets how often the contract liquidates it.

name: Bogged Finance BOG transfer-fee distribution mint
summary: BOG's _txBurn credited each transfer's staker fee share by only raising _totalFees, without debiting the sender, so every transfer minted new BOG for BOG/WBNB LP stakers. The attacker staked most of the LP and made hundreds of transfers to itself per transaction, collecting freshly minted BOG, then sold it into the PancakeSwap WBNB/BOG pair.

name: Paraluni MasterChef depositByAddLiquidity unvalidated tokens
summary: MasterChef.depositByAddLiquidity() passes the caller-supplied token addresses straight into _doTransferIn and paraRouter.addLiquidity without checking them against the pool LP pair, and addLiquidityInternal then credits the deposit with the raw increase of the pool LP token balance (newBalance - oldBalance). The attacker supplied two tokens of their own whose transferFrom re-entered deposit(pid, amount) with real LP tokens, so the same real LP deposit was counted twice: once by the reentrant deposit and once as the balance delta measured by depositByAddLiquidity. Two withdraw() calls then removed roughly twice the LP that had been paid in.

name: Penpie Pendle-market reward reentrancy
summary: PendleStaking.batchHarvestMarketRewards() had no reentrancy guard and credited reward-token balance increases during a market's redeemRewards() to that pool. The attacker registered a Pendle market with its own SY, re-entered depositMarket() from the harvest to deposit real Pendle LP, so Penpie booked it as rewards, then claimed them and withdrew its deposit.

name: Trade On Orion stake-release liability desynchronization
summary: OrionVault.requestReleaseStake() credited locked ORN directly back to the caller's internal asset balance and cleared the stake without reconciling an existing ORN liability. Repeating the stake-release and redeem cycle therefore left duplicate liability entries for the same asset. MarginalFunctionality.calcLiabilities() valued every entry from the same live balance, so a later positive ORN balance was counted several times as collateral and checkPosition() accepted large unsupported debits that the attacker withdrew. The deployed redeemAtomic path did require the recovered signature to equal order.sender; the seed row's signature-bypass classification was incorrect.

name: Telcoin CloneableProxy re-initialisation
summary: Telcoin wallets are EIP-1167 clones of a CloneableProxy master whose initialize(address,bytes) stays callable when the wallet's own initializer overwrote the proxy's initialized flag in slot 0. The attacker, then copycats, re-initialised unused wallets with a module of their own that transferred out their TEL and MATIC.

name: CAROL sell callback manipulates liquidity-rebalancing reserves
summary: sell pays ETH through an external router before computing the LP burn from current ethReserved. The seller callback reduces that reserve with CAROL-to-WETH trades, causing the subsequent burn to consume nearly all protocol LP; flash-loan spot manipulation also inflates bond-token credit.

name: GoodDollar GoodFundManager untrusted staking callback accounting
summary: GoodFundManager.collectInterest called arbitrary caller-supplied staking contracts and counted the reserve's cDAI growth across those calls as interest. A fake staking contract bought G$ from the reserve in the callback, so mintUBI booked the purchase again as interest and inflated the G$ price; selling G$ back drained the reserve.

name: Sumer Money sdrETH repayBorrowBehalf refund reentrancy
summary: Sumer Money's CEther market sdrETH implements repayBorrowBehalf(address) by refunding any excess msg.value with a gas-forwarding msg.sender.call before it calls the nonReentrant repayBorrowBehalfInternal. During that callback the repaid ETH is already part of getCashPrior() while totalBorrows still carries the debt it settles, so exchangeRateStoredInternal() = (totalCash + totalBorrows - totalReserves) / totalSupply double-counts the same ETH. The attacker drained the market's cash with borrow(), repaid it with one wei of excess, and inside the refund callback the sdrETH exchange rate stood at 2.000000282255694646 instead of the 1.000000141462699840 the market carried a moment earlier: they redeemed their full 150 ETH deposit for half their sdrETH and, with the other half still valued at the doubled rate as Comptroller collateral, borrowed 310,000 USDC from sdrUSDC and 10.877 cbETH from sdrcbETH that were never repaid.

name: Rari Ethereum Pool transient ibETH exchange-rate inflation
summary: AlphaPoolController.getBalance valued Rari's ibETH shares with ibETH.totalETH()/totalSupply() during an external Alpha Homora Bank.work callback. The attacker transiently donated ETH to inflate totalETH, caused Rari withdrawals to burn too many ibETH shares at the manipulated rate, then removed the donation and repeated the cycle.

name: Audius Governance proxy re-initialization
summary: AudiusAdminUpgradeabilityProxy stores proxyAdmin in slot 0, where the logic contracts' Initializable keeps its initialized/initializing flags; with the admin address's low bytes nonzero, initializer guards always pass. The attacker re-initialized Governance, Staking and DelegateManagerV2, delegated fake stake to itself, and passed a proposal moving the treasury's AUDIO.

name: NewMarketTrading SquidRouterModule unbound delegate
summary: SquidRouterModule accepted Axelar express execution while treating caller-supplied sourceAddress and delegate values as authority and never binding the delegate to msg.sender. Forged payloads therefore drove victim Safes to approve and swap valuable assets into attacker pools.

name: Platypus sAVAX pool cash/liability accounting manipulation
summary: In the Platypus sAVAX/WAVAX pool a withdrawal reduced the asset's full liability even when cash was short, so flash-loaned deposits, a swap that drained one side, withdrawals and a reverse swap shifted the coverage ratios and slippage in the attacker's favour, returning more WAVAX and sAVAX than deposited.

name: BelugaDex liability/coverage withdrawal accounting
summary: BelugaDex's Platypus-style stableswap pool priced deposits, swaps and withdrawals from per-asset cash and liability with inconsistent slippage, haircut and withdrawal-fee accounting. A flash-loaned cycle of large USDT and USDC.e deposits, swaps between them and withdrawals took out more than it put in, and the attacker repeated it in 21 transactions.

name: MEV bot 0xd61492 router unauthenticated command entry
summary: The bot's vault 0xd614927a executes commands from its whitelisted router 0x8db0efee, whose entry 0x0582f20f runs a caller-supplied command program, including DELEGATECALL to caller-chosen code, for any caller. The attacker had the vault flash-borrow from a fake Aave-style pool, which used the vault's repayment approvals to pull all its tokens.

name: Moonwell mMAMO donated-underlying exchange-rate inflation
summary: mMAMO's exchange rate counts the market's raw MAMO balance, so MAMO transferred straight to the market revalues every share without minting, and the Comptroller's supply cap, checked only on mint, cannot stop it. After pumping MAMO, the attacker donated MAMO twice, lifting the rate 3.68x past the cap, and borrowed cbBTC, WETH, USDC and wstETH against it.

name: Hundred Finance hWBTC exchange-rate inflation
summary: Hundred's Compound-v2 CToken prices shares from its raw underlying balance and rounds the cTokens burned by redeemUnderlying down. In the near-empty hWBTC market the attacker kept two wei of hWBTC, donated WBTC to inflate their value, borrowed every other market against them, then redeemed the donation for almost no hWBTC, leaving bad debt.

name: Singularity DynaVault oracle zero-price share inflation
summary: UniswapV3Oracle prices a token from whatever token/WETH pool the Uniswap V3 factory returns, with no liquidity floor. The attacker created zero-liquidity pools quoting the DynaVault's ERC4626 holdings at almost nothing, so totalAssets collapsed to its idle USDC; a flash-loaned deposit minted almost all shares and redeemProportional took the portfolio.

name: Cyrus Finance CyrusTreasury spot-priced LP withdrawal
summary: CyrusTreasury paid USDT exits through withdrawUSDTFromAny, which sized the PancakeSwap V3 liquidity to remove from the pool's spot slot0 price and then collected both tokens of the removed liquidity to the claimant. The attacker pushed the ETH/USDT price into the position's range with flash-loaned ETH, exited a small position, received most of the treasury's liquidity, and swapped back.

name: SynapLogic sale proxy unbounded referral rebates
summary: The SYP sale implementation paid a per-entry referral rebate without bounding aggregate rebates by the payment received. A bounded pre-remediation campaign depleted the proxy's native ETH and USDC inventory through the affected native and USDC purchase paths.

name: JUDAO sell-hook pair-reserve desynchronization
summary: JUDAO's sell hook moved JUDAO out of its own PancakeSwap pair (daily mining and burn), synced the lowered balance as the reserve, and only then completed the seller-to-pair transfer. With a flash loan the attacker bought JUDAO, sold it into the pair to trigger the hook, and used the balance-over-reserve gap as swap input to withdraw excess USDT.

name: Defrost LSWUSDC flash-loan deposit reentrancy
summary: LSWUSDC.flashLoan() withdrew the loan from Aave before the borrower callback and had no reentrancy guard, and deposit() priced shares off getTotalAssets(), which the outstanding loan depressed. A borrower could deposit inside the callback, mint excess shares, repay the loan and redeem them for more USDC than it supplied.

name: Ploutoz live-reserve collateral pricing
summary: Ploutoz, a bZx-style lending fork, priced DOP collateral with a PancakeOracle that returned the spot reserve ratio of a DOP/BUSD pair. The attacker flash-swapped BUSD, bought DOP to inflate that ratio, borrowed from six iToken pools against a small DOP deposit and sold the DOP back; a copycat and the attacker repeated it later.

name: CorkHook beforeSwap missing pool-manager restriction
summary: The incident combined a rollover-pricing defect that let the attacker acquire an excessive CT position for dust with CorkHook.beforeSwap() lacking the authorization check that restricted calls to the official Uniswap v4 PoolManager. A direct call to the hook abused its callback and refund path to obtain matching DS, and the attacker redeemed the CT/DS pair against the protocol's wstETH reserves.

name: UPS sell path burns the pair's reserve
summary: On every non-whitelisted sale to its USDT pair, the UPS token burns 95% of the sold amount directly from the pair's balance and calls sync() before the swap settles. The attacker used flash-loaned USDT to buy almost all UPS out of the pair, sending it to an address on the public whitelist because ordinary buys revert. It then sold 4,982,240 UPS. The burn cut the pair's UPS reserve to 1 wei, so the swap paid out 560,128 USDT.

name: Sharwa margin Hegic option collateral valued by a Uniswap V3 spot quote
summary: Sharwa's HegicModule values a Hegic option NFT held as margin collateral by passing its USDC.e payoff to UniswapModuleWithoutChainlink.getInputPositionValue, which returns the Uniswap V3 Quoter's live quote through the thin USDC.e/USDC 0.05% pool. Inside a Balancer flash loan the attacker pushed 22,000 USDC into that pool, raising an option with a 0.137528 USDC.e payoff to about 21,223 USDC of collateral value (later 36,584), and borrowed USDC, WETH and WBTC from Sharwa's liquidity pools against it.

name: Libertify LibertiVault deposit swap-callback reentrancy
summary: LibertiVault.deposit priced shares against a NAV read before its 1inch user swap and had no reentrancy guard. The attacker's swap executor re-entered deposit, so outer deposits minted shares against the stale NAV and the inflated supply was redeemed for the vault's reserves. The attacker and two copycats repeated it on the Ethereum vault.

name: YYDS pair-balance price manipulation
summary: consumptionReturnPool.getPriceOfUSDT() converted stored USDT-denominated returns to YYDS using the instantaneous ERC-20 balances of the YYDS/USDT pair, with no TWAP or manipulation protection. During a pair flash swap, the attacker reduced the pair's USDT balance from 1186471.120130432957137499 USDT to 1.2 USDT while its YYDS balance remained 1656.938602269843892480. Integer normalization then produced a price of only 0.000603864734299516 USDT per YYDS. Two attacker-controlled callers used genuine matured return records totalling 1.683 USDT to withdraw 2787.048000000004191719 YYDS and sold it into the same pair. The withdrawal functions do index msg.sender's stored entitlement arrays; the defect is the manipulable pair-balance oracle, not missing entitlement checks.

name: TUR Stake spot-priced power and unaccrued referral power
summary: The TUR Stake contract converts staked TUR into mining power from the spot reserves of the TUR/NOBEL and NOBEL/USDT PancakeSwap pairs, and credits 20% and 5% of that power to the staker's first two referrers by raising their power without adjusting their rewardDebt, so each referrer can immediately claim the new power times the whole accumulated reward per share. The attacker borrowed 1.9M USDT, bought NOBEL and TUR to inflate both spot prices, staked 840,992 TUR from an account bound under its own referrer accounts, and had those referrers claim, draining the contract's entire 18.8M TUR reward balance before selling it back to USDT.

name: Unknown Base account module unauthenticated execute drains vault
summary: Account 0xc851e5a0 is an EIP-1167 clone of a router that resolves its logic through a registry to module 0xa2362ea5. That module's ERC725X-style execute(uint256,address,uint256,bytes) performs the call for any caller. Vault 0x36057cb0 lets 0xc851e5a0 withdraw. An attacker's constructor had the account call the vault's withdraw (0xaaa18f86) with itself as recipient and took 300,000 USDC. A second actor repeated the call nine days later and took 100,000 USDC.

name: Unknown BSC pool poolWithdraw accepts empty signer and signature lists
summary: The unverified implementation behind proxy 0x20dbf429 authorizes poolWithdraw(token, amount, to, ..., signers[], deadline, signatures[]) with a multi-signature check that passes when both arrays are empty. From block 83557908 several unrelated callers withdrew the pool's USDT to themselves with empty signer and signature lists until the owner upgraded the implementation at block 83655321.

name: Parity WalletLibrary unprotected initWallet + kill
summary: The shared WalletLibrary was deployed uninitialised and its initWallet() was callable on the library itself, so anyone could become its owner and call kill(), selfdestructing the delegatecall target and permanently locking the ETH and tokens of every Parity multisig that pointed at it.

name: Visor Finance RewardsHypervisor unvalidated depositor
summary: RewardsHypervisor.deposit() trusted a caller-supplied `from` contract both to report its owner and to transfer VISR, without validating the contract or confirming receipt. The attacker hook no-opped the transfer and reentered deposit once, causing two vVISR share mints backed by zero VISR.

name: Grim Finance GrimBoostVault depositFor reentrancy
summary: GrimBoostVault.depositFor(token, amount, user) takes the deposit token from the caller and mints shares from the vault's balance change around an unguarded token.transferFrom. Passing an attacker contract as the token lets its transferFrom re-enter depositFor with the real LP, so one deposit is credited at every nesting level; withdrawAll then drains the vault.

name: Rari Fuse (Pool reentrancy)
summary: Fuse's CEtherDelegate.borrow sent ETH with an unbounded call before recording the borrow. From the ETH callback the attacker exited its collateral market while the Comptroller still saw no debt, redeemed the flash-loaned collateral and kept the borrowed funds, repeating it against seven Fuse pools.

name: Allbridge CCTP phantom deposit
summary: CCTPTokenMessenger.receiveCctpMessage read amount, source sender and hook hash at fixed offsets of any Circle message it relayed, never checking that Circle's TokenMessenger sent it. A self-sent generic CCTP message with a crafted body recorded a phantom deposit that Router.receiveToken paid out in USDC.

name: Superfluid IDA forged callAgreement context
summary: Superfluid agreements decoded the ctx bytes from caller-shaped call data without checking the host's ctx stamp. Through Host.callAgreement the attacker passed a forged context naming victims as msgSender, created and updated IDA indexes as those accounts, distributed their super-token balances to itself and downgraded them.

name: Lendf.Me (imBTC ERC-777 reentrancy)
summary: Lendf.Me's MoneyMarket.supply computed the supplier's new balance before pulling the tokens and stored it afterwards. With ERC-777 imBTC listed, the attacker's tokensToSend hook re-entered withdraw mid-supply, so the outer supply restored the withdrawn balance; looping doubled its imBTC credit, which it withdrew and borrowed every other market against.

name: Sturdy LendingPool setUserUseReserveAsCollateral skips the oracle reentrancy probe
summary: Sturdy's LendingPool implementation carries an internal _validateOracle(user) that runs Balancer's reentrancy probe (BALWSTETHWETHOracle.check(), a WITHDRAW_INTERNAL manageUserBalance call that reverts inside a Vault context) over every reserve the user holds as collateral. deposit, _withdraw, repay, liquidationCall, finalizeTransfer and _executeBorrow all call it; setUserUseReserveAsCollateral does not, yet its ValidationLogic.validateSetUseReserveAsCollateral path reaches GenericLogic.balanceDecreaseAllowed and prices every collateral through SturdyOracle. The attacker re-entered that one entry point from inside a Balancer exitPool ETH callback, so the cB-stETH-STABLE collateral was valued from mid-exit pool balances: BALWSTETHWETHOracle.latestAnswer() returned 3.008 ETH instead of 1.034 ETH per unit. The invariant violated is that collateral valuation must never be computed while the Balancer Vault is mid-update; the deployed pool enforced it on every oracle-consuming entry point except this one.

name: Unknown Base MEV bot unvalidated uniswapV3SwapCallback
summary: Bot contract 0xe143b486's uniswapV3SwapCallback(int256,int256,bytes) pays the positive delta by transferFrom from a payer named in the callback data to msg.sender. The token comes from msg.sender.token0(), and nothing checks that the caller is a genuine pool. The operator EOA 0xc0ffee47 had approved the bot for WETH. The attacker's contract, posing as a pool, called the callback 219 times with the operator as payer and pulled 55.42 WETH.

name: RubicProxy routerCallNative executes an arbitrary whitelisted call
summary: RubicProxy.routerCallNative() forwards caller-supplied calldata to a caller-supplied router address, checking only that the router is in availableRouters. The contract makes no distinction between a swap router and an ERC-20, so once USDC was added to that list any caller could pass USDC as the router and transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) as the calldata, spending the unlimited approvals users had granted the proxy.

name: Matez stake uint128 truncation credits unpaid referral rewards
summary: MatezStakingProgram.stake charges estimateAmountOut(USDT, uint128(amnt)) MATEZ but credits the full uint256 amnt to selfInvest, directInvest and teamInvest. Stakes of 2^128 cost nothing yet met every achievement threshold, so attacker sub-accounts claimed MATEZ rewards (claim type 3) from the program.

name: Startale smart-account initializer accepts any caller while the transaction-scoped deployment flag is set
summary: StartaleAccountFactory deploys each ERC-7579 account as an AccountProxy whose constructor sets an EIP-1153 transient flag, and StartaleSmartAccount.initializeAccount lets any external caller in once that flag is set. Transient storage lasts for the whole transaction, not the constructor frame. So a contract that calls createAccount for a counterfactual account that users had already funded can call initializeAccount again in the same transaction. It passes a malicious bootstrap that runs by DELEGATECALL in the account and sweeps its tokens and ETH. From 2026-09-15 at least 16 senders drained 1,052 pre-funded accounts this way in 255 transactions.

name: LavaLending borrowable WETH/USDC.e wrapper LP priced from dust residual supply
summary: Lava listed a UniV3 wrapper LP as borrowable collateral priced by WrapperOracle at wrapper assets (including unclaimed fees) over live totalSupply. The attacker borrowed the LP out of the reserve and redeemed it, leaving dust supply, donated fees to inflate the per-share price, and borrowed every reserve's cash against the inflated aLP collateral.

name: Pro Token unrestricted executor campaign
summary: The Pro executor implementation exposed exec() without the caller allowlist added by the post-incident replacement and without a cadence or batch limit, allowing an untrusted caller to force repeated Pro sales under attacker-controlled pool conditions and extract USDT.

name: ACP PaymentManager releasePayment double release
summary: PaymentManager.releasePayment had its escrow check commented out and recorded the claim only on an in-memory copy of the job, so each call paid the full budget again from pooled escrow. The attacker created a 97,000 USDC job with its own provider, completed it and called claimBudget to release it twice; copycats re-claimed other completed jobs.

name: Allbridge Core pool withdraw removes equal token and vUsd amounts and resets the pool price
summary: Allbridge Core's Pool.withdraw subtracted the same absolute amount from tokenBalance and vUsdBalance, so on an imbalanced pool a withdrawal pushed the curve price far from parity at no fee. With flash-loaned BUSD the attacker became the BUSD pool's dominant LP, skewed and withdrew it, then swapped through the Bridge for vUSD paid out as USDT by the USDT pool.

name: xWin referral reward paid on subscription notional that is redeemed in the same transaction
summary: xWinDefi credits XWIN rewards along two paths that disagree. The subscriber's own reward, in _storeRewardQty, is time weighted: it multiplies the accumulated base by the number of blocks the position has been held, so an instantly redeemed subscription earns nothing. The referral and manager rewards, in _updateReferralReward, are a flat fraction of _tradeParams.amount credited at subscription time with no holding period, and Redeem's _updateRewardBal only unwinds the subscriber's accumulators, never the referral's. The only guard against self dealing is require(msg.sender != _tradeParams.referral), an address-equality test that a second attacker-controlled contract defeats. Subscribing 76,000 flash-loaned BNB while naming a second attacker contract as referral, then redeeming in the same call frame, therefore mints 15,200 XWIN to the attacker for a round-trip cost of about 0.03 BNB in fund slippage, and the loop is repeatable until the protocol's rewardRemaining budget runs out.

name: Payy verifier accepted zero-hash USDC burns
summary: Payy L2 admitted UTXO burns of USDC with a zero burn hash, which the UTXO circuit binds to the first input-note commitment and permits only for zero-kind padding notes. The registered recursive Honk verifier accepted the aggregated statements, and two settlement batches depleted the bridge through direct payouts and a reimbursed fast withdrawal.

name: TempleDAO StaxLPStaking unrestricted migrateStake
summary: StaxLPStaking.migrateStake(address oldStaking, uint256 amount) took the migration source as a caller-supplied address and called oldStaking.migrateWithdraw() without checking that the caller was an authorised migrator or that the source was a known staking contract. The attacker passed a contract of their own, was credited a stake equal to the whole StaxLP balance held by the staking contract, and withdrew it.

name: SNK retroactive referral reward accounting
summary: SNKMiner.dynamicEarned() multiplied a parent's accumulated reward-per-token delta by its children's current staked balance. A newly bound child could therefore stake after the delta accrued and retroactively increase the parent's reward; repeating that sequence produced excess SNK that the attacker sold into the SNK/USDT pool.

name: Uniswap V1 ERC-777 sender-hook reserve reentrancy
summary: Uniswap V1 tokenToEthInput pays ETH before collecting tokens and has no reentrancy lock. An ERC-777 tokensToSend callback can sell again before the first transfer updates the token reserve, overpaying ETH against a stale reserve.

name: Likwid MarginPosition leverage-0 borrow reuses an unbooked AMM quote
summary: LikwidMarginPosition's leverage-0 borrow capped each loan at the pool's quote for selling the pledged collateral but never booked that sale, so every new position got the same quote. Attackers bought pool tokens from the vault, pledged them across 16 to 40 fresh positions in one transaction and walked away with more BNB than they paid.

name: ParticleExchange onERC721Received forged lien
summary: ParticleExchange trusted caller-supplied ERC721 callback and lien data, letting a malicious collection fabricate NFT ownership and credit an unbacked ETH balance.

name: Saddle sUSD metapool stale MetaSwapUtils library
summary: The sUSDv2 metapool was linked to a stale MetaSwapUtils whose _calculateSwap path omitted baseVirtualPrice scaling when saddleUSD-V2 was the input or output token. Repeated sUSD/saddleUSD-V2 round trips therefore shifted the invariant and price curve in the attacker's favor until both sides of the metapool were drained.

name: Inverse Finance Anchor xINV InvFeed Keep3r TWAP manipulation
summary: Anchor priced xINV collateral via InvFeed, which read Keep3rV2Oracle.current(): a TWAP from the last observation of the SushiSwap INV/WETH pair, with no minimum window. The attacker pumped INV on Sushi and forced a fresh observation, then a block later minted xINV at the inflated price and borrowed ETH, WBTC, DOLA and YFI from Anchor markets.

name: EFLeverVault flash-loan balance inflation
summary: EFLeverVault authenticated receiveFlashLoan() only by requiring Balancer as caller, so anyone could ask Balancer to invoke its withdrawal branch and release leveraged collateral as ETH. withdraw() then sent the vault's entire ETH balance to one share holder instead of that holder's proportional amount.

name: Sentiment WeightedBalancerLPOracle Balancer vault read-only reentrancy
summary: WeightedBalancerLPOracle.getPrice(token) values a Balancer weighted-pool BPT as the weighted-geometric invariant of vault.getPoolTokens(poolId) balances divided by IPool(token).totalSupply(). Both reads are unguarded external views on the Balancer Vault and the pool token, and the oracle never probes the vault's reentrancy lock. Inside Vault.exitPool the BPT is burned before the pool's native-ETH payout returns, so total supply is already reduced while the token balances are not yet settled, and the quotient overstates the unit value. The attacker re-entered Sentiment from the exitPool ETH callback and had RiskEngine.isAccountHealthy price 221.214516056534546564 B-33WETH-33WBTC-33USDC at 3.5500730700050576 ETH instead of the 0.2201185612401734 ETH the same function returned outside reentrancy, a 16.1x inflation, which let AccountManager.borrow approve four undercollateralised borrows in the same transaction. The violated invariant is that a collateral price must not be derived from a Balancer pool's balances and supply while that pool is mid-update; the deployed oracle has no state in which it can detect that.

name: Minterest mUSDY flashLoan exchange-rate reentrancy
summary: The mUSDY market runs the ERC-3156 borrower callback while its own cash balance is still reduced by the flash-loaned amount, and the mToken exchange rate is computed from that cash balance. Supplying USDY back inside the callback therefore minted mUSDY at an inflated rate. The attacker repeated the cycle 24 times to build collateral it had not paid for and borrowed the WETH and mETH markets out against it.

name: Utopia predictable airdrop balance overwrite
summary: Utopia._airdrop overwrites rather than increments a predictably chosen address balance. A crafted pair skim overwrote the pair’s Utopia balance, allowing sync and tiny subsequent sales to drain WBNB reserves.

name: Umbrella Chain.submit() accepts unstaked signatures, faking FTS and MAHA prices
summary: Umbrella's Chain.submit() counts signatures from addresses without validator stake and never checks signing power, so anyone can publish any price. In one transaction the attacker executed its proposal making fFTS collateral, submitted huge FTS and MAHA prices, borrowed every Fortress market against 100 FTS and minted ARTH on MAHA to dump into Ellipsis.

name: Parity multisig wallet reinitialization
summary: Parity multisig wallets forwarded unmatched calls by delegatecall to a shared WalletLibrary whose public initWallet had no one-time guard. Anyone could call it through a wallet to replace the owner set with their own address and then execute an authorized transfer of the wallet's ETH.

name: Hedgey Finance ClaimCampaigns unvalidated locker approval
summary: ClaimCampaigns.createLockedCampaign approved the caller-supplied claimLockup.tokenLocker for the campaign amount and cancelCampaign refunded the tokens without revoking it. Creating and cancelling a campaign with an attacker contract as locker left an allowance that it spent with transferFrom to drain the contract's tokens, on Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Avalanche and Polygon.

name: yETH weighted-stableswap solver invariant collapse
summary: Extreme imbalanced deposits drove the yETH weighted-stableswap supply solver outside its valid domain until its product term hit zero, and the pool over-minted yETH. The attacker used permissionless rate updates to burn the staking contract's LP, drained the LSTs, then hit an unchecked underflow at zero supply to mint yETH and drain the Curve pool.

name: Internet Token LiquidityUnifier unvalidated V3 pool callback mint
summary: LiquidityUnifier.swapV3 accepts any contract reporting INT and a quote token as a Uniswap V3 pool, and its swap callback mints INT to that pool. The attacker passed its own contract, minted INT in the callback, cycled it through the Convertor so the supply check passed, and dumped INT into the real INT/WETH pool; copycats repeated it.

name: ROE WBTC/USDC LP live-reserve collateral valuation
summary: ROE's custom WBTC/USDC LP oracle divided the pair's current externally priced reserves by current LP supply. It applied no time, donation or deviation bound, so a same-receipt reserve donation immediately raised every recursively minted roeLP collateral claim before the USDC borrow check. The violated invariant is that collateral value used to authorize borrowing must not be increased atomically by the borrower through a live reserve balance that is amplified across repeated claims on the same underlying inventory.

name: GatewayEVM arbitrary-call allowance drain
summary: GatewayEVM.execute with a zero sender routes TSS-relayed calls to _executeArbitraryCall, whose deny-list blocks only onCall and onRevert. An attacker requested arbitrary calls from ZetaChain whose calldata was ERC20 transferFrom, so the gateways on Arbitrum, BSC, Base and Ethereum spent wallets' standing gateway allowances to the attacker.

name: ATM expired-reward reserve-removal campaign
summary: Staking.burnExpiredReward was permissionless and made ATMToken.recycle move up to a third of the ATM/USDT pair's ATM out of the pair and sync. The attacker bought ATM, called it for thousands of expired reward records to strip ATM from the pair and inflate its price, then sold through 30 farmer contracts into the inflated USDT reserve.

name: EarningFarm ENF ETH vault withdraw share-burn reentrancy
summary: EFVault.withdraw() computed the shares to burn, had the controller pay the receiver in ETH, and only then capped the burn at the caller's current balance. In the ETH callback the attacker moved its shares to a helper, so withdraw burned almost nothing and the helper withdrew again with the same shares; repeated until the strategy was drained.

name: Unknown distribution contract unchecked allocation-sum overflow
summary: The unverified Solidity 0.7.6 distribution contract's single-token deposit function 0x317de4f6(token,(recipient,amount)[]) sums allocation amounts without overflow checks, pulls only that sum from the caller, then credits each nonzero recipient its full amount as a claimable balance. The attacker passed a zero-address entry of 2^256-97812920708 and a self entry equal to the contract's USDT balance, paid 1 USDT base unit, and claim() paid out all 97,812.920709 USDT held for unclaimed allocations; a second actor repeated it for the residual USDe.

name: Indexed Finance DEFI5/CC10 reindex minimum-balance manipulation
summary: IndexPool valued itself from one token's spot balance and the controller's permissionless updateMinimumBalance() used that to size a newly reindexed, uninitialized token. After skewing DEFI5 and CC10 balances with flash-loaned swaps, the attacker reset SUSHI's minimum balance and joined with SUSHI to mint index tokens against pool assets.

name: Meter Passport BSC handler credits untransferred wrapped-native deposits
summary: Meter's ChainBridge ERC20Handler.deposit skips the token transfer for the wrapped-native resource, assuming Bridge.depositETH already wrapped msg.value. Bridge.deposit reaches the same path charging only the fee, so the attacker recorded WBNB and WETH deposits it never sent, and relayers released real or minted unbacked funds on destination chains.

name: Uwerx WERX fee burn charged to the sending Uniswap pair
summary: WERX's ERC20._transfer() credits the recipient the full `amount` and then, when `to == uniswapPoolAddress`, charges an extra 1% on top by calling _burn(from, burnAmount) against the sender, while emitting decorative 97/2/1 Transfer events that do not match the balance updates. Because UniswapV2Pair.skim(to) is permissionless and makes the pair itself the `from` of a WERX transfer, anyone can donate tokens to the pair, skim them to `uniswapPoolAddress` and have 1% of the donated amount burned out of the pair's own reserve. The attacker donated 4,429,817.738575912760684500 WERX, exactly 100x the pair's remaining reserve, so the 1% burn destroyed the entire WERX side of pair 0xa41529982bcccdfa1105c6f08024df787ca758c4 and let him buy back all 174.79 WETH for dust. No value of uniswapPoolAddress repairs this: pointing it at the real pair leaves skim(pair) reaching the same _burn(from == pair) path.

name: Velocore ConstantProductPool fee underflow
summary: ConstantProductPool.velocore__execute lacked a vault-only check. The attacker called it directly with extreme amounts to inflate feeMultiplier, then withdrew through Vault.execute, where the unchecked effective-fee arithmetic underflowed and a dust LP burn paid out most of each pool's reserves. Repeated on Velocore's zkSync Era pools.

name: SoulMate vault unprotected redeem()
summary: SoulMate's redeem(amount, to) redeemed BUI SetTokens held by the vault itself through the DebtIssuanceModule without checking the caller, so anyone could burn the vault's BUI and receive the underlying token basket.

name: Whalebit staking level redemption at live CES/USDT pool price
summary: Whalebit's staking proxy 0x40465755eb5846d655bbcc8c186a477469f9ce36 runs implementation 0x9153e149b0d90dea634ed9f7df6ff71c2109b654, whose deposit(level) and withdraw(amount) both convert between CES and an internal point balance at a price read from the CES/USDT Algebra pool 0xd3a9331a654444f9fe7ddbaec6678c2dc9113197 at call time, through pricer 0xb5ea1d17f3d8da34a6d6a1d2acc2a148e1411868 and price source 0xa293baf403299d3d5723e8fa3f9f946752aecf9a. The point balance credited on deposit is fixed by the level table, but the CES charged on deposit and the CES paid on withdrawal are each divided by a fresh price, and nothing ties the redemption price to the price the position was opened at: no price is stored with the position, there is no withdrawal delay, no deviation guard between the two legs and no minimum holding period. In the anchor transaction the pricer answers 1.085562 for five deposits of 5979.492113764512759291 CES each crediting 6491.109418002432000001 points, the attacker then swaps 7240.741153581361260699 CES into the Algebra pool, and the same five positions redeem the same 6491.109418002432000001 points for 6002.255702326453957437 CES each at the new price 1.081445. The contract's own nominally averaged source does not help: getAveragePrice(120) and getActualPrice() return the identical word in every read of the trace, before and after each swap, so the redemption rate follows the pool tick inside one transaction. No parameter value makes this correct - the level price, the priced pool and the averaging argument are configuration, but a deposit and a redemption quoted at two independently sampled market prices is extractable under all of them.

name: Balancer boosted linear-pool rounding
summary: Balancer linear pools rounded tiny BPT-for-main-token swaps to zero output while still taking the BPT out of circulation. Repeating this drove a pool's virtual supply near zero and inflated its BPT rate; nested boosted pools priced that BPT at the inflated rate and paid out sibling linear BPT, redeemed for underlying.

name: UF DAO stale XDAO Shop public offer mints LP below treasury value
summary: Shop.buyPublicOffer mints LP at the DAO's static offer rate, while LP.burn redeems pro rata against the whole DAO treasury. UF DAO's offer of 1 LP per 1 USDC stayed active, uncapped and unexpiring as its treasury grew against a 6.8 LP supply, so anyone could buy LP for far less than its redemption value and burn it to drain the treasury.

name: TIME ERC-2771 Multicall sender spoof
summary: TIME combined a trusted-forwarder ERC-2771 context with self-delegatecall Multicall. A forwarded multicall could append an attacker-chosen address to an inner call, making burn() treat the TIME/WETH pair as the sender; the attacker burned the pair's TIME reserve, synchronized the pool, and drained WETH at the distorted price.

name: Cellframe LP migration calculation flaw
summary: LpMigration.migrate(uint256) burns old CELL/WBNB LP and pairs the returned WBNB with new CELL from its inventory at the new pair's live reserve ratio. With flash-borrowed funds the attacker depressed the new CELL price and inflated the WBNB the old pair returned, so repeated migrations drained almost all of the contract's new CELL.

name: OnyxDAO NFTLiquidation unvalidated repay oToken
summary: NFTLiquidation.liquidateWithSingleRepay accepts any oTokenRepay and sets extraRepayAmount from the caller's repayAmount, which the Comptroller adds to every seize calculation. Having borrowed against flash-loaned oETH and forced a shortfall via oETH redeem rounding, the attacker's fake oToken self-liquidated for 1 wei and seized back its collateral.

name: Silo soUSDC SiloVault externally credited wstUSR-market shares inflate totalAssets
summary: SiloVault.totalAssets() sums previewRedeem of the vault's share balance in every withdraw-queue market, so bUSDC shares a third party mints to the vault through wstUSR/USDC market.deposit(assets, receiver=soUSDC) raise soUSDC's share price without minting soUSDC shares and without the curator allocating. That market prices wstUSR collateral with an immutable wstUSR/stUSR exchange-rate feed (1.1330 USDC) while wstUSR traded near 0.12 after the USR depeg. Each cycle flash-borrowed USDC, deposited into soUSDC, donated USDC into the wstUSR market for soUSDC, borrowed that USDC back against wstUSR, and redeemed the inflated soUSDC shares from healthy markets, leaving soUSDC holding undercollateralised wstUSR-market shares.

name: Euler Finance donateToReserves self-liquidation
summary: EToken.donateToReserves() burned the caller's eTokens without checking account liquidity. The attacker built a leveraged eToken/dToken position with a flash loan, donated collateral to the reserves to push the account deep underwater, then self-liquidated it from a second account at the maximum discount and withdrew the surplus collateral.

name: Secured Finance same-block order-book unit price valued as collateral
summary: Secured Finance valued lend positions used as collateral with LendingMarket.getMarketUnitPrice, which returns the current block's filled amount divided by filled future value once block volume passes a fixed threshold. Attackers matched orders between two of their own accounts inside one transaction to set that price, so a cheaply bought lend position counted as fully backed collateral, and withdrew other depositors' USDC, WBTC, WETH and JPYC from the TokenVault on Ethereum and Arbitrum.

name: Multichain (AnyswapV4 permit)
summary: AnyswapV4Router treated a non-reverting permit call as proof of authorization. WETH's fallback returned successfully without creating an allowance, after which the router consumed users' pre-existing approvals.

name: Spartan Protocol LP share calculation flaw
summary: Spartan pools' removeLiquidity asked the DAO-selected Utils module's calcLiquidityShare to value LP units from the pool's live token balances rather than its recorded reserves. Donating assets to a pool before burning LP inflated the redemption, and the pool's addLiquidity then credited the donated, unsynced balance back to the attacker.

name: Z123 swap burns pool liquidity
summary: Z123's transfer accounting reduced the token-side balance of its own Z123/USDT pair during swaps, breaking reserve accounting and depleting the pair's USDT reserve.

name: FEG SmartBridge relayer whitelists forged Wormhole source on superAdmin payload
summary: FEG's unverified relayer whitelists a Wormhole message's source address whenever the payload's user is a superAdmin, so any contract can make itself a trusted source. The attacker sent such a message naming the FEG admin, then a second one that made SmartBridge.registerWithdraw credit it, and withdrew and sold nearly all bridged FEG on BSC, Base and Ethereum.

name: BabyDoge FarmZAP arbitrary-farm and auto-liquidity manipulation
summary: FarmZAP accepted any caller-supplied farm and gave it an unlimited approval on the swap output; since the zap was exempt from BabyDoge's transfer fees, this gave the attacker fee-free moves of flash-bought BabyDoge. It crashed the PancakeSwap price, triggered BabyDoge's unbounded swapAndLiquify sell into it, bought back and sold on BabyDogeSwap.

name: REVLoans unregistered source and decimal normalization
summary: REVLoans.borrowFrom accepts an unregistered caller-supplied terminal/token pair. _addTo persists the fabricated debt and _totalBorrowedFrom counts it at the fake source's own accounting context, inflating the revnet's borrowed-plus-surplus term, so later loans against dust collateral drain real terminals on every chain REVLoans is deployed on.

name: JulSwap JulProtocolV2 addBNB spot-reserve quote treasury drain
summary: JulProtocolV2.addBNB() sized the protocol's own JULb contribution from the instantaneous WBNB/JULb reserve ratio and added it as liquidity with amountBNBMin = 1. Attackers crashed the JULb price with flash-swapped JULb, called addBNB so the treasury poured JULb into the pair at the crashed ratio, then bought JULb back cheaply and kept the BNB.

name: Ekubo router payCallback settles with a caller-supplied payer
summary: The Ekubo router's payCallback takes the payer of a Core debt from caller-supplied calldata and never checks it against the caller. The attacker locked Core, withdrew WBTC to itself and settled the debt via pay(), whose callback ran transferFrom on a third party holding a router approval. Copycats then drained other approval holders the same way.

name: BurgerSwap DemaxPlatform reentrant swap on DemaxPair without k check
summary: DemaxPlatform computed a multi-hop swap's outputs up front and then pulled each input with transferFrom, so an attacker-issued fake token in the path could re-enter the platform mid-swap. DemaxPair.swap has no constant-product check and trusts the platform's amounts, so the outer swap paid out at stale reserves and drained the pairs.

name: ElasticSwap Exchange removeLiquidity decay accounting
summary: ElasticSwap Exchange.removeLiquidity paid out quote tokens pro rata of the live balance but debited that payout from the internal quote reserve with a zero clamp. Attackers took about half the LP supply, donated quote tokens directly to the exchange, removed liquidity to collapse the internal reserve, then swapped against the broken curve to drain the base token.

name: Scream fUSD collateral priced through the USDC feed
summary: Scream's oracle priced fUSD with Chainlink's USDC/USD feed and the comptroller listed scFUSD as 85% collateral, so fUSD counted near $1 while it traded around $0.70. Accounts bought discounted fUSD, supplied it and borrowed DAI, USDC, WFTM, WETH and WBTC beyond its market value, some in atomic swap-supply-borrow loops.
unverified: 0x0b24e9420c125242a5ec438bc65e48af1e866ddd: slot write attributed to block 15846647, not traced to 0x826e7afd84b6f36960daed799ed5d3db6c7c81b87ba92a1995b53191f9dbae07

name: Alkimiya SilicaPools uint128 share-supply truncation
summary: SilicaPools minted the full uint256 share quantity as ERC-1155 long and short balances but added only an unchecked uint128 cast of it to the pool's sharesMinted. Minting 2^128+1 shares on a permissionless pool recorded a supply of 1; after ending the pool, two retained short shares redeemed twice the deposited collateral, taking WBTC held for other pools.

name: BeatSwap LiquidityVestingConvert slot0 spot-price BTX quote
summary: LiquidityVestingConvert and its Once variant paired a deposit's USDT with BTX from their own reserves, sized from the V3 pool's slot0 spot price and checked only against that same quote. With flash loans the attacker crashed the BTX price, deposited 10,000 and 2,000 USDT so both contracts put nearly all their BTX into LP at that price, then bought it back and sold it.

name: WOOFi WooPPV2 sPMM self-posted price collapse
summary: WooPPV2's sPMM sell-base quote posted a new WOO price to WooracleV2 with no floor or relative-move bound, and the oracle's Chainlink bound check failed open because WOO had no reference feed. Flash-loaned WOO sold into the pool collapsed the price to near zero, letting the attacker buy back the pool's WOO for almost nothing, three times.

name: FoomLottery Groth16 degenerate-verifier proof forgery
summary: FoomLottery's withdraw Groth16 verifier was deployed with gamma and delta set to the same G2 point because the trusted-setup Phase 2 contribution was skipped, so the pairing check no longer binds the public inputs. Anyone could forge collect() proofs for fresh nullifiers; the attacker looped forged collects to drain the Base lottery, and copycats hit the Base and Ethereum lotteries.

name: BRO wrapper callback double-mint SolvBTC drain
summary: The BRO wrapper's mint() pulls the whole ERC-3525 position in with safeTransferFrom, whose onERC721Received callback mints BRO for the received value before the outer mint() mints it again. Looping burn-then-mint doubled the attacker's BRO each round; the unbacked BRO was then exchanged for SolvBTC from the treasury's exchange.

name: Butter Bridge retry-message hash collision
summary: Butter Bridge stored failed-message commitments with abi.encodePacked over adjacent dynamic byte fields. The attacker retried a valid failed message with different field boundaries but the same packed preimage, redirecting execution to MAPO and minting one quadrillion unbacked tokens.

name: Hyperbridge HandlerV1 MMR verifier accepts out-of-range leaves
summary: HandlerV1 verifies post requests with an inlined Merkle Mountain Range verifier that ignores leaves not below leafCount. Passing the stored overlay root as the proof, with leafCount 1 and a forged leaf at index 1, validated any request: the TokenGateway released escrow, and copycats minted bridged DOT and drained host fees.

name: TcrToken/Tecra pool unauthorised USDT drain
summary: TcrToken.burnFrom checked and reduced _allowances[msg.sender][from] instead of _allowances[from][msg.sender]. A caller could therefore approve the pool as a spender of the caller's balance, burn TCR directly from the pool without the pool's authorization, synchronize the depleted TCR reserve, and exchange previously acquired TCR for the pool's USDT.

name: Lazy Summer USDC fleets ark donation NAV inflation
summary: Summer arks valued their position as convertToAssets of their own share balance, and each FleetCommander priced shares from the sum of its arks. The attacker donated Varlamore Silo shares, still valued near par after the Stream collapse, to the LowerRisk Silo ark and LowerRisk-backed Term shares to the HigherRisk Term ark, redeeming both fleets at inflated prices.

name: OmniEstate stale global staking reward
summary: The staking pool reuses the prior investment's global reward when an unsupported duration or a stake below 10,000 ORT skips every reward-calculation branch. A new caller can use an unsupported duration to withdraw immediately and mint that stale reward repeatedly.

name: Curve factory ETH pool Vyper lock reentrancy (pETH, alETH)
summary: Vyper 0.2.15 gave each function's @nonreentrant('lock') its own storage slot, so the factory ETH plain-pool template had no shared lock. From the raw-ETH callback in remove_liquidity() the attacker re-entered add_liquidity() before LP supply was reduced, minting LP at an inflated rate and withdrawing it.

name: Agave ERC-677 reentrancy during aToken burn
summary: Agave's Aave v2 fork liquidation sends the seized collateral to the liquidator before the borrower's accounting is final, with no reentrancy guard. Gnosis bridged WETH is ERC-677 and calls onTokenTransfer on the recipient, so the attacker liquidated its own position and re-entered borrow() from the callback, draining six markets against collateral already seized.

name: GemPadLock collectFees reentrancy
summary: GemPadLock.collectFees() pays a V3 lock's fees as the locker's balance change across collect(), unguarded against reentrancy. With a V3 position in its own hooked token, the attacker re-entered multipleLock during collect, so the same LP was locked and paid back as fees; unlocking those free locks drained other projects' locked tokens.

name: z0r0z V4 Router hardcoded calldata-offset payer check bypass
summary: UniswapV4Router04.swap(bytes data, uint256 deadline) checks the payer with inline assembly comparing calldataload(164) to caller(), assuming the data bytes argument always sits at offset 0x40. Because ABI encoding lets a dynamic argument's offset point elsewhere, an attacker crafts calldata that places their own address at byte 164 to pass the check while the decoded BaseData.payer is a victim who had approved the router. The router then pulls the victim's tokens and sends the swap output to an attacker-named receiver. Sixteen addresses drained 30 approved victims across 54 transactions.

name: FarmingLPToken spot-quote share inflation
summary: FarmingLPToken minted shares from manipulable router spot quotes. After inflating the quoted SUSHI value of a small LP deposit, the attacker used the resulting shares to withdraw the vault's pre-existing USDC/WETH LP tokens and transferred surplus shares away before the withdrawal burn.

name: Yield Strategy live-balance donation
summary: Strategy.burn paid out a share of the live pool-token balance while mint credited only the uncached surplus and burn left that surplus uncached, so a donation was both paid out and minted again. Six old strategies, migrated to invest in new strategies, were looped with donated new-strategy tokens minted via mintDivested to drain their holdings.

name: MahaLend
summary: MahaLend, an Aave v3 fork, had an empty USDC reserve. The attacker supplied a dust amount, inflated the liquidity index by repeated flash loans whose premiums accrued to its lone deposit, borrowed ARTH against the inflated collateral and withdrew the USDC through rounding that burned fewer shares than owed.

name: UniLend V2 pool health-factor miscalculation
summary: UniLend valued a position's USDC lend shares from the pool's live token balance, including a 60 million USDC flash loan. The inflated collateral value let the attacker borrow all available stETH, then burn the lend shares and withdraw the flash-loaned USDC while leaving the stETH debt undercollateralized.

name: bZx iToken empty-pool donation rounding
summary: iToken tokenPrice is the pool's underlying balance over share supply, and bZx accepted iTokens as loan collateral at that price. The attacker reduced iYFI to 5 wei of its own shares, donated flash-borrowed YFI to the pool, borrowed other iToken pools' assets against the 5 wei, withdrew the collateral through integer rounding and redeemed the donation.

name: Transit Swap callBytes claimTokens approval drain
summary: Transit's bridge helper 0x0b47275e, an authorized caller of the TransitSwap claimTokens proxy, decoded the claimTokens token, sender, recipient and amount from user-supplied callBytes data. Through the router, attackers made it pull any user's approved USDT, BUSD, USDC and WBNB to themselves; copycats repeated the call within hours.

name: LlamaLend sDOLA-long2 spot share-rate oracle liquidation
summary: The sDOLA-long2 market bound a direct CryptoFromPoolVaultWAgg oracle that multiplied a pool price by sDOLA.convertToAssets(1e18) without smoothing or a rate-change bound. In one receipt the attacker redeemed and donated through sDOLA, atomically changed that share rate, and used the resulting LLAMMA health state to hard-liquidate all 27 active borrowers.

name: Renegade unconsumed v2 initializer delegate takeover
summary: A May 2025 upgrade introduced Renegade dark pool initializer version 2 but did not consume it on the proxy. The public initializer transferred ownership and installed caller-supplied delegate modules before marking version 2 initialized. The attacker called it with a malicious wallet-operations delegate; the initializer immediately delegatecalled that module, which swept all 26 token balances from proxy storage context.

name: Stake DAO L1BlockOracleUpdater sender check bypass for chain 1
summary: L1BlockOracleUpdater.receiveMessage rejects a LaPoste message only when chainId != 1 and the sender is neither L1_SENDER nor the updater, so any Ethereum sender passes. The attacker sent a fabricated L1 block through LaPoste to the Arbitrum and Base updaters, which wrote it into the Votemarket oracles, then registered a crafted header and storage proofs against an attacker-controlled state root and claimed the current epoch of 54 Votemarket campaigns.

name: Poly Network
summary: EthCrossChainManager called any target contract with a selector derived from an attacker-chosen method name in a cross-chain message. The name f1121318093 hashed to EthCrossChainData.putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes, which the manager owned, so one message replaced the keeper public key; attacker-signed messages then unlocked LockProxy funds on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon.

name: Prime DataStreamConsumer stores stale signed oracle reports
summary: Prime's DataStreamConsumer.verifyReport(bytes) is permissionless and, after the Chainlink verifier confirms the DON signature, stores the report's price for its feed without checking that the report's round or timestamp is newer than what is stored. An old but validly signed PRFI report therefore overwrote the live price, inflating PRFI about 52x. The attacker flash-borrowed 100 WHYPE, bought 795,587 PRFI off the thin pool for 26.82 WHYPE, supplied it as collateral at the inflated price and borrowed the lending pool's entire 425.52 WHYPE reserve.

name: Abracadabra CauldronV4 borrow-share rounding (yvCrv3Crypto and magicAPE cauldrons)
summary: CauldronV4 rounds totalBorrow elastic/base conversions so repeated tiny borrow and repay calls skew the ratio once the debt is nearly cleared. The attacker repaid every borrower and called repayForAll, looped 1-wei borrow/repay until new borrows recorded zero borrow parts, then borrowed the cauldron's MIM against dust collateral.

name: Asset-harvesting contract 0x19a2 unauthorised payer transferFrom
summary: The shared asset-harvesting contract 0x19a2, which BSC MEV bots approve, lets anyone register an order with themselves as executor (0xac3994ec) and then executes token.transferFrom(payer, recipient, amount) with payer and amount taken from calldata (0x1270d364). The attacker drained bot 0x8c2d's full BUSDT allowance; copycats drained other approvers.

name: OpBorrowing liquidation clears shared LToken debt
summary: OPBorrowing and OpenLevV1 shared one LPool debt balance per borrower. During marginTrade(), attacker-controlled 1inch callback data opened a dust-collateral OPBorrowing position under the margin trader's address. OPBorrowing.liquidate() then treated the trader's full margin debt as that position's debt and called repayBorrowEndByOpenLev(), which wrote off the unpaid balance. The attacker closed the now debt-free margin trade in the next transaction.

name: Taiko SGX attestation accepts DEBUG-mode enclaves
summary: Taiko's AutomataDcapV3Attestation checked an application enclave quote's MRENCLAVE and MRSIGNER but never its attributes, so a DEBUG-mode enclave passed SgxVerifier.registerInstance. The attacker re-signed the trusted Raiko enclave with the MRSIGNER key that had been committed to the public raiko repository, ran it in DEBUG mode, and registered instances in both the SGX-GETH and SGX-RETH verifiers. The debug-readable instance keys then signed forged proofs, the Inbox saved forged L2 checkpoints, and forged bridge messages drained ETH and ERC-20s from the L1 Bridge and ERC20Vault.

name: Messina router hop() recursive VAA re-emission (Opulous OPUL)
summary: The Messina router on Avalanche, the Wormhole emitter every destination bridge trusts, re-publishes any verified VAA through hop() without checking its emitter or target chain. Attackers fed the router's own output VAAs back into hop(), turning single deposits into many claimable VAAs that released escrowed tokens on Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base and Polygon.

name: Elephant Status manipulable sweep pricing
summary: Permissionless sweep() withdrew BUSD from the Treasury and bought ELEPHANT through BUSD/WBNB/ELEPHANT PancakeSwap pools with zero minimum output, sized from live reserves. The attacker flash-borrowed BUSD, skewed the BUSD/WBNB pair, triggered the buyback into the skewed price, reversed the trade and kept the spread.

name: Router multicall self-target authorization bypass drives Safe modules
summary: Private DeFi Saver-style Router 0x4f0055926c839d1d960a82cbf84e2ee933958ebc exposes multicall(address,bytes[]) and treats any call whose target is the Router itself as authorized. Wrapping multicall(MODULE, [recipe]) inside multicall(ROUTER, [...]) runs the inner call with the Router as msg.sender. Safe module 0xea18b13d11f705a68f0954f637949e1eaa7ac4ca lists the Router as an executor, so it forwarded an attacker recipe into the victim Safe as a DELEGATECALL to RecipeExecutor. That recipe moved 2,900 aEthrsETH to the Uniswap V4 PoolManager for an MEV frontrunner. Copycats repeated it within 1,443 blocks against this Safe and three other Safes whose modules also trusted the Router, taking aEthrsETH, DUSD, USDC, PAXG and dust.

name: FOX Colony EtherRouter meta-transaction resolver takeover
summary: Colony's executeMetaTransaction (reached through the colony's resolver) forwards the signed call via address(this).call, and the EtherRouter's DSAuth trusts src == address(this). The attacker meta-signed setResolver to point the FOX Colony router at its own resolver, then called drain() through it to sweep USDC and FOX; copycats repeated it on other colonies on Arbitrum and Gnosis.

name: Gnosis Pay Zodiac Delay forged ERC-1271 module signature
summary: Zodiac SignatureChecker._isValidContractSignature accepted a module contract signature whenever isValidSignature's return data began with 0x1626ba7e, ignoring whether the call reverted. The owner Safe bubbled an attacker contract's revert, so anyone could queue transfers through each card Safe's Delay modifier and execute them after the cooldown.

name: SwapX arbitrary transferFrom on approval holders
summary: SwapX's swap entry point 0x4f1f05bc takes the token owner as a caller-supplied argument and runs transferFrom on it into a caller-chosen pair without checking that the owner is the caller. Anyone could swap any SwapX approver's balance into pools they had pumped; the attacker swept 59 BUSD approvers at once and copycats drained approvers for years.

name: Gyroscope GYD L1 CCIP escrow arbitrary call on message receipt
summary: GydL1CCIPEscrow._ccipReceive sends the bridged GYD to the message's recipient and then runs recipient.functionCall(data) as the escrow. The attacker bridged 1 wei GYD from Arbitrum naming the GYD token as recipient and approve(attacker, max) as data, then pulled the escrow's whole GYD balance and sold part of it on several chains.

name: PegaBall
summary: buyGamesFrom self-funds purchases from the proxy balance instead of requiring msg.value, letting a vendor drain vendor/referrer cuts.

name: Civfund attacker-supplied pool callback
summary: An unrestricted CivTrade function accepted a caller-supplied contract as a Uniswap V3 pool and called its mint(); the fake pool then invoked CivTrade's uniswapV3MintCallback, which paid the owed amounts with transferFrom from users who had approved CivTrade. The attacker and copycats repeated this to drain those allowances.

name: Phoenix Finance missing delegateCallSwap authorization
summary: The main implementation exposed delegateCallSwap(bytes) without authorization and forwarded caller-supplied swap calldata to its configured swap module, so the attacker could route assets borrowed into the Phoenix proxy through an attacker-priced token pair.

name: Fun.xyz retired CheckoutPool unauthenticated bridge()
summary: A retired CheckoutPool's bridge() had no caller check and setAllowAll(true) had lifted its target allowlist, yet it stayed a CheckoutPaymaster operator. The attacker registered a checkout with an inflated targetAmount through the live pool's permissionless deposit(), then had the paymaster call the live pool's execute(), which paid it from pool excess.

name: Polygon PoS MRC20 unbacked native issuance
summary: The genesis MRC20 contract holding Polygon's native MATIC let transferWithSig proceed when ecrecovery returned the zero address for a malformed signature, and paid native MATIC out of its own reserve without checking that sender's balance. The attacker sent malformed-signature transfers, directly and from constructors, to pay out MATIC.

name: FloorStaking stake/unstake supply accounting
summary: FloorStaking.stake() pulls FLOOR in before rebase() sets the next distribution to balance minus circulating supply, so the staked principal counts as profit. With the epoch clock months behind, each stake or unstake could run another rebase: the attacker flash-borrowed FLOOR and looped stake to gFLOOR and unstake with rebase, redeeming at rising indexes.

name: Reddio RedSonic Vault stETH double count via permissionless registerErc20
summary: The RedSonic Vault diamond prices its ETH share class from provider legs that read the vault's raw stETH balance, and anyone could register stETH as a separate share class whose assets are that same raw balance. The attacker registered stETH, bought nearly all rsvETH with flash-loaned ETH, deposited stETH to inflate rsvETH's backing without minting rsvETH, then redeemed rsvETH at the inflated rate and withdrew its stETH, draining the vault's native ETH.

name: Abracadabra CauldronV4 cook() unhandled action clears the solvency check
summary: CauldronV4.cook() sends unrecognised action ids to the empty base _additionalCookAction() and assigns its zeroed CookStatus over the running status, clearing the needsSolvencyCheck flag ACTION_BORROW had set. Calling cook([5, 0]) borrowed MIM with no collateral; the attacker drained the free MIM of six cauldron clones of two masters in one transaction.

name: CIVNFT unvalidated mint callback
summary: CIVNFT accepted a caller-supplied contract as a Uniswap V3 pool and paid from its uniswapV3MintCallback without checking the caller was a real pool. The attacker's fake pool called the callback with victims encoded as payer and its own token addresses, so CIVNFT transferFrom'd victims' approved tokens to it.

name: DungeonSwap swap router pulls approved tokens for any caller-named user
summary: DungeonSwap's unverified router exposed 0x4f1f05bc, which pulled the input token from a caller-named user and swapped it along a caller-supplied path and minimum output, never checking the caller. Anyone could spend every allowance granted to the router; attackers forced approved wallets' tokens into thin pools they had front-run, then dumped.

name: TrustedVolumes RFQ permissionless signer registration and taker-funded fills
summary: TrustedVolumes' RFQ module let anyone call registerAllowedOrderSigner, and its fill path pulled the sell-side tokens from the order's taker field without that party's consent. The attacker registered its own EOA as signer, signed orders naming the inventory wallet 0x9ba0cf15 as taker, and filled them for 1 wei of USDC each, spending the wallet's approvals.

name: GoodDollar GoodCompoundStaking COMP reward swap sandwich
summary: GoodCompoundStakingV2 sold its claimed COMP rewards on Uniswap V2 with zero minimum output, capped only by a share of the pool's spot reserve. The attacker dumped borrowed COMP into the pool, called collectInterest listing the staking clone five times to sell all rewards at the crashed price, then bought the COMP back.

name: Poolz LockedDeal CreateMassPools integer overflow
summary: LockedDeal.CreateMassPools(address,uint64[],uint256[],address[]) charges the caller getArraySum(_StartAmount), and getArraySum accumulates the caller-supplied array with an unchecked sum = sum + _array[i] under Solidity 0.6.12. An amount array summing to 1 modulo 2**256 therefore transferred a single token unit in while CreatePool credited the attacker's pools with the full element values, and because the pools' _FinishTime was already past, WithdrawToken immediately paid out the contract's entire balance of each token.

name: Curve CRV/ETH Vyper lock reentrancy
summary: Vyper 0.3.0 allocated the same named nonreentrant lock to different storage slots in different functions. The CRV/ETH pool's native-ETH callback therefore allowed cross-function reentrancy from remove_liquidity() into add_liquidity(), minting an invalid claim on pool reserves.

name: Equilibria transferable-share reward replay
summary: VaultEPendle updated reward debt only in deposit, withdraw and getReward, not on share transfers, and getReward(account) was public. The attacker deposited, moved the shares to fresh helper contracts and claimed for each, so every receiver was paid the full accumulated reward per share again, then pulled the shares back and repeated.

name: Balancer V2 composable stable pool rounding
summary: The Stable Pool exact-out path rounded the calculated input amount down instead of up. In low-liquidity, rate-scaled Composable Stable Pools, repeated crafted swaps amplified that error enough to manipulate the invariant, mint underpriced BPT, and extract reserves.

name: Sodium smart-account session-key validation bypass draining Lumi Finance users
summary: Sodium wallets validate an executeWithSodiumAuthSession userOp when the calldata session key equals the signature's self-declared ERC-1271 signer, deferring the real auth proof to execution. An attacker contract as signer passed validation, so wallets paid gas prefunds and approved attacker paymasters for tokens then pulled with transferFrom.

name: Beefy Moo CAKE CTK vault: StrategySyrup unsettled-reward share pricing
summary: StrategySyrup.balanceOf() omitted CAKE rewards pending in MasterChef, while deposit() claimed them; the vault priced new shares from the balance before calling deposit(). The attacker deposited 50,000 flash-borrowed CAKE at the stale share price, let the deposit and a harvest settle about 53,800 CAKE of prior depositors' rewards, and withdrew its pro-rata share.

name: Channels Finance cCLP_BTCB_BUSD donated-balance exchange-rate manipulation
summary: The cCLP_BTCB_BUSD market's permissionless gulp() books donated LP and accrueInterest() stakes idle LP, so donations move its exchange rate. The attacker donated LP and gulped to make cCLP positions liquidatable, seized and redeemed all but 2 wei of cCLP, then donated LP to revalue those 2 wei as collateral and borrowed the cash of seven Channels markets.

name: SAND Base OFT delegate-confused-deputy bridge drain
summary: OFTSand exposed an unrestricted approveAndCall callback whose first-argument check did not constrain the callback target, selector, or authority used by the callee. Calling the LayerZero Endpoint through OFTSand therefore made the Endpoint see the OFT itself as msg.sender and let an unprivileged caller replace the OFT's configuration delegate. This is an executed confused-deputy defect in the direct OFTSand runtime, not a compromised credential or an initially unsafe configured parameter.

name: VerusBridge supplemental-export parser divergence
summary: VerusProof did not reject a cross-chain-export output carrying the supplemental flag. A crafted output that Verus treated as inactive supplemental data was therefore parsed on Ethereum as an active export whose attacker-chosen transfer hash authorized unbacked ETH, tBTC, and USDC payouts.

name: SubQuery Settings missing setter authorization
summary: Settings.setContractAddress() and setBatchAddress() lacked owner checks, so five transactions installed attacker-controlled critical-role addresses and used the resulting StateChannel, staking, rewards, token, and booster authority to drain Treasury funds, pooled stake, deployment boosters, and 272 approved wallets.

name: Aztec Connect RollupProcessorV3 numRealTxs settlement gap
summary: RollupProcessorV3's decoder hashes whole inner-rollup chunks into the proof's public inputs, but processDepositsAndWithdrawals() settles only the first numRealTxs txs. The attacker put deposits after numRealTxs, so the rollup credited notes without debiting any pending L1 deposit, then withdrew them from pooled funds.

name: 1inch Fusion v1 Settlement calldata corruption (resolver drain)
summary: Settlement._settleOrder() used the attacker-supplied interactionLength in unchecked Yul pointer arithmetic. A wrapped length moved the appended suffix backward in memory, overwriting the authenticated resolver field, so the deprecated Fusion v1 contract called a third-party resolver and spent its standing token approvals.

name: Univ3CollateralToken
summary: Univ3CollateralToken stored deposited Uni V3 positions under the vault minter and balanceOf(vault) valued that minter-wide list. One position deposited for vault 40 therefore supplied borrowing power to every vault owned by the same minter.

name: RigoBlock Drago setMultipleAllowances missing owner check
summary: Drago v2 pools expose setMultipleAllowances(proxy, tokens, amounts) without the onlyOwner and whenApprovedProxy modifiers that guard setAllowance, so anyone can make a pool approve an arbitrary spender for its ERC-20 holdings. The attacker had the Pure Alpha Drago approve its contract for six tokens and then pulled and sold them; a second actor later used the same call on the byte-identical PayRue 1 Drago to take its aDAI.

name: LootBot xLoot staking redeem pays each duplicated NFT id in the input array
summary: LootBot Staking.redeem(uint256[] xloots) sums each listed xLoot NFT's unclaimed per-epoch ETH and only afterwards marks the ids redeemed, without rejecting repeated ids. The attacker passed one or a few owned ids hundreds of times per call; later it flash-borrowed ETH to open a new epoch and redeemed the duplicated ids again.

name: ERC20TokenBank
summary: ExchangeBetweenPools.doExchange(uint256) is permissionless: as a trusted issuer it pulls the USDC ERC20TokenBank's balance and swaps it through the Curve y pool with min_dy 0. The attacker skewed the pool, called doExchange so the bank's whole USDC balance bought almost no USDT, then unwound the skew and kept the difference.

name: Aztec 2.0 escape-hatch circuit data-root binding failure
summary: The escape-hatch circuit behind the verification key the Aztec 2.0 RollupProcessor's TurboVerifier used never forced the note-membership root to equal the public old data root L1 checks. The attacker proved ownership of notes in a fabricated tree while publishing the real root, and escapeHatch() paid the withdrawals from the pooled reserves.

name: INK Finance payroll plugin unprotected addSchedulePayee
summary: The INK Finance DAO payroll plugin's addSchedulePayee(scheduleId, payees) has no caller check. A throwaway contract added the attacker's precomputed CREATE2 address to payroll schedule 3 with a 165,162.83 USDT payout; the attacker then deployed that contract, topped the treasury up with a flash loan and called claimPayroll(3), draining the treasury.

name: ether.fi AtomicQueue unauthenticated solver
summary: AtomicQueue.solve takes the solver as an argument and pulls the want token from it with transferFrom, without requiring solver == msg.sender. The attacker queued a request offering a worthless token at a price equal to each victim's balance and solved it naming wallets with standing liquidETH or USDC allowances to the queue as solvers; copycats followed.

name: MEV bot 0x0ad8 unprotected arbitrary call
summary: The bot's public entry 0x090f88ca executed caller-supplied calldata with no access control. The attacker, then copycats, made it call transferFrom on tokens that the operator's wallets had approved to the bot, pulling their USDC, WETH, DAI and renBTC.

name: ZED RUN GaslessReservoirEnabler whitelisted-token module allowance drain
summary: GaslessReservoirEnabler.erc20WithTransfersAndExecute lets anyone run caller-chosen calldata against any whitelisted module, while users hold standing token allowances to the enabler. After the admin whitelisted the WETH token itself as a module, anyone could make the enabler call WETH.transferFrom(victim, attacker) and spend every approver's allowance.

name: Nimiq HTLC handler GSN execute verification bypass
summary: Nimiq's ERC20PermitHTLCHandler and ERC20MetaHTLCHandler are each their own OpenGSN forwarder, paymaster and recipient. Their forwarder execute() (onlyRelayHub) discards the signature, domain and type hash, skips checkOpen/checkRefund, and opens or closes an HTLC for request.from; signature, nonce and business checks live only in the handler's own preRelayedCall. RelayHub lets a staked relay name any paymaster, so a relay naming its own always-accept paymaster made the handlers pull a liquidity wallet's approved USDC, USDT0 and USDC.e into attacker-recipient HTLCs, and a later actor refunded other users' expired HTLCs to itself.

name: NFT Trader BatchSwap counterparty reentrancy
summary: BatchSwap.closeSwapIntent() re-reads the swap's counterparty from storage for each leg and has no guard against editCounterPart() during settlement. The attacker closed its own swap, re-entered from onERC721Received on the first leg, and repointed the counterparty at an address holding a WETH or NFT approval to BatchSwap, so the second leg pulled that asset to the attacker.

name: Compounder StrategyDAICurve permissionless deposit manipulation
summary: StrategyDAICurve let anyone call deposit(), which added its loose DAI to the thin Curve y pool as yDAI with zero minimum output, and valued its yyCRV through the same pool's spot quote. The attacker unbalanced the pool, cycled DAI through the cVault and the strategy, forced deposit() and reversed the Curve trades for profit.

name: OMNI404 transfer treats small amounts as ERC-721 ids and pays a full unit per Uniswap V3 exact-output swap
summary: O404.transfer(to, valueOrId) treats any value up to maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an ERC-721 id and, if the caller owns that id, moves a full 1e18 ERC-20 unit plus the NFT. A Uniswap V3 pool pays swap output with transfer(recipient, amountOut). The attacker flash-borrowed O404 from the O404/WETH pool and repaid it through id transfers, leaving the pool owning ids 1..21. It then swapped exact outputs of id-many wei, receiving 1e18 O404 per id for about 2 wei of WETH, and sold the O404 back for the pool's WETH, repeating across four transactions.

name: GMX v1 GLP reentrancy short-price manipulation
summary: GMX v1 PositionManager executed decrease orders with Vault leverage enabled while refunding ETH to the order account, so a contract account could re-enter and open Vault shorts outside the tracker update path, skewing the global short average. GlpManager priced GLP from that average, so GLP redeemed after the skew over-withdrew Vault reserves.

name: Limit Break Payment Processor V2 forwarded-calldata offset sender spoof
summary: Payment Processor copied a forwarded call's trade data from the caller-supplied ABI offset but sized it as if canonical, so through a permissionless trusted forwarder attacker bytes became the ERC-2771 sender. Attackers acted as any wallet that had approved it: accepting zero-price offers for victims' NFTs and making victims buy worthless listings with approved tokens.

name: DeFi Plaza single-sided removeLiquidity rounds reserve to zero
summary: DeFiPlaza.removeLiquidity pays X*(1-F) of one token with F=(1-R)^16 in truncating 0.64 fixed point and no bound on the burnt LP fraction R; above R≈0.94 F truncates to 0 and the whole reserve is paid. swap() then prices against a zero reserve, so a flash-loaned LP majority emptied all 16 reserves.

name: BvaultsStrategy convertDustToEarned unprotected swap
