summary: BvaultsStrategy.convertDustToEarned() is public and swaps the strategy's entire want-token balance to the earned token through PancakeSwap with a zero minimum output. The attacker flash-loaned to skew the BUSD→WBNB→ALPACA route, called the function so the strategy sold its BUSD into the skewed pools, and unwound the skew for the difference.

name: Huma credit approval bypass
summary: Huma v1 BaseCreditPool.refreshAccount is open to anyone and runs _updateDueInfo on a merely requested credit line; with no due date the fee manager reports one elapsed period, so the line becomes GoodStanding without evaluation-agent approval. The attacker requested oversized lines, refreshed them and drew down each pool's liquidity.

name: Planet Finance borrow discount treats freshly borrowed principal as accrued interest
summary: PlanetDiscountDelegate.changeUserBorrowDiscount treats the growth of a borrower's stored balance since the last snapshot as interest and subtracts a discount share of it from the recorded debt, while GToken.borrowFresh raises the principal without refreshing that snapshot. After staking GAMMA to reach a 5% discount tier and supplying USDT collateral, the attacker alternated gUSDT borrow() with the public updateUserDiscount(). The discount was applied to new principal 76 times, cutting its recorded debt by 10,183.70 USDT before it repaid and redeemed.

name: Idols NFT self-transfer reward double-credit
summary: IdolMain._beforeTokenTransfer settles stETH rewards twice for the same holder when the sender and the receiver are the same address. It first calls _claimEthRewards(_from), which pays balanceOf(_from) * (rewardPerGod - claimedSnapshots[_from]) and writes claimedSnapshots[_from] = rewardPerGod, and then, because the sender will hold one fewer token, executes delete claimedSnapshots[_from] whenever balanceOf(_from) == 1. It then evaluates the receiver branch, where balanceOf(_to) > 0 still holds, and calls _claimEthRewards(_to) against a snapshot that has just been zeroed, paying the whole cumulative rewardPerGod again. Calling safeTransferFrom(self, self, tokenId) in a loop therefore mints one full rewardPerGod payout per iteration while the token never leaves the caller. The onlyAllowedContracts(_to) guard, which relies on Address.isContract, does not stop it because the loop runs inside the exploit contract's constructor, when its code size is still zero.

name: DBXen burnBatch ERC-2771 sender split
summary: Called through its trusted ERC-2771 forwarder, DBXen.burnBatch credits burned batches to _msgSender() but burns XEN from msg.sender, so the burn callback updates the forwarder's lastActiveCycle, not the user's. The user's batches settle against cycle 0, and claimFees pays it accrued protocol fees. Attackers and copycats drained the deployments on seven chains.

name: Ambient WarmPath concentrated-position harvest on wrapped fee mileage
summary: CrocSwapDex's WarmPath harvest pays concentrated LPs liquidity x (feeMileage - oldMileage) but compares the uint64 range odometer non-circularly, although tick odometers rely on wrapping arithmetic. Attackers pushed price with swaps, minted a dust-sized narrow range at freshly initialized ticks, crossed a tick, and harvested huge rewards from pool reserves.

name: Ajna ERC20Pool liquidation accounting campaign
summary: Ajna ERC20 pools let one actor control a borrower and the bucket deposit its liquidation settles against. Attackers drew debt and kicked their own loan, then settled the auction through bucketTake, take and repayDebt so the pledged collateral came back while the drawn quote stayed with them, leaving the debt to other lenders.

name: iEarn yUSDT hard-coded iUSDC accounting mismatch
summary: iEarn yUSDT was deployed with its Fulcrum lender set to bZx iUSDC instead of iUSDT, and its pool value counts that iToken as USDT. The attacker emptied the vault, donated iUSDC so rebalance burned it into USDC the pool value ignores, leaving pool value near zero against live supply, then deposited a little USDT for vast yUSDT and swapped it out of Curve pools.

name: Cashverse staking distributor public depositBNB swaps with no minimum output
summary: An unverified staking reward distributor exposed depositBNB() without access control. Once any stake existed it swapped its entire BNB balance for ADAcash on PancakeSwap with amountOutMin 0. The attacker pumped ADAcash with flash-borrowed WBNB, called depositBNB() so the distributor bought at the inflated price, and sold its ADAcash back into the pair.

name: Royal1155LDA amount-blind batch bookkeeping inflating a royalties claim 100x
summary: Royal1155LDA._beforeTokenTransfer loops over the ERC-1155 ids array and never reads the parallel amounts array, so it credits the recipient's shadow per-tier balance _BALANCES_[tierId][to] with exactly one unit per array entry regardless of how many units the ERC-1155 transfer actually moves. Its sender-side branch is additionally skipped whenever _IS_OWNED_TOKENS_BACKFILL_COMPLETE_ is false and the sender's shadow balance has already reached zero, so the same id can be listed many times without reverting. A safeBatchTransferFrom listing LDA id 42<<128|424242 one hundred times with one hundred zero amounts therefore left tierBalanceOf(42, receiver) at 100 against a tier supply of 1, and Royalties, which pro-rates a tier's deposited USDC by tierBalanceOf, paid a claim 100 times the attacker's own 2638.089539 USDC royalty deposit and emptied the contract.

name: kTAF empty-market exchange-rate inflation and redeem rounding
summary: kTAF, a Compound V2 fork market, let a donation inflate the exchange rate of a near-empty market and truncated the shares burned by redeemUnderlying. The attacker emptied kTAF by liquidating its only, underwater supplier, then per helper minted, donated TAF to leave 3 wei backing 3,300 TAF, borrowed DAI and redeemed nearly all TAF, leaving bad debt.

name: StepHeroNFTs referral-claim reentrancy
summary: claimReferral(address) sent the caller's accrued BNB referral commission before reducing its recorded balance, so the attack contract's receive hook could reenter and claim the same self-referral commission repeatedly.

name: BankrollNetworkStack self-funded buyFor inflation
summary: buyFor() accepted the pool itself as the beneficiary. WBNB.transferFrom(pool, pool, amount) was balance-neutral, but purchaseTokens() still minted internal stake and allocated virtual fees. Repeating that self-funded buy inflated dividends owed to the attacker's real stake, which sell() and withdraw() paid from the pool's WBNB reserve.

name: Unidentified proxy 0x6f7a unauthorized balance routing
summary: Proxy selector 0xbfd479c4 processed arbitrary token amounts with no caller authorization or ownership check, letting anyone route the victim's live balances into a liquidity path.

name: MainPool public calcStepIncome()
summary: MainPool.calcStepIncome(id, amount, step) was callable by anyone with arbitrary arguments and credited the caller's withdrawable income directly, so the attacker joined the game and then wrote itself an income entry it withdrew as ETH.

name: Ribbon Gamma Oracle unrestricted setAssetPricer
summary: Ribbon's Gamma Oracle.setAssetPricer lacked an owner check, so anyone could install a pricer for an asset that had none. The attacker installed its own pricers for stETH, AAVE, LINK and PAXG, admitted products through the equally open Whitelist, minted oTokens on dust collateral, posted expiry prices inflated ~1e7-fold and redeemed against the MarginPool.

name: Dolomite legacy exchange submitRingsThroughDyDx approval drain
summary: The legacy Dolomite exchange's public submitRingsThroughDyDx decodes caller-supplied ring orders and, before any order is validated in settlement, pulls each signer's deposit through the TradeDelegate into dYdX accounts it operates as global operator. The attacker forged orders naming wallets with stale TradeDelegate approvals and withdrew their funds.

name: pNetwork Burner convertAndBurn slippage sandwich
summary: pNetwork's PNT fee Burner let anyone call convertAndBurn, which sold the contract's whole ETH, WBTC and USDT balances for PNT through Kyber with a minimum conversion rate of 1. The attacker flash-borrowed WETH, bought PNT on the Uniswap pair Kyber routed through, triggered the conversion at the inflated price and sold the PNT back.

name: HedgePay staking forceExit pays out the stake without clearing the staked balance
summary: The HedgePay HPAY staking proxy's implementation pays a staker's full balance on forceExit() but never reduces that balance or totalSupply, so the same stake can be paid out again by withdraw() or by repeated forceExit() calls, draining other stakers' HPAY.

name: Thetanuts zero-supply residual-asset share pricing
summary: deposit() used a one-to-one initialization rate whenever totalSupply was zero even though the vault retained WBTC, so the attacker minted all new shares with a two-satoshi seed and a 4.68 WBTC deposit, then redeemed those shares for the deposit plus the unowned residual balance.

name: Ocean BPool single-sided join-exit math drain
summary: Ocean BPool's joinswapExternAmountIn minted shares for a base-token-only deposit while SideStaking mirrored it with datatokens, and exitswapPoolAmountIn redeemed via calcSingleOutGivenPoolIn, so the same shares bought back more base token than the join paid. The attacker flash-swapped mOCEAN and cycled joins and exits over eight clones.

name: Unifi UP reward manager accepts a caller-supplied fake pool for LP reward eligibility and reward math
summary: The unverified Unifi UP reward manager 0x5d8aa155 treats any contract that calls mintUP(self) as a pool once its token0() returns WBNB, and claimUP(pool, a, b) sizes the payout from balanceOf and totalSupply read from that same address. The attacker's contract, whose runtime differs from every Unifi pool, minted UP with 0.001 flash-borrowed BNB, then claimed the manager's whole 0.559 UP reward reserve by reporting a huge LP balance. It redeemed the UP at the UPRedeemer for 5.86 BNB.

name: Futureswap exchange position asset wraparound
summary: The Futureswap exchange implementation's changePosition accounting wrapped a small negative asset balance into a huge positive one: helper accounts opened offsetting positions so one stored long read back as about 2^108 asset units, and a follow-up changePosition settled against that fabricated collateral and paid out the exchange's USDC.e and WETH.

name: SWAPP Staking unchecked cToken transferFrom deposit credit
summary: Staking.deposit ignores transferFrom's return value and credits the caller anyway; emergencyWithdraw pays that balance out for any non-stablecoin token. cUSDC returns false on a failed transferFrom, so the attacker 'deposited' the contract's whole cUSDC balance without owning any and emergency-withdrew the real cUSDC backing users' USDC.

name: Thetanuts legacy IndexVault zero-cost remint
summary: IndexVault.mint() computes each required component-vault transfer with truncating division and accepts zero amounts. After claiming flash-borrowed index shares cut totalSupply to three, the attacker made 37 sub-supply mints whose transfers all rounded to zero, reminted the shares to repay the loan, and kept the five component-vault balances.

name: Futureswap governance in-transaction snapshot flash-loan vote
summary: Futureswap governance snapshots FST in createProposal and weights votes by balanceOfAt at that snapshot in the same tx, so flash-swapped FST counted as votes. The attacker passed a proposal granting itself Registry wallet access and drained the Wallet; a second actor repeated it to seize the executor and drain Ethereum and Avalanche holdings.

name: DHC award contract repeatable claim
summary: The DHC award implementation (unverified) pays a claim (0x43609f36) from the proxy's pooled DHC without marking the award spent, and a dust re-participation (0xe3db9b54) makes the same award claimable again. The attacker funded awards once with flash-bought DHC, re-claimed them hundreds of times and sold the DHC.

name: Alkemi Earn self-liquidation collateral inflation
summary: AlkemiEarn.liquidateBorrow() let a borrower liquidate their own position with the borrowed asset also serving as the collateral asset, crediting more supply than the repayment consumed, so a flash-loaned supply/borrow/self-liquidate/withdraw sequence walked out with more ETH than was deposited.

name: VerifierExit exit-proof verification always returning true
summary: ZKSwap 1.0's VerifierExit implementation 0xd12f4d8329584f36aed67f807f42d9a02beb9534 accepts every exit proof: each verifyExitProof frame in the campaign - one in the anchor, fifteen in the later batch transaction 0x5488f6bb - returns true after exactly 1,496 gas and makes no elliptic-curve precompile call, so no pairing check is performed on the 708-byte proof argument. Once the rollup was in Exodus Mode the ZKSwap L1 contract 0x8eca806aecc86ce90da803b080ca4e3a9b8097ad therefore credited the attacker's forged exits against the frozen state root and released the bridge's balances on withdrawal. The invariant violated is that an exit may only be credited for a balance actually committed in the frozen rollup state.

name: DoinGud marketplace acceptOffer zero-amount replay
summary: The DoinGud marketplace facet's acceptOffer(offerer, tokenId, price, amount) pays the full offer price from the diamond's USDC escrow even with amount 0, transfers no NFT, keeps the offer and lets the offerer accept its own offer. The attacker funded a self-offer with flash-swapped USDC and accepted it twice, draining other users' escrow.

name: BonfireSwap router transfer() pulls BONFIRE from any approved holder
summary: BonfireSwap.transfer(to, amount, beneficiary, deadline) moved BONFIRE from the caller-chosen 'to' into the pair with transferFrom and then skimmed the pair's surplus to 'beneficiary', without checking that the caller was 'to'. The attacker named 65 holders with standing router approvals as 'to', took their balances and sold them for BNB.

name: Float Hypervisors mint and redeem shares at the pool's instantaneous tick
summary: Float Protocol's Visor-style Hypervisors on the FLOAT/WETH Uniswap V3 pool price deposits and holdings at the pool's current tick. Their only guard, the DepositProxy ratio check, compares against the same manipulable holdings. Swapping the pool, depositing through the DepositProxy, swapping back and withdrawing returns more than was deposited.

name: Truebit TRU bonding-curve purchase-price overflow
summary: The pre-0.8 Purchase implementation computed the TRU purchase price with unchecked arithmetic. Crafted buy amounts overflowed the price numerator so the ETH cost wrapped to near zero, letting the attacker mint vast TRU (Purchase holds TRU's minter role) and sell it back to the bonding curve, draining its ETH reserve in repeated buy-sell rounds.

name: Enjin CryptoItems ERC-1538 registry adapter initialize manager takeover
summary: Two Enjin ERC-1538 adapter registries route the adapter template's initialize(uint256) through their own fallback, so it runs in registry storage and writes the caller into the pending-manager slot. The attacker took both registries, routed adapter selectors to its own code, then pulled others' items through new adapters without approval and melted them for ENJ.

name: USM FUM defund split-invariance
summary: USM.defund() prices a FUM redemption off the mean of the current and post-redemption sell price and contracts adjShrinkFactor per call, so redeeming one position in 64 slices paid strictly more ETH than one call - a pure rounding/split-invariance flaw with identical oracle reads throughout the trace.

name: TimeBridge cross-contract signature-domain collision
summary: TimeToken.mint verified validator signatures over (sender, fromChainId, chainid, lockId, amount) without the contract address. The CGU bridge on BNB Chain signed the same message with the same validators, so the attacker replayed CGU unlock signatures on TimeToken to mint 519,000 unbacked TIME and sold it into the TIME/WBNB pair.

name: Lixir forged-permit vault drain
summary: Lixir vault tokens' permit accepted a signature as long as ecrecover returned any nonzero address, without matching it to the owner. The attacker reused one dummy signature to grant itself allowances over every holder's shares in six Lixir vaults and withdrew the underlying Uniswap V3 liquidity to itself.

name: Goose Finance StrategyGooseEgg prices deposits before folding harvested EGG into wantLockedTotal
summary: StrategyGooseEgg._deposit mints shares against wantLockedTotal before _farm() adds the strategy's whole idle EGG balance, including rewards harvested on earlier withdrawals. With flash-swapped EGG the attacker ran VaultChef deposit/withdraw rounds that captured the idle rewards and sold the surplus; 22 later transactions by others repeated it.

name: EtherFreakers capture pays out before settling the target, transfer hook re-dissipates stale energy
summary: EtherFreakers.attack() pays a captured target's energy to the defender before transferring the NFT; the transfer hook then recomputes the target's energy from its stale balance and dissipates 0.1% of it into the reward indexes, unbacked. Attackers looped flash-loan-charged captures between their own Freakers to inflate the index and discharged the excess.

name: Projekt Reward Vault unbacked purchase-delta allocations
summary: The reward vault's permissionless trackPurchase(buyer) treated a buyer's token-balance increase as purchase value and credited withdrawable ETH without authenticating ETH spent, a genuine purchase, or unique economic activity. Reversible balance movements could therefore create unbacked allocations that massWithdraw paid from the vault.

name: Amnext prize strategy draws winners from a blockhash seed known to the completer
summary: Amnext's PoolTogether V3 fork MultipleWinners lets anyone call completeAward(), whose seed comes from RNGBlockhash.randomNumber(), i.e. blockhash(block.number - 1), known before the caller's transaction runs. After depositing for a ticket share and starting the award, the attacker completed it in a block whose seed made every draw land on its contract, then withdrew the prize.

name: Goldfinch legacy Pool unauthenticated collectInterestRepayment
summary: The deprecated Goldfinch V1 Pool's collectInterestRepayment(from, amount) had no caller check: it pulls USDC from any address that approved the pool and adds it to the share price. The attacker flash-borrowed USDC, bought nearly all pool shares, pulled a stale approver's USDC in and withdrew the inflated shares; a copycat took the rest.

name: DxSale DxLockLPDep repeat-unlock drain
summary: DxLockLPDep.unlockToken() paid out a locker's full amount on every call and cleared its locked flag only once the unlock time had passed, never zeroing the amount. The attacker created small, unmatured locks of many PancakeSwap LP tokens and called unlockToken hundreds of times per lock, draining other users' locked LP.

name: Flamincome USDT Strategy donatable Convex NAV
summary: The USDT Strategy's balanceOfY(), which prices VaultYUSDT shares, adds Convex BaseRewardPool.balanceOf(Strategy) times the USDP/3CRV get_virtual_price() to its Aave USDT. Anyone can stakeFor the Strategy, and virtual price ignored USDP's depeg. The attacker deposited flash-loaned USDT, staked cheap USDP/3CRV LP for the Strategy to inflate NAV, and withdrew more USDT.

name: Lien BondMaker exception-count bond exchange mint
summary: BondMakerCollateralizedEth.exchangeEquivalentBonds checked only the total count of exception matches, so groups listing a bond twice let the attacker except every input bond and mint unbacked bonds. Lien's OTC exchanges priced these permissionlessly registered bonds from payoff metadata alone and paid for them from an LP's USDC allowance.

name: sMYX dividend token transfer creates unbacked profit-per-share while shrinking recorded supply
summary: The 2020 sMYX dividend token raised its profit-per-share on every transfer without any MYX inflow and, through a reversed subtraction, also shrank its recorded supply. The attacker bought a dominant sMYX position split over two contracts and alternated transfers with withdraw() calls, paying out other holders' MYX deposits as dividends.

name: Notional V1 Escrow uint128 truncation in free-collateral ETH conversion
summary: Notional V1 Escrow.convertBalancesToETH (ExchangeRate._convertToETH) casts abs(balance) to uint128 without a bound check, so a net currency balance of -2^128 converts to 0 ETH. Via public ERC1155Trade.safeTransferFrom fCash pair mints the attacker made one account owe exactly 2^128 DAI fCash while passing the free-collateral check, used the unbacked 2^128-1 receiver leg as collateral to mint matured DAI/USDC claims sized to the escrow balances, then settled and withdrew all DAI and USDC from the escrow.

name: GebProxyActions quitSystem callable directly for library-owned SAFEs
summary: GebProxyActions is a shared library meant to be DELEGATECALLed from each user's DSProxy. Its quitSystem(manager, safe, dst) has no authentication and forwards to GebSafeManager.quitSystem, which only checks that msg.sender owns the SAFE. SAFEs 3, 5, 8 and 18 were opened with the library itself as owner in October 2020. Calling quitSystem directly on the library therefore passed the ownership check. In the post-shutdown system the attacker processed each SAFE, moved its free ETH-A collateral into its own SAFE, and exited 5.94 ETH.

name: Balancer V1 BPool single-join rounding drain
summary: BPool single-asset join math (joinswapPoolAmountOut, also joinswapExternAmountIn) has no minimum-balance or rounding guard. After swaps compress one reserve to a few wei, each join rounds the required input down, minting BPT below cost; repeated joins followed by exits drained BPools, and copycats replayed it across the BFactory pools.

name: OMPxContract treasury-inventory mispricing
summary: getBuyBackPrice divides the contract's ETH reserve by token.totalSupply() even though the contract itself held ~79% of that supply as unsold inventory, so purchase() sold that inventory for a fraction of the reserve share it entitles the buyer to and buyBack() immediately redeemed it at the full per-supply price, letting a flash-loaned purchase/buyBack loop drain the reserve.

name: NovaBox uninitialised dividend checkpoints
summary: NovaBox adds new dual ETH/NOVA depositors to the dividend list without initialising their dividend checkpoints, and its extcodesize guard is bypassed from a constructor, so a fresh depositor could immediately withdraw and collect the whole stale historical ETH dividend.

name: UController.newOrganization adopts another organization's Reputation
summary: DAOstack's shared UController.newOrganization(avatar) was permissionless and adopted whatever Reputation the given avatar reported, making the caller a full-permission scheme. The attacker registered a fake avatar reporting Genesis Alpha's Reputation, minted a REP majority, voted itself in as a scheme on the real avatar, and had the UController send its ETH.

name: Laundromat free-deposit ring withdrawal
summary: Laundromat's deposit function did not enforce its configured payment, allowing the attacker to fill the remaining participant slots with chosen keys, satisfy the ring-signature withdrawal flow, and withdraw 1 ETH without depositing it.

name: OrderFactory permissionless createOrderForBuyer drains buyer escrow
summary: The unverified 2017 order factory's order-creation entry point (selector 0xbde886fc) checks only that the named buyer has an active request (getState(buyer) == 1). Any caller can create an order for any buyer with an attacker-chosen seller. The factory then moves the buyer's whole Account System ETH balance into a new order proxy and records the attacker as seller, and the proxy's seller-gated abort(address) sends that ETH wherever the caller says. From 2017 to 2018 only the platform operator EOA called this entry point. In September 2026 an attacker helper contract drained the platform's dormant buyer balances.
